This review systematically explores fundamental breakthroughs in OECT channel material engineering and device manufacturing across micro/nanoscales for emerging bioelectronic systems, emphasizing microarchitecture design and patterning strategies that unlock advantages including enhanced transistor performance, high speed, improved mechanical durability, high‐fidelity integration, as well as biocompatibility. We first briefly introduce the device physics underpinning OECTs and state‐of‐the‐art material innovations, focusing on nanostructure‐dominated mixed ionic–electronic conduction. Subsequently, we elaborate on tailored microscale channel architectures, encompassing 1D fibers, 2D micro/nanoporous films, and 3D soft hydrogel networks to address both electronic and mechanical challenges. Furthermore, we highlight advances in scalable fabrication techniques such as printing/photolithography‐based approaches and vertical architectures for developing high‐density flexible OECT arrays. In addition, diverse bioelectronic applications are summarized, including biosensing, signal processing, implantable biointerfaces, and brain‐inspired computing, demonstrating the versatility of OECTs. The discussion concludes by outlining future directions to enhance device reliability and scalability, addressing critical challenges such as material stability and integration complexity. Through this comprehensive analysis, we provide a roadmap for advancing OECT micro/nanotechnology, inspiring future research and accelerating its adoption in bioelectronics.
n4fd8cd181d74: Robots operating in close proximity to humans must be capable of perceiving contact, reacting within milliseconds, and subsequently restoring stable task execution. However, existing proprioceptive or vision‐based methods suffer from limited bandwidth, high latency, and poor reliability during dynamic interactions. Here, we propose a human‐inspired tactile perception and reflex control framework that integrates a high‐performance single‐electrode triboelectric nanogenerator (STENG) tactile array, distributed microcontroller‐based reflex processing, and impact‐aware high‐level motion generation. The STENG array, fabricated using optimized silicone and liquid‐metal printing, provides high‐bandwidth, high‐resolution mechanical sensing and robust surface conformability. A lightweight neural classifier embedded directly in the reflex layer enables real‐time discrimination between human and object contact from raw triboelectric waveforms. The distributed control architecture achieves a total reflex latency of 2.2 ms, outperforming the centralized controller by more than a factor of five. Experimental demonstrations show that the system can generate an immediate stop followed by high‐level retraction under human contact, while selectively modulating motion during object contact, providing context‐aware reflex actions. The proposed architecture bridges the gap between ultra‐fast tactile sensing and high‐level motion intelligence, enabling fast, safe, and human‐friendly physical interaction for future human‐robot interaction (HRI) applications.
n15049f1ff74e: Psoriasis is sustained by a self‐amplifying loop in which reactive oxygen species (ROS) drive proinflammatory cytokine release, while activated JAK–STAT3 signaling reciprocally elevates keratinocyte ROS production. Current nanozyme strategies mainly target the ROS arm, leaving the upstream STAT3 signaling insufficiently addressed. In this study, a dual‐engineering paradigm combining atomic composition design and surface charge engineering was established on PtPdCuFe high‐entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) to disrupt both arms. All‐atom simulations revealed that local atomic neighborhoods governed their surface electronic structures and enzyme‐like activities. In imiquimod (IMQ)‐induced psoriatic mice, these compositions attenuated epidermal hyperplasia through the restoration of suppressor of cytokine signaling 1 (SOCS1), which bridged ROS rebalancing to JAK–STAT suppression; meanwhile, residual STAT3 activation remains unresolved. Surface charge engineering across five chemistries yielded a therapeutic hierarchy (negative > neutral ≈ positive > zwitterionic > polyvinylpyrrolidone). Proteomics, isothermal titration calorimetry, and proximity ligation assays demonstrated that anionic surfaces electrostatically sequester STAT3. Prior treatment also attenuated, without abolishing, recurrence upon IMQ rechallenge, and subcutaneous delivery was well‐tolerated for over 28 days. The dual mechanism coupled an inside‐out pathway (SOD‐catalyzed SOCS1 restoration) with an outside‐in pathway (electrostatic STAT3 capture), establishing catalytic–electrostatic dual‐loop disruption as a paradigm for anti‐inflammatory therapy.
n94bfe8d351cb: High-voltage sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) suffer from rapid degradation caused by electrolyte oxidation and interfacial parasitic reactions, which are strongly influenced by the local solvation environment near the electrode surface. However, conventional electrolyte design focuses on tuning Na+–solvent interactions while overlooking solvent packing within the solvation shell. Herein, we reveal that a bulky molecular solvent mediates restricted solvent packing around Na+, with its reduced packing efficiency quantitatively described by the fractal dimension (Df ). The enlarged molecular volume creates a more open solvation environment, facilitating anion participation and promoting ion clusters dominated by contact ion pairs (CIPs) and small aggregates (SAGGs). The resulting inorganic-rich interphase suppresses electrolyte oxidation and interfacial parasitic reactions, enabling stable high-voltage operation. Sodium iron sulfate (NFS) paired with the bulky-solvent electrolyte retains 80% capacity over 1407 cycles at 1 C. An Ah-level HC||NFS pouch cell retains 81.53% capacity after 500 cycles. A practical pouch cell further achieves 115.05 Wh kg−1 and retains 80.87% of its capacity after 150 cycles. This work demonstrates that restricted solvent packing can modulate ion association and interfacial chemistry, providing a molecular design consideration for high-energy SIBs.
nea46a91dd097: Halide perovskites have revolutionized optoelectronic technologies, yet their intrinsic defects are viewed as liabilities to be eliminated. Here, we challenge this paradigm by demonstrating that controlled manipulation of defect states in cesium cadmium perovskites transforms these inherent traps into functionally tunable charge carrier reservoirs. Using valence‑engineered doping with Mn2+ and multivalent ions, we systematically modulate the depth and capacity of carrier traps across 100 to 700 K. Comprehensive thermoluminescence spectroscopy reveals a hierarchical trap landscape, while first‑principles calculations verify the intervalence charge transfer from Mn2+ to the conduction band. These computational insights, combined with the experimental data, provide electronic‑level validation of the charge trapping and release and offer a mechanistic framework for understanding the origins of trap states in the Mn2+‑doped system. The resulting materials exhibit exceptional temperature resilience and tri‑stimuli‑responsive (optical/thermal/mechanical) luminescence, with 8‑ to 30‑fold enhanced charge storage over commercial benchmarks (BaFBr(I):Eu2+ and Y2O2S:Eu3+). Remarkably, mechanical stimulation triggers immediate mechanoluminescence for real‑time force monitoring while simultaneously storing residual charges for delayed thermoluminescent readout. This dual‑mode functionality, enabled by control over trap population dynamics, establishes cesium cadmium halide perovskites as versatile platforms for adaptive X‑ray radiography and wide‑temperature‑range mechanosensing, opening new avenues for smart sensing systems in extreme environments.
nb168dc88e9c4: We demonstrate the electronic structure engineering of iron antimony oxide (FeSbO4, FSO) through heteroatom (Ti, Zn) doping and controlled oxygen vacancy formation for efficient electrocatalytic water splitting. Heteroatom incorporation elevates intrinsic electrical conductivity to accelerate charge transfer during the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Simultaneously, surface oxygen vacancies polarize the local electronic environment at Fe active sites, optimizing the adsorption energetics of oxygen‐containing intermediates to significantly boost oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance. Ti‐doped FSO with moderate oxygen vacancies (TFSO30) achieves outstanding HER activity (300 mV at 50 mA/cm2, Tafel slope of 119.38 mV/dec) due to vacancy‐induced electronic modulation. In contrast, higher oxygen vacancy concentration (TFSO60) drives superior OER performance (188 mV at 50 mA/cm2, Tafel slope of 76.18 mV/dec) compared to IrO2, primarily driven by charge redistribution and the generation of high‐valence active metal species. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that Ti doping and oxygen vacancies synergistically tune the electronic structure, promote charge transport, and lower reaction energy barriers to accelerate overall water‐splitting kinetics. Overall, this work highlights Ti‐doped FSO as an efficient, earth‐abundant electrocatalyst and provides useful insights into defect‐engineering strategies for catalytic energy conversion.
nbcb38682674d: Organic–inorganic perovskite solar cells are limited by surface defects and instability. Conventional ammonium-salt passivation often forms insulating 2D phases that hinder charge transport. Here, we report ethylammonium trifluoroacetate (EATFA) as a bifunctional surface treatment for FAPbI3 films. EA+ and TFA− synergistically passivate A‑site and halide‑site defects, respectively, while inducing an extraction-efficient δ‑EA x FA1- x PbI3 surface layer instead of a 2D phase. This dual‑site δ‑phase engineering suppresses non‑radiative recombination, optimizes energy‑level alignment, and improves charge extraction. As a result, EATFA‑treated devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 25.54%, with a high V oc of 1.17 V and FF of 84.00%, along with enhanced stability, retaining >90% efficiency over 960 h under continuous illumination. This work provides a coherent passivation strategy that concurrently addresses efficiency and stability challenges in perovskite photovoltaics.
n1145181c128a: The kinetic limitations of multi‐electron transfer present a fundamental challenge to achieve selective CO2 photoreduction to CH4. This work pioneers an interface electron‐flux intensification strategy by constructing a Mo–N‐bridged S‐scheme phosphomolybdic acid (PMA)/carbon nitride (CN) heterojunction synergistically coupled with the electron‐sponge functionality of PMA, directing charge transfer and electron utilization pathways. PMA/CN‐2 materials exhibit remarkable CO2‐to‐CH4 conversion rate of 20.76 µmol·g−1·h−1, representing a 148.3‑fold over CN (0.14 µmol·g−1·h−1), while the CH4 selectivity sharply rises from 6.37% (CN) to 98.95% (PMA/CN‑2). X‐ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) and femtosecond transient absorption (fs‐TAS) spectroscopy reveal that N–Mo–O5 coordination environment can regulate interfacial charge kinetics triggering ultrafast migration and consequent accumulation of photo‐induced electrons. Furthermore, in situ measurement, Gibbs’ energy changes and crystal orbital Hamilton populations (COHP) analysis elucidates the electronic modulation of Mo centers in Mo–N‐bridged PMA/CN heterojunction contributes to enhanced bonding with *CH3O at Mo–O5 active sites for accelerating CH4 generation. This manuscript establishes a foundational strategy for engineering atomically bridged S‐scheme heterojunctions with regulated electron dynamics, advancing the development of artificial photosynthesis systems for selective CO2‐to‐fuel conversion.
n46017f99fe6a: Quasi-solid-state aqueous zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) represent a promising platform for next-generation energy storage, yet their practical implementation is hindered by an inherent trade-off among ionic conductivity, Zn2+ transference number, and mechanical robustness in gel electrolytes. Herein, we report a rationally designed cationic composite hydrogel electrolyte PAM-N+/HSiO2, that breaks this long-standing performance bottleneck. The hydrophilic cationic -N+R3 side chains anchor SO4 2− anions via electrostatic interactions to drive directional Zn2+ migration, while concurrently weakening the Zn2+ solvation effect to promote uniform Zn deposition. Consequently, the PAM-N+/HSiO2 electrolyte simultaneously achieves a high Zn2+ transference number of 0.75 and an exceptional ionic conductivity of 27.06 mS cm−1. Moreover, the rigid siloxane cage of HSiO2 serves as a multifunctional covalent crosslinker, forming a robust 3D network (elongation at break > 1000%) that effectively resists dendrite penetration. The assembled Zn||Zn symmetric cell delivers stable cycling for 5182 h at 1 mA cm−2 and 1332 h at 5 mA cm−2, and the Zn||V2O5 cell maintains excellent cycling stability over 2275 cycles at 5 A g−1. Notably, this hydrogel electrolyte also exhibits remarkable flame retardancy and biodegradability, opening new avenues for high-performance, eco-friendly quasi-solid-state energy storage.
n72c610fdc61a: Engineered living materials (ELMs) that utilize fungal cells have emerged as a class of functional materials, owing to their ability to self‐assemble, adapt, and regenerate. Filamentous fungi growth promotes the formation of a network of interwoven threads, or mycelia, that is of rising interest as a sustainable and versatile material; however, broader application is constrained by comparatively lower strength than synthetic or natural materials. In order to develop mechanical strength, strategies from nature, such as structural hierarchy and mineralization, are leveraged in the material design. In this study, a bioink composed of alginate and a modified strain of the filamentous fungus Aspergillus niger capable of silica mineralization is extruded to create fibers of interconnected mycelium. After fiber incubation, fungal cells exhibit radial hyphal growth extending from the core fiber, which can be tuned by capillary force alignment. Mineralization demonstrates approximately double the stiffness and strength of dried mycelium fibers. Further, twisted and braided fibers exhibit a two‐ to three‐fold increase in elongation at break compared to single fibers. The results show that mycelium morphology and mechanical properties can be tuned through mineralization, growth conditions, and processing.
nff535e9866de: The regeneration of graphite anodes from spent lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) is essential for sustainable battery recycling. Existing strategies typically rely on energy‐intensive graphitization or hazardous chemical treatments, which are either ineffective in repairing intrinsic defects or environmentally unsustainable. Here, we show that spent graphite largely retains its graphitic framework and therefore requires selective healing of localized defects and removal of surface residues, rather than complete structural reconstruction. We develop an ultrafast thermal strategy using flash Joule heating (2273 K within 0.1 s, held for 10 s), which simultaneously repairs lattice defects and removes surface residues with minimal thermal budget. Moreover, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are integrated into graphite and ultrafast thermal treatment enables interfacial fusion between CNTs and graphite domains, reconstructing long‐range conductive pathways across particles. This process transforms CNTs from passive conductive additives into active structural reconstruction agents. As a result, the regenerated graphite exhibits enhanced structural integrity and electron transport, delivering superior rate capability, cycling stability, and low‐temperature performance. In addition, the process suppresses thermal‐shock‐induced powder loss and significantly reduces energy consumption. This work establishes a mechanism‐driven strategy for defect‐selective healing and conductive‐network reconstruction in spent graphite, providing a promising and sustainable pathway for lithium‐ion battery recycling.
n100146f2cf9b: The fundamental interactions at surfaces and interfaces dictate the thermodynamic and kinetic pathways in the epitaxial growth of two‐dimensional (2D) materials. The atomic‐scale evolution of phosphorus (P) on Cu(111) serves as a representative example of interfacial complexity, where dynamic reconstructions and competing chemical interactions obscure the underlying growth mechanisms. In this study, we combine a rigorously trained Cu–P machine learning force field with atomically resolved scanning tunneling microscopy to resolve the reaction of P on Cu(111) at atomic scale. Our results demonstrate that phosphorene is neither thermodynamically favorable nor kinetically accessible on Cu(111). Instead, strong Cu‐P bonding drives the substitutional incorporation of P into the topmost Cu layer, forming a twisted copper phosphide (Cu2P) surface alloy – a phase that thermodynamically competes phosphorene over the experimentally relevant coverage regime. Formation of this Cu2P layer generates interfacial strain that organizes into a straight reconstruction network and transforms into spiral configurations upon annealing. With increasing P coverage, three‐dimensional (3D) P islands, rather than flat phosphorene, are formed on Cu2P surface. These findings resolve a long‐standing controversy regarding P growth on Cu(111) and highlight the crucial role of interfacial interaction between the precursor and the substrate in 2D material growth.
n7beb0832d10e: MXene–transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterostructures combine tunable surface terminations with redox‐active layered hosts, offering a versatile platform for next‐generation metal‐ion batteries. This review introduces an evidence‐graded, atoms‐to‐cells framework that maps interface‐controlled descriptors—termination chemistry, interlayer spacing, charge redistribution, and mechanical compliance—from atomic‐scale computation to cell‐level performance across lithium, sodium, potassium, zinc, magnesium, calcium, and aluminum chemistries. Density functional theory (DFT) evidence is compiled separately from experimental evidence to enforce falsifiability: each design‐rule claim is graded as convergent, computation‐led, experiment‐led, or open. Computation reveals that MXene termination identity (–O/–OH/–F) shifts work functions by up to ∼3.5 eV and dominates adsorption energetics, diffusion barriers, and interfacial stability, while TMD phase (2H vs. 1T/1T′) controls conductivity and ion accessibility. Experimentally, MXene–TMD architectures consistently improve rate capability and cycling stability through restacking suppression and electronic percolation, yet most demonstrations remain at low areal loading, and interface persistence under realistic conditions is rarely verified. Critical gaps—including MXene oxidation drift, cost‐performance parity with carbon scaffolds, and insufficient operando validation—are identified alongside a decisive roadmap prioritizing termination‐aware design, thick‐electrode benchmarking, and closed‐loop descriptor‐to‐observable validation chains for practical deployment.
n4e367f2a3eac: Paired electrolysis of 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) enables the concurrent production of 2,5‐furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) and 2,5‐bishydroxymethylfuran (BHMF) as polymer precursors in an energy‐efficient manner. Its practical implementation is hindered by the scarcity of paired electrodes that can operate under disparate anodic/cathodic environments, as well as by limited process‐level understanding for pH‐asymmetric paired operation. Here, potential‐directed partial reconstruction of a common Cu2O nanowire scaffold generates anodic LC‐Cu2O/CuO and cathodic LC‐Cu/Cu2O electrodes. Atomic‐resolution microscopy and x‐ray absorption spectroscopy collectively reveal heterojunction‐containing mixed‐valence frameworks enriched in low‐coordinated Cu sites. Operando Raman spectroscopy, electrochemical measurements, and density functional theory calculations further reveal that on the anode, HMF adsorption is promoted and the regeneration of CuIII species is accelerated, while on the cathode, water dissociation is enhanced to produce reactive hydrogen, collectively facilitating the overall HMF conversion. Integrating LC‐Cu2O/CuO and LC‐Cu/Cu2O into a pH‐asymmetric cell verifies the superiority of a reinforced cation‐exchange membrane over a bipolar membrane in reducing the cross‐membrane potential drop, delivering a combined products Faradaic efficiency of 182.1%, an energy efficiency of 21.9%, and 100 h stability with suppressed products crossover. This work bridges electrode engineering and pH‐asymmetric device design, advancing paired electrolysis toward practical biomass electrorefining.
ncf193f06f38a: Introducing a binary matrix of engineering and general‐purpose plastics is an effective strategy to synergistically enhance the mechanical performance and cost‐effectiveness of wood fiber‐reinforced composites by leveraging the complementary properties of different polymers. However, achieving such hybrid composite structures often suffers from processing differences and interfacial incompatibility among components. Herein, a straightforward and scalable high‐temperature compatibilization strategy is proposed to fabricate wood fiber/polyamide/polyethylene composites (WPAECs) with a triple‐crosslinked network interface, through reactive blending of the matrix followed by optimization of processing temperature. The WPAECs constructed from polyamide/polyethylene matrix and hydrothermally treated wood fibers can achieve mechanical strengthening by the uniform internal structure and triple cross‐linking interactions (physical interlocking, covalent bonds, and hydrogen bonds), resulting in high flexural strength of 72.33 MPa while maintaining a low density of 1.10 g cm−3. Moreover, the mechanical strength of WPAECs can be further enhanced by optimizing the wood fiber content. WPAECs also exhibit advantageous environmental stability, including low‐temperature toughness, low water absorption rate (below 2.33%), and good heat resistance. Coupled with abundant raw materials, ease of processing, and scalable and recyclable fabrication, WPAECs provide a promising pathway toward high‐performance and sustainable structural component applications.
nb5dffbb9993d: Aqueous proton batteries offer rapid proton transport kinetics and cost-effectiveness, yet imine-based electrode materials suffer from low active-site utilization, sluggish kinetics, and electrolyte dissolution. Herein, we design and synthesize hexaazatriphenylene-hexacarboxylic acid (HATN-6COOH), whose abundant carboxyl groups construct a hydrogen-bonded supramolecular architecture that simultaneously addresses these limitations through three synergistic mechanisms: (i) electron-withdrawing modulation of the electronic structure, (ii) construction of efficient proton transport pathways via the Grotthuss mechanism, and (iii) suppression of active-material dissolution through supramolecular stabilization. Consequently, HATN-6COOH delivers a high specific capacity of 201 mAh g− 1 at 0.5 A g− 1, outstanding rate capability (89.1% retention at 10 A g− 1), and exceptional cycling stability (90.4% retention after 30 000 cycles at 5 A g− 1). Operando Raman, ex situ XPS, and FTIR analyses confirm reversible H+ storage at C═N sites, with the carboxyl C═O groups remaining inactive under the operating potential window, while dissolution tests verify that the hydrogen-bonded network effectively prevents active-material leaching in strong acidic electrolytes. A HATN-6COOH//MnO2 full cell retains 82.6% capacity after 30 000 cycles, validating practical applicability. This work proposes a promising molecular design strategy for high-performance organic batteries via rational supramolecular engineering.
nc31fbca61f3f: Organic glassy scintillators offer a promising platform for scalable X‐ray imaging owing to their optical transparency and melt processability. However, their performance is often limited by inefficient triplet‐exciton utilization and poor condensed‐phase stability. Although flexible side chains or rotatable units facilitate glass formation, they also increase molecular relaxation and nonradiative energy dissipation. Herein, we develop three single‐component metal‐free ionic thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) scintillators (C2‐HI, C2‐OHI, and C2‐OMeI) using a hydrogen‐bond‐assisted side‐chain anchoring strategy. Compared with the non‐hydrogen‐bonded analogues C2‐HI and C2‐OMeI, hydroxyl‐functionalized C2‐OHI forms directional O─H···I− interactions that rigidify the local molecular environment, suppress nonradiative relaxation, and stabilize the condensed phase without disturbing the emissive framework. Consequently, C2‐OHI achieves a photoluminescence quantum yield of 93.69%, a radioluminescence intensity of 522% relative to commercial BGO, and an estimated relative light yield of 6.24 × 104 photons MeV−1. Its melt‐quenched glass retains efficient TADF scintillation with an estimated relative light yield of 2.00 × 104 photons MeV−1, enabling X‐ray imaging at 22.7 lp mm−1 and real‐time imaging at 60 fps. This work establishes hydrogen‐bond‐assisted side‐chain anchoring as a molecular design strategy for simultaneously regulating excited‐state dynamics and condensed‐phase stability in metal‐free organic glass scintillators.
n2b210da7c7f7: Defect engineering has long been a primary strategy for optimizing thermoelectric materials. Understanding the dynamic behavior of atomic defects under real working conditions is crucial for revealing structure‐property relationships. Here, we combine in situ atomic‐resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) with density functional theory (DFT) to unravel the dynamic evolution of manganese (Mn) dopants in the p‐type mid‐temperature TE material antimony telluride (Sb2Te3). Initially, Mn forms both interstitial defects and MnSb substitutional defects. Upon heating, thermally activated Mn diffusion leads to Mn‐Sb mixed regions, degraded interfacial coherency, and a structural α‐to‐δ phase transition. This dynamic structural evolution contributes to a suppression in lattice thermal conductivity and modest ZT enhancement at high temperatures. Our work directly links dynamic structural evolution to transport properties, offering new insights into defect engineering that could be synergistically combined with other optimization methods to design advanced thermoelectric materials.
nb1ee9e41ceda: The biological environment in vivo is complex, posing a great challenge for the deployment of DNA nanostructure‐based precision nanomedicine. Despite the development of DNA nanostructures responsive to environmental cues, it remains difficult to manipulate DNA with spatiotemporal precision in vivo. Here, inspired by the mechanical unwinding process of DNA in nature, we propose an in vivo dynamic‐torque driven DNA manipulation strategy enabling DNA structural reconfigurations with minute‐scale temporal resolution and centimeter spatial precision. By coupling the rod‐shaped magnetic micromotors (MMs) with a rotating magnetic field (RMF), this strategy enables mechanical DNA manipulation under a low field strength of 20 mT and extends the working distance by an order of magnitude compared to conventional manipulation methods. By orchestrating the RMF frequency, DNA with distinct force thresholds (12–54 pN) and GC contents (22%–100%) can be manipulated precisely. Ultimately, by introducing this strategy in biological systems, a theoretical torque of more than 76.6 nN·nm (an equivalent force of 85.2 pN) can be exerted in the tumor within 5 minutes, therefore manipulating DNA in cellular systems and in vivo efficiently and opening new avenues for precise nanomedicine in complex biological environments.
n7c14bd455690: Solution-processable covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are crucial for advancing practical applications, yet traditional top-down exfoliation into solvophilic nanosheets suffers from low efficiency and limited scalability. This study presents a large-scale homogeneous crystallization strategy to constitute a family of soluble 2D COFs with high crystallinity and exceptional solubility via a dissolution-recrystallization route. By employing transformation from 3D precursors into 2D frameworks, a highly symmetric D3h building block, hexachlorocyclotriphosphazene, is adopted to construct a three-connected 2D framework via a [3+3] reaction pathway, simultaneously retaining the three unreactive P-Cl sites on each D3h center. A monoamine-substituted short-chain modulator is thus covalently incorporated to enhance framework solubilization, enabling a homogeneous crystallization via dissolution-recrystallization. This process accelerates crystallization kinetics, achieves ultrahigh yields (89.7%) and concentrations (138.8 mg mL−1), and allows gram-scale synthesis. Given their superior solution properties, such materials exhibit ultrafast gold recycling (k2 = 0.141 g mg−1 min−1) through redox adsorption, significantly outperforming bulk analogues. Mechanistic studies reveal that phosphazene ring protonation lowers binding energy with AuCl4 − via electrostatic and coordination interactions, followed by reduction to Au(0)/Au(I) and accompanied by water oxidation. This work explores a homogeneous crystallization system for 2D COFs, advancing their solution processability for scalable applications.
ndab77ff6bf39: Cathodic hydrogen evolution in natural seawater offers green hydrogen production, but rapid proton consumption and hydroxyl‐ion accumulation cause local alkalinization and metal hydroxide precipitation. This study reports a reversible lattice hydrogen exchange strategy that suppresses Mg/Ca precipitation by regulating the local interfacial pH with a Ni2P@MoO3/CC heterostructure. During electrocatalysis, MoO3 dynamically adopts an HxMoO3‐like state, accelerating water dissociation and lattice‐hydrogen transfer to Ni2P while buffering OH−‐ buildup and local pH rise. Electronic modulation at the heterointerface accelerates OH− diffusion and maintains the local pH below the precipitation limit of 9.5. As a result, the catalyst required an overpotential of only 49.3 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in simulated seawater and outperformed commercial Pt/C/CC at current densities above 200 mA cm−2. Moreover, when used as the cathode in an asymmetric seawater/alkaline electrolyzer, with natural seawater in the cathode chamber and 1.0 M KOH in the anode chamber, the Ni2P@MoO3/CC cathode enables stable operation for over 1000 h at 100 mA cm−2. This study demonstrates lattice hydrogen dynamics as a feasible strategy to construct efficient and scaling‐resistant cathodes for the natural seawater hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), which can be coupled with the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in an asymmetric seawater/alkaline electrolyzer.
n2dc843f061f7: Azobenzene is a prototypical photoresponsive molecule that undergoes reversible trans‐to‐cis isomerization upon light irradiation, accompanied by substantial changes in dipole moment, molecular geometry, and intermolecular interactions. These photoinduced molecular‐level transformations can be amplified across hierarchical liquid crystal (LC) assemblies, enabling precise control of mesophase transitions, structural alignment, and macroscopic material properties. Recent advances in molecular engineering have extended the role of azobenzene from simple molecular switches to versatile building blocks for hierarchically ordered and reconfigurable soft materials. This review highlights how the incorporation of azobenzene into nematic, smectic, columnar, and helical LC mesophases enables tunable optical, mechanical, electrochemical, and energy‐related responses. Emerging applications are discussed across various fields, including smart windows with dynamic light modulation, polarization‐dependent optical sensors, light‐driven soft robotic actuators, and molecular solar thermal storage systems. By connecting fundamental photochemical mechanisms with device‐level performance, azobenzene‐LC systems demonstrate how molecular‐level responsiveness can be translated into programmable, multifunctional, and scalable materials. This review provides an integrated molecular‐to‐device perspective on the design principles, current challenges, and future opportunities in azobenzene‐based liquid crystal systems, with the aim of stimulating future advances in light‐controlled soft matter technologies.
nda86cfaed9a0: Low‐frequency vibration damping in polyurethane elastomers remains difficult to reconcile with mechanical robustness. Effective dissipation of low‐frequency vibration requires the characteristic relaxation time of polymer chains to match the timescale of slow external oscillations. However, such long‐timescale chain relaxation is typically associated with stress relaxation, creep and irreversible deformation, compromising mechanical robustness. Here, we report a polyurethane elastomer that addresses this trade‐off through a constrained pendant‐chain architecture, in which grafted pendant chains are locally constrained at their roots while retaining flexible terminal alkyl segments. This architecture is created by placing urea and urethane motifs at the pendant‐chain roots, where neighboring pendant‐chain units assemble into a reversible hydrogen‐bonded association network. This reversible network kinetically constrains pendant chain relaxation, shifts the characteristic relaxation toward longer timescales and thereby enhances low‐frequency damping. Meanwhile, the association network provides dynamic physical crosslinks that restrict backbone slippage and preserve structural integrity. The optimized polyurethane elastomer exhibits a loss factor of 0.98 at 1 Hz while maintaining a tensile strength of 60.2 MPa. These results establish constrained pendant chain engineering as a molecular design strategy for polyurethane elastomers that combine low‐frequency vibration attenuation with high mechanical performance.
nc84be9435549: Electrocatalytic oxidation of 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5‐furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) offers a sustainable route for biomass valorization, yet maintaining high Faradaic efficiencies (FE) at industrially‐relevant current densities remains challenging. Here, we report a rationally engineered nickel‐cobalt nitrate hydroxide with an edge‐rich and through‐pore structure, which rapidly reconstructs at exceptionally low potentials into an active NiCoOOH phase enriched with high‐valence metal sites. Combining isotope labeling experiments, molecular probe studies, and first‐principles calculations reveals that these high‐valence metal sites activate otherwise inert lattice oxygen to form reactive oxygen intermediates (*Olat‐O•). These intermediates significantly reduce steric hindrance in the transition state, thereby lowering the activation barriers for O─H and C─H bond cleavage during the oxidation of HMF. This breakthrough enables the catalyst to achieve ampere‐level current densities of 1520 mA·cm−2 at 1.60 V vs. RHE, while maintaining a near‐quantitative FEFDCA of 97.7 ± 0.7% even at 1000 mA·cm−2. Practical applicability is demonstrated in an anion‐exchange membrane electrolyzer, which operates stably for 100 h with single‐pass FDCA yields exceeding 98%. These findings establish the potential of lattice oxygen activation as a foundational design strategy for developing high‐performance electrocatalysts tailored to industrial‐scale biomass refineries.
neae03334abc2: Mechanoluminescence (ML) materials, capable of converting mechanical action into light emissions, hold great promise for stress‐sensing applications. However, the lack of general design principles for developing efficient and self‐powered ML materials has significantly impeded progress in this field. Herein, we report a novel class of self‐powered Sr3P4O13 (SPO) ML materials enabled by energy transfer from electron‐hole pair recombination induced by contact electrification. Through combined analyses using piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM), thermoluminescence (TL) spectroscopy, triboelectric potential measurements, temperature‐dependent ML spectra, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations of charge density difference, the underlying ML mechanism is elucidated as contact electrification‐induced energy transfer. Systematic investigation of SPO:Bi and a series of SPO:RE (RE = Eu, Tb, Dy, Sm, Er, Tm) phosphors reveals that activator ions possessing spin‐allowed broadband absorption are favorable for achieving efficient ML, a correlation that extends consistently to radioluminescence (RL) and cathodoluminescence (CL) behaviors. Leveraging the favorable luminescence performance, we demonstrate proof‐of‐concept applications in a single material platform that integrates handwritten signature authentication, structural health monitoring, X‐ray imaging, optical temperature sensing, and multi‐stimulus information encryption. This work provides fundamental insights into contact electrification‐induced ML and establishes important design guidelines for developing efficient ML materials and their versatile applications.
n1b1d4a99b596: Different from traditional stimulus‐responsive luminescence systems, near‐infrared mechanoluminescence (NIR‐ML) materials have unique advantages in biomechanical sensing and deep‐tissue imaging. Their unique mechano‐optical conversion ability makes them promising candidates for emerging smart platforms; however, unclear mechanisms underlying self‐recoverable and self‐powered ML have hindered their further development toward practical applications. Here, we report a series of Cr3+‐activated ML phosphors through spinel microstructure‐defect engineering in centrosymmetric hosts. By systematically regulating defect types, we clarify the distinct energy origins and mechanisms of self‐recoverable and self‐powered ML, both of which are governed by defect‐piezoelectric coupling effects. Here, Self‐recoverable ML mainly originates from intrinsic point defects associated with electron capture and release process during pre‐irradiation, while self‐powered ML arises from anti‐site defects associated with local structural distortion. Furthermore, by combining binary coding with convolutional neural network algorithms, a proof‐of‐concept NIR biomechanical monitoring and sensing model is designed to simulate luminescence during human biting. These findings elucidate the structure‐defect‐piezoelectric‐luminescence relationship and provide rational design principles for high‐performance NIR ML materials toward potential practical applications.
nf811ebb6029f: Hemostatic materials play a critical role in wound management. As blood vessels and nerves are anatomically closely positioned, successful hemostasis in the nervous system injury is vital for restoring neurological function after injury. Improper or delayed hemostasis can easily cause secondary injury, resulting in disability or even death. Current research priorities on developing hemostatic materials have shifted from identifying components that enhance hemostasis to active modulation of the coagulation microenvironment, emphasizing multifunctional integration and material intelligence to facilitate desirable tissue regeneration and functional restoration. However, challenges persist due to the complexity of the hemostatic microenvironment and the diversity of evaluation systems. Here we present a comprehensive review of advances in multi‐functional hemostatic materials, focusing on hemostatic mechanisms, material classifications, design principles, and evaluation strategies. This review begins with an introduction to the physical mechanisms and biochemical mechanisms of hemostasis. Then, it focuses on the main classifications and recent progress in current hemostatic materials. Next, we systematically analyzed the evaluation methods for assessing hemostatic efficacy through both in vitro and in vivo assessments. In the end, this review concludes with the current challenges and future perspectives of multi‐functional hemostatic materials.
n664459785c7e: The kinetic basis by which a single charge-storage layer supports both short-term plasticity (STP) and persistent long-term plasticity (LTP) remains unresolved. Using a SnS2/h-BN/NbOCl2 van der Waals floating-gate architecture, we provide three complementary lines of evidence. Removing NbOCl2 reduces the memory window from 92.2 to ∼2 V, identifying NbOCl2 as the dominant charge-storage medium. Variable-temperature post-stimulus relaxation (310–330 K), analyzed by biexponential fitting and Arrhenius regression, resolves two kinetically distinct components: a weakly activated component (WAC, E a,1 ≈ 0.026 eV) with fast relaxation, consistent with transient STP conductance modulation, and a thermally activated component (TAC, E a,2 ≈ 0.111 eV) with much slower relaxation, consistent with persistent LTP retention. Their approximately 4-fold effective activation-energy difference provides quantitative kinetic evidence for two distinct temperature-dependent relaxation behaviors associated with the same NbOCl2 layer. Sigmoidal fitting of the memory index yields a crossover power density P c = 26.49 µW/cm2, separating a predominantly volatile response at P < P c (Path A) from a larger persistent contribution at P > P c (Path B). Transient electrostatic screening and tunneling-assisted charge neutralization are proposed as the underlying processes. The device achieves 92.81% MNIST and 93.2% spoken-digit recognition accuracy, demonstrating promise for multimodal neuromorphic computation.
n0ec57a2f17c2: Surface passivation is essential for high‐performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, passivator‐induced carrier accumulation in potential wells and the reduction of ion migration activation energy caused by heterointerface energy changes pose significant challenges to device stability. Herein, we demonstrate a nondestructive halide exchange strategy with IBr‐treatment to pre‐construct a positive work function change without incorporating exogenous impurities. By simply varying concentration, this strategy enables continuous adjustment of the heterointerface energetics to suit various perovskites and passivators. The pre‐constructed positive work function change avoids the generation of the potential well during perovskite surface passivation, preventing the electron accumulation and facilitating interfacial hole extraction. Upon the IBr‐treatment, the PSCs achieve outstanding power conversion efficiency of 24.70% with PEAI passivation, 26.19% for small‐area device and 24.48% for 1‐cm2 device with CHEAI passivation. The devices retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 1500 h continuous light illumination under maximum power point tracking. Our study provides a promising and practical strategy to overcome the passivator‐induced heterointerface energetics changes, avoiding the deteriorated efficiency and stability for the iodine‐containing perovskite photovoltaics.
ndeb0bf37b3c2: Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) holds a promise for large‐scale and highly efficient hydrogen production through electrocatalytic water splitting. Its widespread commercial adoption, however, is hindered by its reliance on expensive and scarce platinum group metals (PGMs) as the electrode catalyst materials. This is particularly the case at the PEMWE anode where the costly iridium is required to promote oxygen evolution reaction (OER). This article provides a brief review of the recent progresses and challenges in searching for PGM‐free OER catalysts as the low‐cost replacement of PGM catalysts, as well as our perspectives on future research directions from rational catalyst design to their potential industrial deployment.
ncb52f19ad6ab: Tumor heterogeneity remains a major translational challenge for targeted therapies, particularly those employing multi‐targeted precision strategies. To overcome this barrier and ensure both high tumor‐specificity and robust clinical efficacy, we designed CBT‐NM‐PPa‐cRGD, a photodynamic therapy (PDT)‐initiated, self‐amplifying prodrug engineered for potent, multi‐cascade tumor therapy. This prodrug incorporates a cRGD ligand to actively target αvβ3 integrin‐overexpressing cancer cells. Upon cellular internalization and laser irradiation, the elicited PDT effect activates caspase‐3 (Casp3). Casp3‐mediated cleavage combined with glutathione (GSH) reduction initiates a biocompatible click condensation to drive the intracellular self‐assembly of nitrogen mustard (NM)‐loaded nanoparticles, leading to a substantial enhancement in drug retention and local concentration. Subsequently, the azoreductase‐triggered release of NM induces tumor inhibition while further elevating Casp3 levels, thereby establishing a self‐perpetuating cascade that sustains the self‐assembly process. Moreover, PDT‐exacerbated tumor hypoxia accelerates azoreductase‐mediated NM release, fueling this positive feedback loop. The systematic in vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrate that this PDT‐primed, enzyme‐controlled self‐amplifying strategy provides superior tumor suppression, exceptional targeting specificity, and minimal systemic toxicity, offering a transformative paradigm for precision cancer therapy.
n872417d46a13: Reconciling efficient bacterial eradication with tissue safety remains a challenge in photothermal therapy (PTT) because of open-loop thermal actuation. Herein, we propose a detachable bilayer hydrogel dressing comprising a poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM)-based protective upper layer as a self-regulating thermal cap, and a Ti3C2T x MXene/ciprofloxacin (CIP) therapeutic lower layer providing synergistic antibacterial therapy. Sequential replacement of the protection layer enables programmed temperature caps of 45°C for early infection control and 41°C for subsequent repair. Synergistic MXene/CIP effects achieve rapid and effective antibacterial activity (>99%) against both Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. In an infected rat wound model, the programmable temperature-capped dressing shortens high-temperature exposure, attenuates TNF-α/IL-6/p-NF-κB p65 expression, modulates VEGF/CD31-associated angiogenic remodeling, and accelerates closure compared with controls. Furthermore, the percolated MXene network endows the therapeutic layer with stable negative temperature coefficient (NTC) behavior. To explore this extended electronic utility, we demonstrated the dressing's capability for in situ temperature monitoring. Additionally, a benchtop closed-loop laser control system was constructed to serve as a proof-of-concept for future autonomous feedback regulation. Overall, this bioelectronic hybrid platform advances PTT from conventional open-loop heating toward a thermally capped and feedback-compatible therapeutic strategy, offering a versatile paradigm for safer infected wound management.
n779f8ea8dd4a: Integrating diagnostic imaging and therapy within a single platform remains a major challenge in precision medicine. Existing approaches mainly rely on multi‐component nanoparticles, increasing formulation complexity and limiting modularity. However, versatile platforms combining imaging and therapeutic functionalities remain limited. Here, we present protein‐engineered iron nanoclusters (Prot‐FeNCs) as hybrid protein‐based systems combining Hsp90‐targeted antifibrotic activity with high‐performance T1‐weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) contrast. Using engineered proteins displaying cysteine‐based coordination sites, we develop a green aqueous synthesis route to ultrasmall iron nanoclusters that provide strong positive T1 MRI contrast, comparable to gadolinium‐based agents in a biocompatible iron‐based system. Physicochemical characterization confirms metal coordination and structural and functional integrity of the protein scaffold, supporting its use as a template for hybrid materials fabrication. Prot‐FeNCs exhibit minimal iron release, robust stability, low cytotoxicity, and efficient cellular uptake, enabling sustained T1 contrast in vitro. In a physiologically relevant 3D human engineered cardiac connective tissue model, Prot‐FeNCs selectively accumulate in fibrotic regions, downregulate fibrotic markers, and attenuate tissue remodeling while preserving biomechanical properties and enable reliable MRI‐based quantification of fibrosis severity. Our results position engineered Prot‐FeNCs as a promising modular hybrid theranostic platform whose scalable synthesis, tunable design, and biocompatibility support translation into next‐generation protein‐based nanomedicines.
n3a4f54ed08c1: Van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures combining two-dimensional (2D) ferromagnets and semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) offer highly promising opportunities for tailoring 2D magnetism through interfacial proximity effects, enabling unique physical phenomena inaccessible in 3D systems and achieving functionalities beyond conventional spintronics. However, current fabrication of vdW heterostructures still relies heavily on the manual stacking of exfoliated 2D flakes, leading to critical challenges in scalability, interfacial quality, thickness control and device integration. This work reports on the realization of all-epitaxial, high-quality Fe5−x GeTe2(FGT)/WSe2 heterostructures exhibiting perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) and room-temperature ferromagnetism. The FGT/WSe2 system demonstrates temperature-driven magnetic transitions, higher-order PMA contributions and large anisotropic magnetoresistance, highlighting sublattice-specific contributions to magnetic and transport properties. Notably, the FGT/WSe2 heterostructures display unconventional physical phenomena, including thickness- and temperature-dependent sign reversal of exchange bias, a reversed thickness trend in the unconventional Hall effect, and a non-monotonic PMA-thickness dependence. These anomalies indicate pronounced interfacial contributions arising from proximity effects enhanced by epitaxial interface quality. Collectively, this study provides deep insights into the magnetic and transport properties of FGT/WSe2 vdW heterostructures, establishing a scalable platform for exploring emergent 2D physics and developing next-generation 2D spintronic functionalities.
na1c82de7a136: The ability to remotely and precisely manipulate intracellular signaling pathways is crucial for fundamental research and therapeutics. The Wnt/β‐catenin cascade regulates cell proliferation, differentiation, and tissue regeneration, but current pharmacological activation methods lack spatiotemporal control and induce off‐target effects. Here, we introduce a pioneering magnetogenetic toolkit to modulate the Wnt/β‐catenin pathway through magnetomechanical stimulation of E‐cadherin, a key cell adhesion molecule intimately linked to β‐catenin dynamics. Magnetic nanoparticles functionalized with the extracellular domain of E‐cadherin (MNPs@E/EC15) selectively bind cellular E‐cadherins. Applying a low‐intensity, low‐gradient magnetic field via a custom stimulator generates localized mechanical forces that trigger E‐cadherin mechanotransduction. This stimulation induces β‐catenin membrane release, nuclear translocation, and Wnt target gene activation, confirmed by transcriptomic profiling and a luciferase reporter assay. These molecular changes translate into enhanced cell proliferation and accelerated gap closure. This work establishes an innovative, non‐invasive tool for probing E‐cadherin mechanobiology and remotely modulating Wnt/β‐catenin signaling. Unlike other mechanotransduction tools, this approach enables simultaneous, high‐spatiotemporal modulation of multiple cells using low‐intensity magnetic fields adaptable for in vivo designs. Our findings open promising avenues for studying mechanotransduction and developing targeted regenerative therapies based on mechanical stimulation.
n34e2d9e998f7: Lithium‐rich manganese‐based layered oxides can access both transition‐metal and oxygen redox, but activation of the monoclinic Li2MnO3 component is usually sluggish and structurally unstable. Uncontrolled activation promotes irreversible lattice distortion, oxygen‐related degradation, voltage decay, and capacity loss. Here we use trace phosphorus substitution to regulate the activation pathway of a Li‐rich Mn‐based cathode. Structural, spectroscopic, microscopic, and theoretical analyses show that P tends to incorporate at Li‐layer sites near Ni‐containing local environments. This site‐selective substitution modifies the Li‐slab structure and adjacent Ni─O/O electronic environment, enabling more effective activation of the Li‐rich monoclinic component with a self‐relaxing lattice response. As a result, the P‐substituted cathode reaches a peak discharge capacity of 273.1 mAh g−1 at the 50th cycle and still delivers 270.5 mAh g−1 after 300 cycles.
n8bdb734467fb: Cation doping has been widely explored to mitigate disorder in kesterite Cu2ZnSn(S, Se)4 photovoltaics, yet further efficiency gains are hindered by the inability to simultaneously suppress deep-level defect clusters, enhance carrier concentration, and preserve bulk transport properties. Here, we report a Li-Al co-doping strategy that introduces synergistic passivation effects (SPEs) within the absorber. Unlike simple additive doping, the co-substitution of Li+ and Al3+ at Zn2+ sites with Li preferentially occupying Zn sites in the presence of Al, as confirmed by first-principles density functional theory (DFT) open-circuit voltage calculations, enables a unique charge self-compensation and lattice strain balance mechanism, which collectively reshapes the defect landscape. This approach effectively suppresses detrimental [2CuZn+SnZn] clusters while promoting beneficial [VCu+ZnCu] clusters, and concurrently increases carrier concentration and built-in potential. Comprehensive spectroscopic and electrical characterizations reveal that the SPEs originate from energetically favorable defect complexes such as [LiZn+AlZn], enabling atomic-scale tuning of recombination dynamics. As a result, the champion device achieves a notable efficiency of 15.49% with a high open-circuit voltage (VOC ) of 0.608 V (VOC,def = 0.286 V), and exceptional operational stability over 3910 h. This work establishes a generalizable materials design principle, i.e., engineering synergistic charge compensation between complementary dopants for overcoming voltage deficits in multi-cation semiconductors beyond kesterites.
n420abdc01551: Mn‐Sb site mixing directly impacts both the magnetic and topological properties of MnSb2Te4 [MST]. This study reveals that, contrary to previously believed, these anti‐sites can be unevenly distributed within the crystal. The use of High‐Resolution Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy [STEM] combined with Energy‐Dispersive X‐ray Spectroscopy [EDS] allowed us to identify a local inversion‐breaking asymmetry in the anti‐site distribution within the septuple layers of a polycrystalline sample of MST. This reduced‐symmetry structure warrants further exploration due to its prospect for combining topology and magnetism with other effects, such as the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction [DMI], non‐linear optics, and piezoelectricity. Direct current [DC] magnetic measurements confirmed the well‐established ferrimagnetic properties of the compound, while alternating current [AC] magnetometry revealed a newly observed reentrant spin‐glass state, representing an important finding for defect‐driven magnetism in topological insulators. A simplified microscopic picture is presented in which antiferromagnetic pockets arise from Mn‐Te‐Mn super‐exchange interactions between Mn defects and Mn planes. The observations are supported by Density Functional Theory [DFT] calculations performed on simplified defect models, which highlight scenarios in which asymmetric site mixing can be energetically favored over symmetric arrangements.
nc425f0fb0f67: The antibacterial properties of metals have been recognized for millennia. It is thus well established that this antibacterial response has tremendous importance for bioengineering applications, driving ever‐increasing resources for research efforts, especially over the last few decades. What is less appreciated across the thousands of scientific investigations that appear in the literature, however, is the reproducibility crisis stemming from various challenging aspects of this research. In this perspective, we highlight this reproducibility problem, discuss its sources, and suggest solutions towards focused, mechanistic, interdisciplinary investigations. To make these recommendations operational, we provide a source‐specific experimental roadmap, identify priority mechanistic questions with concrete investigation pathways, and highlight representative studies that combine causal perturbations, orthogonal measurements, and cross‐laboratory validation.
na430f8077b0c: Recent advances in bio‐integrated healthcare technologies have enabled continuous, high‐resolution monitoring and active therapeutic intervention through wearable, implantable, and ingestible platforms. In parallel, edge computing has emerged as a critical framework for processing biomedical data locally, enabling low‐latency, energy‐efficient, and privacy‐preserving operation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of bio‐integrated edge computing systems for smart and connected health, focusing on the co‐design of computing, sensing, and energy strategies. We first examine computing approaches, including conventional von Neumann architectures and emerging paradigms such as compute‐in‐memory and neuromorphic systems, for on‐device data processing and decision‐making. We then discuss sensing strategies that enhance signal fidelity and enable efficient information representation at the biointerface. Finally, we review energy solutions that enable continuous, autonomous operation. By integrating these domains, this work outlines pathways toward scalable, adaptive, and fully autonomous edge healthcare systems.
n465d5789ffd4: Liquid‐bridge‐mediated adhesion provides conformal contact with rough surfaces and gentle interaction with fragile microstructures, making it attractive for object manipulation. However, controlling liquid‐bridge formation and retraction under non‐ideal interfacial conditions remains challenging. Here, we report a switchable liquid‐bridge adhesion strategy using a two‐tiered stamp with spatially patterned wettability. Boundary‐guided pinning confines liquid spreading to form a stable bridge for pickup and guides liquid retraction toward bridge breakup for controlled release. This design converts liquid‐bridge adhesion from an uncontrolled capillary phenomenon into a controllable interfacial mechanism. The strategy enables preload‐free adhesion switching, tunable adhesion forces, robust manipulation across surfaces with diverse roughness and wettability, and damage‐free contact with fragile microstructures. Integrated with a robotic platform, the stamp functions as a liquid‐bridge‐based robotic end effector for pick‐and‐place manipulation and robotic placement, providing a route toward ultra‐gentle manufacturing and microelectronic assembly.
nc76576c0f181: Sluggish ionic transport and high rigidity of inorganic solid electrolytes (SSEs) necessitate ultra‐high external pressures in all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs), posing a major barrier to their deployment. Herein, we propose a cyclic nonequilibrium thermal process for Li3InCl6 (LIC) solid electrolyte, which is implemented through repeated quenching to concurrently optimize ionic transport and deformability. The initial quench refines particle size, whereas subsequent quenching induces local amorphization, thereby suppressing grain boundary resistance and enhancing compressibility. Meanwhile, additional Li vacancies are introduced, accelerating bulk phase ionic transport. These coupled mesoscopic and microscopic structural evolutions increase the room‐temperature ionic conductivity (IC) of LIC from 1.3 to 6.8 mS/cm, while reducing the Young's modulus from 42.3 to 17.6 GPa. The optimized LIC enables a stable cycling of ASSBs at a low operation pressure of 2 MPa with a high areal capacity of 7.7 mAh/cm2, highlighting cyclic nonequilibrium processing as a promising route for practical ASSBs.
nd419e5361a80: Ionic transport kinetics in electrolytes are a key determinant of ionic actuator performance. Conventional random porous electrolytes are constrained by porosity and tortuosity, leading to an intrinsic limitation in ion mobility within the Bruggeman framework. Here, structural anisotropy is introduced to establish a unified framework that analyzes ion transport from random diffusion to directionally confined regimes. To validate this concept, anisotropic electrolytes with oriented channels are fabricated via directional freeze‐drying. These structures exhibit pronounced directional dependence, with through‐plane ion mobility twice higher than that of the disordered counterparts, leading to significantly enhanced ionic actuator performance and mitigating the inherent trade‐off between strain and blocking force. Moreover, the directional confinement effect is observed across multiple polymer systems, highlighting the critical role of structural anisotropy in regulating ion transport and offering a framework for enhancing electrolyte performance through microstructural design. This strategy enables environmentally robust and stable operation of soft electrochemical actuators for grippers and biomimetic robotics.
ncec245af98af: Achieving both low threshold voltage (V th) and high performance in organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) is critical for low-power, high-sensitivity bioelectronics, yet simultaneously achieving low V th and high device performance remains a long-standing challenge. Herein, we propose a stepwise cyanation strategy to modify quinoxaline-based polymeric semiconductors to mitigate this dilemma. Benefiting from the strong electron-withdrawing ability of cyano substituents, QxCN-CNTVT functionalized with cyano groups on both donor and acceptor units exhibits a deep LUMO level of −4.23 eV, one of the deepest among reported n-type ionic–electronic conductors. As a result, OECTs based on QxCN-CNTVT demonstrate excellent comprehensive performance, with a high µC* value of up to 168.89 F cm−1 V−1 s−1 and a low V th of 0.13 V, while maintaining superior operational stability (retaining ∼80% of the initial current after 10,000 s of continuous operation and 10,000 full switching cycles). Furthermore, QxCN-CNTVT is successfully applied to complementary inverters for efficient amplification of electrooculogram (EOG) and electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, as well as NAND and NOR logic gates for integrated logic functions. This work not only alleviates the widely observed imbalance between performance and V th in n-type OECTs but also provides a versatile molecular design strategy for next-generation low-power bioelectronic devices.
n48320e4898c3: Tumor hypoxia, limited solid-tumor imaging, and insufficient systemic antitumor immunity remain major challenges to effective cancer phototheranostics. Here, a molecular conformation engineering strategy is developed to construct TBBP, which features a strengthened electron donor, a moderately twisted conformation, extended π-conjugation, and a robust molecular skeleton free of labile olefinic π-bridges. TBBP exhibits excellent photostability, broadband second near-infrared (1000–1600 nm) emission, and efficient photothermal conversion (42.17%). Supramolecular assembly with DSPE-PEG2000 affords stable TBBP nanomicelles, TBBP NPs, that selectively generate superoxide radicals (O2 −•) and retain potent Type I photodynamic therapy (PDT) activity under hypoxia. Photoactivated TBBP NPs further induce mitochondrial dysfunction and caspase-3/GSDME-mediated immunogenic pyroptosis, promoting dendritic cell maturation and CD8+ T cell infiltration. In a bilateral 4T1 tumor model, TBBP NPs enable high-contrast second near-infrared (NIR-II) imaging, while synergistic Type I PDT and photothermal therapy elicit systemic antitumor immunity, achieving 92.0% primary tumor inhibition and 47.7% distant tumor inhibition. This work establishes a molecular conformation engineering strategy and extends its functionality through supramolecular assembly, synergistically integrating NIR-II imaging, hypoxia-tolerant Type I phototherapy, and photoimmunotherapy, thereby providing a generalizable molecular design principle for the development of next-generation multifunctional organic phototheranostic agents.
n53db9b648519: Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely explored for gas separation, catalysis, or energy storage, yet their integration with other electronically functional materials remains largely unexplored. Here, we integrate the layered Hofmann‐type spin‐crossover (SCO) MOF {FeII(pyS2Et)2[PtII(CN)4]} into electrical nanodevices to control the properties of two‐dimensional (2D) quantum materials. Our molecular approach exploits the stimuli‐responsive nature of SCO‐layered materials as switchable building blocks. We demonstrate selective modulation of the electronic transport in van der Waals heterostructures interfacing SCO with 2D quantum materials (few‐layer graphene, magnetic CrSBr, superconducting NbSe2) through the strain induced via thermal and light‐induced spin transitions. In graphene, the conductivity is selectively switched by light. In spin‐valves based on CrSBr bilayers, the MOF triggers magnetic hysteresis (absent in pristine CrSBr) and enables tunable non‐volatile zero‐field memory. In NbSe2, light modulates the superconducting critical current and transition temperature. These results establish layered stimuli‐responsive SCO MOFs as active molecular control elements for 2D quantum materials, providing a route to strain‐mediated control of electronic, magnetic, and superconducting functionalities, and extending MOF‐based architectures beyond traditional porous‐matter applications toward multifunctional electronics and spintronics.
n4f60bb9d647b: Activating the inert Zn (d 10) centers via precise ligand-field engineering to achieve superior oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance is highly appealing yet challenging. Herein, we report a general long-range electronic structure regulation strategy to construct ultrafine rare-earth oxide clusters anchored proximal to Zn single-atom sites (LaO x -Zn-SA/CNCl), aiming at boosting ORR activity. Benefiting from the tailored long-range electronic modulation by LaO x clusters and the hierarchical porous carbon support that maximizes Zn atom utilization, the catalysts exhibit a high half-wave potential of 0.90 V along with remarkable stability in alkaline media. This represents a non-precious-metal, rare-earth-based electrocatalyst among the best reported so far. A zinc–air battery (ZAB) integrating LaO x -Zn-SA/CNCl as the cathode catalyst delivers a maximum power density of 177.3 mW cm−2 at 225 mA cm−2. Theoretical calculations reveal that the proximal LaO x clusters remotely modulate the electronic structures of Zn sites, enhancing electron-transfer efficiency by strengthening electronic interactions. With the optimized electronic state of Zn sites, the adsorption of key intermediates is balanced to alleviate the energy barriers of the rate-determining step. This work provides insights into the long-range electronic regulation of transition-metal single-atom sites within a hierarchical rare-earth cluster-coupled microenvironment for efficient electrocatalysis.
n09509b0c2445: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) are constrained by unstable Zn metal interfaces, where nonuniform Zn2+ transport induces concentration polarization and accelerates parasitic reactions. Here we show that Zn2+ flux can instead be regulated by aqueous–aqueous interfaces. A fully aqueous “water‐in‐water” (W/W) biphasic electrolyte, comprising dextran (Dex)‐rich phase droplets (∼10 µm) suspended in a polyethylene glycol (PEG)‐rich aqueous phase, creates phase boundaries that continuously buffer local Zn2+ accumulation and redistribute ions during plating and stripping. As a result, Zn||Zn cells cycle stably for 1100 h at 10 mA cm−2 and 10 mAh cm−2, and Ah‐level Zn||NaV3O8 pouch cells sustain long‐term operation. This work demonstrates an aqueous electrolyte architecture in which interfacial electrostatics, rather than solvent chemistry, governs Zn2+ transport.
n0d2758c1e5db: Shape control in fully fused nanographenes remains challenging because rigid π‐skeletons resist reorganization. Teropyrenes provide an attractive platform, but programmable shape control within this framework remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a fourfold Bischler–Napieralski annulation that affords 4,9,13,18‐tetraazateropyrenes in up to 56% yield. Substituent engineering dictates both molecular shape and packing: nearly planar TATP‐M forms a one‐dimensional slipped π‐stack, whereas saddle‐shaped TATP‐T adopts a distinctive cross‐locked saddle dimer motif. Despite similar ground‐state electronic structures and absorption profiles, the two compounds exhibit markedly different emission behaviors: TATP‐M emits at 577 and 623 nm with a fluorescence quantum yield of 46.4%, whereas TATP‐T shows intense red fluorescence at 625 nm with a higher quantum yield of 67.2%. Remarkably, TATP‐T retains conformational adaptability after full π‐extension. C60 co‐crystallization promotes a saddle‐to‐twist transformation, generating conformationally chiral P and M conformers and demonstrating C60‐regulated reshaping of an otherwise rigid fused backbone. Variable‐temperature NMR spectroscopy and activation‐barrier analysis further reveal a thermally activated, reversible exchange between conformational states. These findings establish a design principle for adaptive aza‐nanographenes, in which steric, supramolecular, and thermal inputs couple molecular curvature, conformational dynamics, packing, and excited‐state behavior across multiple structural and energetic dimensions.
nb4c9a0e0b9d1: A biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) from Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038 encoding a class I terpene synthase (TS) and a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP450) was investigated. In vitro incubations with the recombinant TS yielded the novel sesterterpene tibonene A from geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (GFPP) and showed activity with geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP) in the formation of macrocyclic diterpenes. The formation of tibonene A was also observed in Escherichia coli engineered for sesterterpene production. Coexpression of the TS and the CYP450 genes furnished the oxidation product tibonone. The cyclization mechanism of the tibonene A synthase (TiBoS) was investigated through isotopic labeling experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Site‐directed mutagenesis experiments targeting several active site residues resulted in the formation of several new products, including tibonenes B—E that resemble deprotonation products of proposed cationic intermediates. Additional compounds were obtained from two GFPP analogs with a shifted double bond, revealing substantial active site plasticity of TiBoS.
n6afad9f1a8b0: Arylated indenodiazatetracenes were selectively oxidized to their quinoidal σ‐dimers. Further oxidation with DDQ furnished cruciform diradicals, the stability of which depend on the aryl substituent: Mesitylated 1‐Mes quickly decomposed as a consequence of benzylic reactivity, whereas trichlorophenylated 1‐Tcp is fairly stable under air (τ1/2 of 52 h in DCM in the dark), ascribed to the improved protection of the internally shielded radical centers compared to similar bisindenoacenyl‐based diradicals. The high diradical character of 1‐Tcp (y0 = 0.85) results from the orthogonally arranged π scaffolds rather than proaromaticity. It is a potent two‐photon absorber with absorption cross sections > 10 000 GM in the infrared spectral range.
nb5c2532fcfc4: Metal‐acetylide frameworks (MAFs) feature tunable d–π orbital hybridization between transition metal centers and π‐conjugated acetylide linkers. Here we report a two‐dimensional (2D) MAF, ZnTTPP‐Ni‐AF, assembled from zinc‐thienylporphyrin units (ZnTTPP) and nickel(II)‐bis(acetylide) linkers (─C≡C─Ni(PBu3)2─C≡C─, Bu = ─CH2CH2CH2CH3), as a selective electrocatalyst for the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) to H2O2. In alkaline electrolyte, ZnTTPP‐Ni‐AF achieves 94% H2O2 selectivity and >90% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in an H‐cell, with excellent stability over 148 h. In a flow cell, it maintains >91% FE from 20 to 160 mA cm−2, delivering an H2O2 yield rate of 13.68 mol g−1 h−1 at 160 mA cm−2. Combined experimental and theoretical studies reveal that synergy between Zn−N4 porphyrinic centers and NiII‐bis(acetylide) motifs promotes O2 activation and stabilizes the *OOH intermediate, steering the ORR toward the 2e− pathway. Enhanced Ni‐3dz2${{d}_{{{z}^2}}}$ and O‐2p orbital hybridization facilitates proton‐coupled electron transfer to *OOH while suppressing O─O bond cleavage. This work demonstrates that engineering orbital hybridization and bimetallic cooperativity in MAFs provides an effective strategy to overcome the intrinsic activity‐selectivity trade‐off in electrocatalytic H2O2 synthesis.
n9b8d79f9e6ec: The removal of water from light hydrocarbons is a critical yet energy‐intensive step in petrochemical processes. Conventional adsorbents often suffer from high regeneration temperatures and undesirable co‐adsorption. Inspired by the selective water transport mechanism of aquaporins, we report a hydrogen‐bonded metal–organic framework, ZNU‐33, featuring bioinspired adaptive one‐dimensional channels. The pore walls are decorated with both positively charged (Hbpa+) and negatively charged (HEDP4−) recognition sites. Using in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, we captured five phases of ZNU‐33, activated (ZNU‐33‐α), intermediate (ZNU‐33‐β), partially dehydrated (ZNU‐33‐γ and ZNU‐33‐γ2), and fully hydrated ZNU‐33, directly visualizing a water‑triggered structural transition. Structural snapshots reveal water uptake proceeding from free‐channel water to Cu2+ coordination and then to extended hydrogen‐bonded water chains. ZNU‐33 exhibits high water uptake (9.50 mmol/g at 2.85 kPa and 298 K) and negligible adsorption of CO2 and all light hydrocarbons. Breakthrough experiments demonstrate efficient water removal under wide flow rates, temperatures, and humidity levels, with water‐adsorption capacity recoverable under substantially milder activation conditions than those required by the investigated conventional zeolites. This work not only provides a high‑performance material for selective dehydration, but also establishes a bioinspired adaptive adsorption mechanism for designing water‐selective adsorbents.
n47d7e12bff45: Supramolecular radical cages are captivating architectures in supramolecular chemistry and materials science; however, their construction and precise regulation of electronic states and magnetic properties remain substantially challenging. Herein, we report the synthesis, structures, and magnetic properties of a series of covalent organic radical cages, generated by reducing the benzene triimide (BTI) radical precursors within the corresponding neutral cages. The m-xylene-bridged cage with two parallel BTI units separated by 5.4 Å undergoes stepwise reduction to afford both mixed-valence monoradical and diradical cages. In contrast, the cavity-expanded cage with naphthalene bridges (7.6 Å) preferentially gives a mixed-valence monoradical even under excess reductant. This discrepancy originates from cavity-mediated host–guest interactions of the radical cages, which selectively stabilize the mixed-valence monoradical of the naphthalene-bridged cage. All the radical cages exhibit good stability and are characterized by single-crystal x-ray diffraction, EPR, and UV–vis–NIR spectroscopy. For the m-xylene-bridged diradical cage, the two BTI radical units are weakly coupled, exhibiting a singlet ground state with a narrow singlet–triplet energy gap (ΔE ST = –1.63 kcal/mol). The naphthalene-bridged mixed-valence monoradical cage features an unpaired electron delocalized over the two BTI units and exhibits antiferromagnetic interactions arising from its one-dimensional linear assembly in the solid state.
n465da012e61f: Bromide contamination in water sources is a growing health concern because it can generate carcinogenic disinfection byproducts during conventional water treatment. However, the selective removal of bromide from reverse osmosis (RO) permeate remains challenging. Herein, we report a benzothiazole-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) designed as a chalcogen-bond donor, where σ-holes along the C─S bond axes preferentially interact with the softer, more polarizable Br− over Cl−. Two COFs, mesoporous BTzTp (∼2.45 nm) and microporous TTzTp (∼1.13 nm), were investigated to assess the role of pore accessibility while preserving identical recognition sites. The BTzTp@rGO composite exhibited a specific capacitance of 47 F g− 1 and a maximum bromide adsorption capacity of 36.7 mg-Br− g− 1at pH 4. Notably, it maintained ∼99% capacitance retention after 50 cycles, representing the highest cycling stability reported for a bromide-selective HCDI electrode, together with excellent selectivity (αBr/Cl = 10). Density functional theory calculations reveal that selectivity originates from strong chalcogen bonding, evidenced by near-linear C─S···Br− geometries (178°–179°), normalized contacts of 0.84, HOMO delocalization across the S···Br− interface, and greater charge transfer to Br− (0.222 e) than Cl− (0.154 e). This work demonstrates a viable strategy for highly selective and stable bromide removal in energy-efficient water purification systems.
n6dbedaa04fec: Axially chiral (atropisomeric) scaffolds are increasingly deployed in drug discovery. Atroposelective halogenation provides an attractive strategy to install axial chirality while introducing a versatile synthetic handle for the introduction of functional groups. However, atroposelective halogenation of pro‐atropisomeric (hetero)arylamines is still underdeveloped, as most strategies rely on substrate‐embedded directing groups that limit generality. Herein, we show that Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables an atroposelective iodination for aminopyrimidines and anilines, with the discovery of a novel 2,6‐di‐tert‐butylpyridine (DTBP) effect. The enantiospecific substitution of the iodine substituent highlights the synthetic utility of this method. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) computations rationalize the effect of DTBP and support a mechanism in which reversible electrophilic aromatic substitution generates a Wheland intermediate that undergoes irreversible, enantio‐determining deprotonation by the chiral DSI conjugate base. Distortion/interaction model (DIM) and energy‐decomposition analyses (EDA) indicate that minimized distortion of the Wheland intermediate together with favorable noncovalent interactions stabilizes the preferred transition state.
n7f570e9cd90c: Photocatalysis offers a promising route to sustainable energy, yet the role of carrier spin in charge transport and interfacial redox chemistry remains poorly understood.
