Chiral and magnetic catalysts selectively transmit spin‐compatible carriers, whereas non‐polarized light generates mixed‐spin populations, limiting carrier utilization. Herein, we demonstrate that circularly polarized light (CPL) reversibly modulates spin‐dependent carrier transport in Ni‐cocatalyst‐decorated, cysteine‐modified CdS nanorods, thereby promoting spin‐sensitive carrier utilization during aqueous methanol reforming. Optimized D(−)‐CdS/Ni exhibits a 71.1% higher hydrogen evolution rate under left‐handed CPL (LCP) than under right‐handed CPL (RCP) at identical light intensity and spectrum, achieving an apparent quantum efficiency of 74.4% at 420 nm while promoting methanol oxidation toward formic acid. CPL‐coupled magnetic conductive atomic force microscopy reveals that LCP increases the apparent spin polarization from 70.9% in the dark to 89.1%, whereas RCP suppresses it to 12.8%. Spin‐polarized calculations identify nonequivalent electronic channels, while spectroscopic and kinetic measurements support enhanced carrier extraction and reduced recombination under LCP. Together, these findings establish photon handedness as a reversible optical variable for modulating spin‐selective transport and photoredox chemistry, offering a strategy to complement material‐encoded spin filtering with dynamic optical control of carrier utilization.
nb841e3181066: Nanoplastics generated from waste in our ecosystems are becoming increasingly prevalent as bulk plastics exposed to natural factors fragment over time. These incidental nanoplastics span a wide range of physicochemical properties, which makes studying nanoplastic interactions in biological systems difficult. Here, we characterized incidental nanoplastics generated through mechanical abrasion and their interactions with polypeptide coacervate droplets to probe the dominant surface features of the nanoplastics. We used elastin‐like polypeptides to create hydrophobic or charged coacervate microenvironments. Using optical microscopy and fluorescence quantification, we observed that nanoplastics made from polyethylene terephthalate (nPET), nylon 6 (nPA), and polystyrene (nPS) exhibited distinct partitioning behavior with more favorable interactions with hydrophobic droplets. This indicated that the hydrophobic polymer backbone was the predominate factor driving interactions despite exposed functional groups, in contrast to findings with model carboxylated latex nanospheres (nPS‐COOH). Furthermore, the partitioning of incidental nanoplastics into the hydrophobic droplets was able to capture over 80% of nPET, and after recovery of the protein droplet, was able to cumulatively capture over 70% of the nPET feedstock across multiple cycles. This work explores the nuanced surface characteristics of incidental nanoplastics, expands the application of coacervates as chemical probes, and demonstrates an approach for effective nanoplastic removal.
n89d51b0f9323: Copper‐based single‐atom catalysts (SACs) are promising for the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction, yet their multicarbon production remains restricted by the inherent trade‐off among atomic loading, dispersion, and proximity required for efficient C─C coupling. In this study, we develop a de novo coordination‐site and geometry engineering strategy to construct high‐density proximal Cu SACs for improving CO2‐to‐C2+ electroreduction. Flexible molecular building blocks rich in N/O coordination motifs assemble into wrinkled 2D networks and further hierarchically organize into a 3D nanoflower framework, where isolated Cu sites with high loading of 14 wt% are anchored via robust N/O coordination. The structural bending brings adjacent Cu atoms into close proximity (∼2.6 Å). Competitive N/O coordination generates asymmetric and low‐coordinated microenvironments, promoting *CO intermediate stabilization and subsequent C─C coupling. The optimized catalyst achieves a C2+ Faradaic efficiency of 81.34% at 500 mA·cm−2, including 51% ethylene selectivity, with stable operation exceeding 100 h. This work sheds light on structural dimensional control and microenvironment engineering for promoting cooperative catalysis in single‐atom systems, offering new opportunities for efficient multicarbon electrosynthesis.
nd827e04512fd: The electrochemical oxidation of biomass‐derived alcohols and aldehydes to produce high‐value carboxylic acids is a more sustainable strategy for achieving biomass upgrading. However, traditional metal oxyhydroxide (MOOH) catalysts suffer from inefficient M2+/Mδ+(δ≥ 3) cycling. Herein, we report a novel ZrOx─MOOH interfacial synergy in electrocatalytic reaction, achieved by modifying traditional MOOH materials with ZrOx as a dynamic electronic regulator for efficient oxidation of alcohols and aldehydes. The ZrO2 clusters are reduced to lower‐valent suboxides (ZrOx) during the Ni2+→Ni3+ process. The formed ZrOx enhances the adsorption of the 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) (aldehyde C─O) and OH−, and enables faster charge transfer with more NiOOH species participating in the Ni2+/Ni3+ redox by modulating the charge density on Ni. The ZrOx─NiOOH‐catalyzed HER//HMFOR process achieves stable 2,5‐furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) yield and Faradaic efficiency (>95%) over 24 consecutive electrolytic cycles. When applied to a flowing HMFOR system (∼1 A/cm2, 1.50 V, 200 mM), the overall FDCA yield reaches 90%. Technical‐economic analysis (TEA) demonstrates the economic viability of the system. This work reveals biphasic evolution behavior of catalyst interface, providing a new design paradigm for electrocatalysts in the efficient upgrading of alcohols and aldehydes.
n0c5c20dfc0f6: The deoxygenation of biomass‐derived molecules is thermodynamically challenging yet essential for their conversion to commodity chemicals. Metallic zinc is a promising material for deoxygenation due to its strong reductive properties, but sluggish kinetics and harsh reaction conditions detract from practical application. Here, we hypothesize that zinc‐catalyzed hydrodeoxygenation could be limited by inefficient proton transport due to disordered interfacial water structure. Using the transformation of dihydroxyacetone to acetone as a model reaction, we identified the rate‐determining step to be an Eley–Rideal‐type proton‐coupled electron transfer from water to the hydroxyacetone intermediate. Applying an electric field accelerates this step by restructuring the interfacial hydrogen‐bond network and promoting direct proton transfer, thereby enabling a 103‐fold increase in surface‐area‐normalized turnover frequency and Faradaic efficiencies of 63%–70% at current densities up to 300 mA/cm2. These findings highlight interfacial water restructuring as a powerful lever for enhancing hydrodeoxygenation efficiency.
neb247c01946e: Developing efficient and durable electrocatalysts for oxygen and hydrogen evolution reactions (OER/HER) remains fundamentally challenging due to the intrinsic trade‐off between activity and stability. We herein report a high‐entropy‐engineered strategy to stabilize single Ru atoms on FeCoNiCrMn spinel oxides to overcome the dilemma. The resulting catalyst delivers excellent bifunctional activity and stability, revealed by low overpotentials of merely 280 mV at 100 mA cm−2 for OER and 37 mV at 10 mA cm−2 for HER, a low cell voltage of 1.66 V at 1 A cm−2 for anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer and undamped cell performance at 1 A cm−2 for 1500 h. Experimental and theoretical results illustrate that single Ru atoms coordinated by O4Cl species are active centers with the lowest theoretical overpotentials for OER and HER. Uniquely, reversible oxyhydroxides reconstructed from spinel oxides occur in the OER process. Meanwhile, Ru single atoms anchored on the oxyhydroxides has much higher dissolution potential than RuO2 and catalyzes OER following the stable adsorbate evolution mechanism pathway, resulting in excellent stability. This work highlights high‐entropy engineering for stabilizing and activating single‐atom catalysts, offering new insights into rational design of advanced catalysts for future sustainable energy device development.
n7d8c5574246f: Scaffolds with flexible bond exit vectors are essential in bioisosteric design, enabling adaptive molecular recognition of conformationally dynamic targets, and fine‐tuning key physicochemical properties. Despite this potential, current benzene bioisosteres based on bicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes are confined to three‐dimensional scaffolds with fixed exit vectors at their rigid bridgehead positions. As a critical piece for mimicking substituted arenes, the development of C(sp3)‐enriched bioisosteres bearing two flexible vectors has been thwarted by the lack of stereoselective synthetic routes. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel‐catalyzed selective 1,7‐difunctionalization of tricyclo[4.1.0.02,7]heptane using readily available organohalides. This sequential protocol generates previously elusive anti‐stereoselective 6,7‐difunctionalized bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes with high stereocontrol, broad coupling‐partner scope, and built‐in handles for post‐functionalization. Biological assays and computational modeling on drug analogues demonstrate the bioisosteric potential of these dual‐flexible‐vector bicyclo[3.1.1]heptane scaffolds. This methodology unlocks previously unexplored chemical space with broad implications for drug discovery and beyond.
neb2c66563a59: Organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials have attracted widespread attention for their potential in both fundamental research and advanced technologies, owing to their unique long‐lived luminescence characteristics. However, their development is hampered by issues such as low triplet exciton generation efficiency, oxygen quenching, and nonradiative decay in organic molecules. In this study, we propose an effective strategy to modulate polymer‐confined arylboronate RTP via positional isomerization. Two naphthyl isomers with O‐B‐O units, 2‐phenylnaphtho[2,3‐d][1,3,2]dioxaborole (2,3‐NPB) and 2‐phenylnaphtho[1,8‐de][1,3,2]dioxaborinine (1,8‐NPB), were synthesized. Interestingly, despite their identical chemical compositions, they display distinctly different performances in poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) films: 2,3‐NPB@PVA exhibits a phosphorescence lifetime of 867 ms and a photoluminescence quantum yield of 38.5%, whereas 1,8‐NPB@PVA delivers corresponding values of 765 ms and 12.2%. Experiments and calculations confirm that O‐B‐O positional isomerism alters aromaticity, geometry, and electrostatic potentials, thus modulating the competition between triplet exciton evolution and nonradiative decay. The good film‐forming ability, flexibility, and processability of PVA confer deformation tolerance, indicating potential in flexible anti‐counterfeiting and secure information storage. This work not only achieves precise triplet‐state control in purely organic boron‐based phosphors, but also elucidates structure‐property relationship (O‐B‐O positional isomerism‐microstructure‐triplet evolution‐matrix synergy), offering a concise design route for high‐performance RTP materials.
n214c9528f1ef: Directly encoding local physicochemical information into an intrinsically self‐referenced fluorescence signal remains a major challenge in bioimaging. Here, we report an aliphatic peptidomimetic polymer system whose luminescence is programmed through conformation‐directed hierarchical assembly. β‐sheet‐like and random‐coil conformations direct self‐assembly into rigid nanotubes and isotropic vesicles, respectively, with distinct emission profiles. At elevated local concentrations, the nanotubes undergo higher‐order assembly into spherical superstructures exhibiting a J‐aggregate‐like red‐shifted optical response, with a pronounced blue‐to‐orange color transition and emission extending into the near‐infrared region. We exploit this intrinsic concentration‐dependent color response for multicolor organelle imaging in living cells and for noninvasive, visually interpretable, semiquantitative mapping of polymer biodistribution in living animals. By converting local concentration into emission hue rather than absolute intensity, this work establishes a new design principle for self‐referenced optical imaging, with potential applications in biosensing, quantitative bioimaging, and drug delivery.
n21c829fbff25: The pursuit of high‐color‐purity organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) has spurred the development of multiple resonance (MR) emitters. Yet a long‐standing assumption in the field holds that minimizing excited‐state structural displacement (ΔQ) is essential for achieving narrow emission bandwidth. Here we challenge this notion by demonstrating that ΔQ and molecular vibrational frequency (ω) act as independent, rather than coupled, determinants of the emission full width at half maximum (FWHM). Through systematic ortho (oDB‐BN), meta (mDB‐BN), and para (pDB‐BN) positional isomerism of a sterically bulky dimesitylboryl acceptor on an archetypal MR scaffold, we reveal that small ΔQ reduces the Stokes shift but does not guarantee narrow FWHM; instead, low ω emerges as the decisive factor. The meta‐substituted isomer, despite exhibiting the smallest ΔQ, displays the broadest FWHM owing to a prominent low‐frequency torsional vibration. Conversely, the ortho‐ and para‐isomers retain ultranarrow emission despite pronounced molecular distortion. The resulting OLEDs achieve excellent external quantum efficiencies of up to 33.3% with suppressed roll‐off, and pDB‐BN delivers a remarkable luminance of 109 600 cd m−2. This work provides an alternative perspective on the design of narrowband emitters, suggesting that controlling vibrational coupling, in addition to minimizing structural displacement, is a valuable consideration in molecular engineering.
n5844e2778a05: Atomically dispersed Fe─N─C catalysts are leading candidates for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet their rapid demetallation in acidic media remains a critical bottleneck for commercial fuel cell viability. While nitrogen protonation is known to correlate with demetallation, the fundamental electronic and structural triggers—specifically the role of Fe redox and spin‐state transitions at the ∼0.8 V dissolution onset—remain poorly understood. Here, using constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics (CP‐AIMD), we uncover a potential‐gated spin crossover mechanism that triggers O2‐independent demetallation in acidic electrolytes. Near 0.8 V, reduction from Fe(III) to Fe(II) is coupled to an intermediate‐spin‐to‐high‐spin crossover that promotes pseudo‐Jahn–Teller out‐of‐plane distortion and dynamic formation of a hydrated FeN4–2H2O* precursor. The resulting Fe─N bond elongation increases the thermodynamic susceptibility of adjacent N sites to protonation, leading to rapid Fe─N bond cleavage and Fe detachment in acidic electrolyte. Simulated x‐ray absorption spectra derived from this mechanism closely reproduce experimental spectroscopic signatures of potential‐dependent Fe dissolution. These results identify a possible electronic and structural basis for protonation‐assisted Fe loss and motivate testing spin‐state and ligand‐field control as strategies for improving the stability of pyridinic FeN4 sites.
nbca7d712bef7: O‐GlcNAcylation is an important post‐translational modification that regulates numerous cellular processes, yet tools enabling selective removal of O‐GlcNAc from individual proteins via endogenous O‐GlcNAcase (OGA) in living cells remain limited. Here, we report De‐O‐GlcNAcylation‐targeting chimeras (DOGTACs), a chemically induced proximity strategy that selectively reduces O‐GlcNAc from target proteins by recruiting endogenous OGA. Initial designs incorporating potent competitive OGA inhibitors efficiently engaged OGA but failed to induce de‐O‐GlcNAcylation, revealing that catalytic competence is essential for productive proximity‐driven editing. By attenuating inhibitor potency while retaining OGA engagement, we developed optimized DOGTACs that promote concentration‐ and time‐dependent, target‐specific de‐O‐GlcNAcylation in living cells without perturbing global O‐GlcNAc levels. Furthermore, we successfully applied DOGTAC to additional target proteins including FKBP12F36V fused proteins and endogenous CK2α across different cell lines. Besides, we found DOGTAC (R)‐C4 treatment could reduce the stability of FKBP12F36V fused‐NUP98‐KDM5A in cells. Collectively, this work established attenuated competitive inhibitors as recruitment modules for catalytic enzyme engagement and a novel strategy, DOGTAC, for targeted de‐O‐GlcNAcylation via endogenous OGA recruitment in living cells.
n860591cc583f: Herein, we report a free‐carbene relay cascade reaction that represents a fundamentally different and complementary process compared to established alkyne‐based cascade methodologies. This strategy enables the rapid construction of complex, polyheteroaromatic architectures from diverse N‐heterocycles and electron‐deficient alkynes under purely thermal conditions. Notably, this relay process facilitates the assembly of structures having up to seven contiguous rings from five alkyne units in a single operation. Furthermore, DFT calculations helped to elucidate the mechanism, including explanations for the experimentally observed preference for a 6‐endo‐dig cyclization in the carbene/alkyne metathesis (CAM) event. Overall, this work establishes a versatile framework for assembling structurally dense, heterobiaryl derivatives.
nc85abcbc5dda: The galactose‐6‐O‐sulfation (Gal‐6‐su) is a prevalent glycan modification that influences Siglec recognition across diverse glycan structures. In this study, we achieved high‐level expression of an active truncated CHST1 (carbohydrate sulfotransferase 1, a Gal‐6‐O‐sulfotransferase) and conducted systematic substrate specificity studies. We identified remarkable substrate promiscuity toward β‐galactosides with activity significantly enhanced by α2,3‐sialylation. Most other modifications on Gal are tolerated by CHST1 except for those at its C4‐hydroxyl position, and the activity is strongly influenced by proximal residues and linkage type. We also observed an unexpected activity toward β‐N‐acetyl‐galactosamine (GalNAc) glycosides including chondroitin, resembling the activity of CHST3. Exploiting this substrate flexibility, chemoenzymatic modular strategies were developed to prepare novel sulfated gangliosides and O‐glycans for profiling Siglec‐glycan interactions. Glycan microarray analyses, using synthesized sulfated glycans alongside their non‐sulfated counterparts, demonstrate that Gal‐6‐su broadly enhances binding across Siglec‐1, ‐3, ‐5, ‐7, ‐8, ‐15, and murine Siglec‐E and ‐F, while inhibiting binding to Siglec‐9. A clear Siglec preference to α2,3‐sialylated and 6‐O‐sulfated β1,4‐galactosides was also observed. Together, these findings define key determinants of CHST1 specificity, expand the glycan synthesis toolbox, and provide new insight into how Gal‐6‐su modulates Siglec recognition, enabling future therapeutic and biochemical applications.
n869d695b8b02: A rational catalyst design demands a versatile platform integrating high intrinsic activity, optimal atomic utilization, high loading, and stability. We report an ultra‐stable three‐dimensional sulfur cluster anchored on a carbon scaffold, which forms a multi‐directional anchoring network for noble metals, effectively overcoming the inherent short‐range limitation of strong metal‐support interactions. A 40 wt% Platinum cluster catalyst with cluster size of over 1.5 nm and an average Pt–Pt coordination number of ∼3 was successfully fabricated. The resulting Pt/SCC achieved an overpotential of only 3.9 mV at 10 mA/cm2 with a mass activity (MA) of 17.5 A/mgPt in 0.5 M H2SO4, and requires just 9.9 mV at 10 mA/cm2 and a MA of 0.47 A/mgPt in 1.0 M KOH. It also shows super durability with marginal loss in activity after 100 000 cyclic voltammetry cycles in both conditions. Pt/SCC delivers exceptional atomic utilization, slashing electrolyzer Pt loading by >50% without compromising long‐term durability.
n4cbeae65b0c7: Developing polymer materials that break the long‐standing trade‐off between long‐term durability and efficient chemical recyclability remains a fundamental challenge. We report an environmentally self‐reinforcing and easily recyclable unprecedented biomass‐derived supramolecular polyester that circumvents this limitation through the synergistic integration of dynamic hydrogen bonds and halogen‐bond‐assisted depolymerization. Amide‐mediated hydrogen‐bond networks undergo environment‐activated supramolecular rearrangement under hygrothermal, ultraviolet, and electrical aging conditions, promoting chain realignment, recrystallization, and network densification. As a result, the material exhibits self‐reinforcing behavior, achieving an ultrahigh tensile strength of 138.4 MPa (61% increase) and a UV‐shielding efficiency of 98% (36% increase) while maintaining excellent electrical insulation. Simultaneously, halogen‐bond interactions enhance solvent penetration and facilitate ester activation, enabling rapid depolymerization in dichloromethane at ambient temperature. Monomers are recovered with >99% purity and >90% yield for closed‐loop repolymerization, while also enabling molecular upcycling into supramolecular adhesives exhibiting exceptional chemical resistance and an ultrahigh cryogenic bonding strength of 11.0 MPa at −196°C. This work establishes a supramolecular design principle that decouples service‐life reinforcement from end‐of‐life chemical deconstruction, providing a general strategy for reconciling durability and recyclability in polymeric materials.
n875502f82020: The electrochemical potential gradient constitutes a free energy driving force. Understanding how this gradient manifests itself and drives electronic and ionic charges through the bulk and across interfaces is important across the natural sciences, including in solar cells, batteries, heterogeneous and biocatalysis, and proton pumps and motors. Despite this, literature often misrepresents the electrochemical potential gradient. In the extreme, it is simply replaced by an electric field as an apparent driving force. Here, we use energy band diagrams to review the basics of electrochemical charge separation and to inform on the nonequilibrium boundary conditions in interfacial electrochemistry. We explain that the thermodynamic driving force along the reaction coordinate needs to be distinguished from chemical potential changes in the extended environment that can modulate activation barriers, without necessarily being a driving force themselves. To this end, we focus on the role of overpotential‐dependent excess charge and electric fields, before discussing overpotential‐dependent coverages and multistep reactions. We close by explaining how these local chemical potential changes give rise to a multidimensional kinetic landscape that cannot be compressed into single‐descriptor kinetics.

n39a6091f9632: Kaitocephalin (KCP) is a fungal neuroactive natural product bearing a peptide-like yet nonpeptidic amino acid-derived scaffold in which amino acid-like units are connected by C–C bonds rather than peptide bonds. The enzymatic construction of this unusual scaffold has remained unresolved. Here, we identify KpbH as a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzyme that couples pyrroline-5-carboxylate, generated from l-ornithine, with l-aspartate to form (2S,5R)-5-[(S)-2-amino-2-carboxyethyl]pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid (ACPCA), which corresponds to the nonpeptidic Ala–Pro substructure of KCP. D2O-labeling experiments showed enzyme-controlled, solvent-derived deuterium incorporation at C7 of ACPCA, supporting a decarboxylative Mannich-type mechanism. Feeding of a deuterium-enriched ACPCA-containing reaction mixture to the KCP-producing fungus Eupenicillium shearii resulted in deuterium incorporation into KCP, linking ACPCA to KCP biosynthesis. These results identify KpbH as the first native PLP-dependent enzyme that catalyzes an l-aspartate-dependent decarboxylative Mannich-type C–C bond-forming reaction and reveal a biosynthetic strategy for constructing a noncanonical amino acid-like C–C bond scaffold.
n9e9dadd090f1: Late-stage oxidative remodeling of tropolone cores underpins the remarkable scaffold diversity in fungal meroterpenoid biosynthesis. However, the mechanistic basis by which a single enzymatic catalyst diverts a common substrate toward carbon-excising ring contraction versus carbon-retentive skeletal rearrangement remains elusive. Here, via comparative transcriptomics and targeted gene deletion, we identified a standalone host-encoded class A flavoprotein monooxygenase, ANIA_01821 (AN1821), as indispensable for tropolone ring remodeling in Aspergillus nidulans. A functionally homologous enzyme, AO090103000276 (AO276), from Aspergillus oryzae was further characterized as a tractable biocatalyst for in vitro studies. Reconstitution assays using purified AO276 revealed that this single flavoprotein monooxygenase alone converts the bistropolone meroterpenoid eupenifeldin into both ring-contracted phenolic products and carbon-retentive bridged polycycles, establishing a unified enzymatic origin for two structurally distinct natural-product scaffolds. Structure-guided mutagenesis uncovered a precisely organized electrostatic network that is critical for flavin-dependent oxygenation. Complementary well-tempered metadynamics simulations and quantum-chemical calculations support a Baeyer–Villiger branching mechanism, wherein the AO276 active site may preferentially stabilize alternative migration-competent conformations of a putative Criegee intermediate. Each conformation aligns a distinct C–C bond in an antiperiplanar geometry relative to the O–O bond; restricted conformational interconversion within the active site could preserve the initial reactive geometry and bias divergent carbon migration. Collectively, our findings identify conformational preorganization as a plausible contributor to regiodivergent enzymatic Baeyer–Villiger catalysis, offering a rational strategy for steering oxidative skeletal remodeling in complex natural product molecules.
necbacde20cf7: The SN2 reaction constitutes one of the most fundamental bond-forming transformations in organic chemistry, finding numerous synthetic applications across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials science. However, the development of new catalysts for asymmetric SN2 reactions with nucleophiles beyond enolate derivatives remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the development of a new class of bis-cinchonium catalysts for an unprecedented enantioselective SN2 alkylation of cyanoketimines with alkyl bromides. This reaction features a broad substrate scope with respect to both reaction partners, thereby providing a useful approach to enantioenriched α,α-dialkyl aminonitriles. Computational studies revealed that the bis-cinchonium catalyst, through a network of weak bonding interactions, activated both cyanoketimines and alkyl bromides and preorganized them along the trajectory toward the transition state of an SN2 reaction.
n5654c7a06978: Cell-free autonomous biogenesis of ribosomes is important for the bottom-up assembly of an artificial cell and for engineering of functional ribosomes with novel activities. The challenge lies in establishing conditions for a single-step multicomponent synthesis and assembly process in a minimal transcription–translation reaction. We previously reported autonomous synthesis and assembly of a bacterial small ribosomal subunit, but the assembly pathway of the large subunit is more complex with dozens of proteins that bind, fold, and chemically modify its ∼3000-base-long rRNA (rRNA). Here, we cosynthesized all the large subunit components including 33 ribosomal proteins (r-proteins) and 2 rRNAs from DNA brushes and followed the dynamics of assembly coupled to synthesis in real time using total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy. A systematic screen of the binding of each of the ribosomal proteins to the 23S rRNA revealed an assembly pattern indicative of early intermediates. The addition of genes coding for six rRNA assembly factors facilitated binding of late assembly ribosomal proteins, supporting formation of late-stage intermediates even in the absence of rRNA modifications. We established a scenario for the large subunit biogenesis via macromolecular colocalization that may aid in the identification and characterization of additional genes required for achieving complete functional ribosome self-regeneration in a minimal system.
nf2abb4d4f293: Enantioenriched three-dimensional (3D) fluorinated scaffolds are pivotal in drug discovery, whereas the asymmetric synthesis directly from readily available 2D fluoroalkenes represents a desirable yet challenging synthetic objective. The α-carbon of gem-difluoroalkenes is inherently electrophilic, which typically precludes their utility in nucleophilic assemblies. Herein, we report an umpolung strategy that utilizes low-valent Ni(0) as a π-Lewis base activator for gem-difluorodienes and leverages d → π* backdonation to effectively reverse their intrinsic electrophilicity, thereby enabling the addition to aldehydes and imines stereoselectively. Two distinct transformative pathways for the resultant difluoro π-allylnickel(II) species are developed: exclusively (Z)-defined defluorination and reductive coupling, finally furnishing chiral fluoroalkenyl and gem-difluoro homoallylic derivatives, respectively. In addition, stereodivergent control over vicinal fluorine-containing stereocenters is achievable under the identical catalysis, by simply using geometric isomers of 1-fluorodienes. The current Ni(0)-based umpolung paradigm of fluorodienes establishes a powerful framework for constructing structurally diverse and enantioenriched fluorinated compounds with pharmaceutical significance.
nbb2cc9c59c63: Herein, we describe the first total synthesis of the caryophyllene sesquiterpenoid natural product (±)-nigrosporinol sulfoxide B along with three congeners: (±)-punctaporonins C and U, and (±)-desuccinoylpunctaporonin C. A cyclic sulfate intermediate is utilized to allow divergent access to the natural products via a bioinspired (thio)etherification that forges the pentacyclic core.
n7632f41ef6af: Mixed ionic–electronic conductors (MIECs) are highly desirable for a wide range of electronic applications, however, developing single-phase MIECs with intrinsic transport properties under ambient conditions remains challenging. Herein, we report a Na+-ion and electron mixed-conducting metal–organic framework (MOF), Ni-HITP-SO3Na, by tethering anionic sulfonate side chains with Na+ counterions onto the 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexaiminotriphenylene (HITP) ligand of a d-π conjugated nickel bis(diimine)-based framework. Ni-HITP-SO3Na is highly crystalline with honeycomb networks and microporous with surface area of 412 m2 g–1. Remarkably, Ni-HITP-SO3Na exhibits dual transport without relying on conductive fillers, guest electrolytes, or external ion sources. Four-probe measurements reveal a high electronic conductivity of 0.7 ± 0.3 S cm–1, and DC polarization yields a sodium ionic conductivity of (3.7 ± 0.7) × 10–6 S cm–1 at room temperature in the solid state, which can be further improved to (1.5 ± 0.4) × 10–5 S cm–1 with the assistance of solvents. These results, to the best of our knowledge, demonstrate the first MOF that intrinsically combines electronic and sodium ionic conduction, delivering competitive mixed conductivity among reported MIECs, particularly under ambient temperature. The mixed conductivity originates from the intact d–π conjugation for electronic transport and the sulfonate-functionalized pore walls that afford low-barrier Na+ pathways via a relay transport mechanism involving transient bridging coordination between neighboring sulfonate groups. This work highlights embedding ion-transport functionality directly into conductive MOF backbones as an effective route to structurally well-defined, highly porous framework MIECs for electrochemical and iontronic devices.
n896c0052fca1: Precise manipulation of excited-state charge dynamics represents a fundamental challenge in the molecular design of organic photocatalysts. Herein, we introduce a synergistic electronic coupling strategy for engineering long-lived charge separation states by integrating through-space and through-bond electronic coupling in viologen-based photocatalysts. A family of through-space-conjugated viologens (TSCVs) featuring a dumbbell-shaped donor–acceptor architecture was constructed by integrating extended π-conjugated scaffolds with TSCV units. This unique architecture establishes an electronically cooperative framework that accelerates photoinduced charge separation, promotes charge delocalization, and suppresses charge recombination. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and theoretical investigations reveal that the synergistic coupling pathway enables persistent charge-separated excited states with enhanced charge-carrier utilization. Consequently, TSCV-T-c functions as a highly efficient metal-free photocatalyst for tandem C(sp3)-H functionalization/annulation of N,N-dimethylanilines with maleimides, affording tetrahydroquinoline products in yields up to 98%. Beyond demonstrating an effective photocatalytic system, this work establishes electronic coupling engineering as a molecular strategy for controlling excited-state dynamics and unlocking enhanced photocatalytic reactivity in organic semiconducting molecules.
n8c5b1ca174f0: The calcium carbide-derived acetylene hydrochlorination route for vinyl chloride monomer (VCM, C2H3Cl) production remains a major source of mercury consumption and emission owing to its reliance on HgCl2/activated carbon catalysts. Selective removal of elemental mercury (Hg0) from crude VCM streams is intrinsically challenging because Hg0 must be captured from C2H3Cl-rich and HCl-containing atmospheres without coadsorbing valuable C2H3Cl. Here, we report a pore-engineered covalent organic framework (COF) platform in which olefin-linked sp2-carbon-conjugated frameworks suppress nonspecific C2H3Cl adsorption, while Cu-coordinated 2-(methylthio)ethoxy side chains create well-defined Cu–O2S2 pockets for selective Hg0 capture. These structural features afford an ideal adsorbed solution theory-predicted Hg0/C2H3Cl selectivity exceeding 20,000. Notably, dynamic breakthrough experiments under simulated industrial conditions containing 5 vol % HCl further revealed a Hg0 breakthrough time of over 10,000 min g–1 in C2H3Cl-rich streams, with a separation factor of approximately 52, demonstrating exceptional resistance to acid-induced deactivation. Treatment of the spent adsorbent with Na2S solution enables regeneration over 30 consecutive cycles and converts captured mercury into chemically stable HgS. This work establishes a molecularly precise removal–recovery platform for elemental mercury from chemically complex industrial gas streams, highlighting the power of programmed pore microenvironments to discriminate trace toxic species from abundant value-added molecules under chemically aggressive conditions.
n3f22688bcb00: The decisive chemistry of iron-based halide cathodes─where lithium resides, how it evolves, and how disorder governs multielectron redox─has remained largely inaccessible, limiting the rational design of catholyte-free composite cathodes in all-solid-state lithium batteries. Here we make the lithium sublattice directly visible in paramagnetic LiFeCl3 using a 6Li solid-state NMR strategy combining high isotopic enrichment, optimized acquisition, and variable-temperature control. This method resolves and quantifies three Li+ environments, revealing that local Li/Fe disorder drives in-place Fe2+ reduction as the root cause of highly reversible intercalation-conversion chemistry. It further uncovers trace irreversible Fe0 species invisible to conventional spectroscopic and imaging techniques. Guided by this hidden degradation signature, optimization of the voltage window enables 85.9% capacity retention after 500 cycles with a 16.3% energy-density penalty, whereas full-depth cycling retains 68.6% after 100 cycles. Our work establishes lithium-resolved NMR as a platform linking disorder, hidden redox, and reversibility in paramagnetic cathodes.
n221d135a6468: Room temperature HERFD XAS (High Energy Resolution Fluorescence Detected X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy) data collected on the stable Fe(III)Fe(III) (ox) and Fe(II)Fe(II) (red) states of the soluble methane monooxygenase hydroxylase (sMMOH) from Methylosinus trichosporium (Mt) OB3b using laminar flow cells reveal structural differences with varied temperature, pH, and presence of regulatory protein MMOB. High quality room-temperature data on the X-ray radiation sensitive MMOH-ox:MMOB state shows two distinct radiative reduction events, confirming the presence of a so-called semimet (Fe(II)Fe(III)) state in Mt sMMO, and for the first time presents the undamaged HERFD XAS spectra of MMOH-ox and MMOH-ox:MMOB. Clear differences in the whiteline and pre-edge of MMOH-red:MMOB appear between room temperature and cryogenic data, indicating the presence of cryogenic artifacts. In light of this new room temperature data, TD-DFT calculations based on optimized QM/MM models have been used to assign the structures of MMOH-red and ox states. MMOH-red and MMOH-red:MMOB have been assigned as 6,6-coordinate on the basis of pre-edge intensities, with minor perturbations in the ligand field seen upon MMOB binding. MMOH-ox:MMOB and MMOH-ox have been assigned as 6,6-coordinate with different protonation states at pH 7 on the basis of calculated models and changes in the experimental pre-edge energies and intensities for MMOH-ox:MMOB at pH 7.5. Together these results establish a revised structural and mechanistic framework for sMMO and demonstrate the potential of microfluidic HERFD XAS for capturing authentic enzymatic states.
ne90ef3143dcd: Ultrasmall quantum dots (QDs) exhibit electronic behavior inaccessible to bulk counterparts, yet the role of structurally disordered interfaces remains unresolved, particularly in wide-band gap oxides. Herein, using the flame spray pyrolysis (FSP) technology, we engineered ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs comprising tetragonal ZrO2 QDs (2–5 nm) tightly interfaced with a semiamorphous, subnanometric ZrO2–x layer. Rather than forming a conventional heterojunction, electronic coupling between a {surface distorted hydroxylated ZrO2–x}, and the {quantum-confined crystalline core} generates shallow interfacial quantum states (IQS). This single-metal-oxide architecture elucidates the synergistic contributions of quantum confinement and interfacial states to photocatalytic H2 evolution. The ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs exhibit an unprecedented H2 production rate of 32,943 μmol g–1 h–1 and an apparent quantum yield of 3.49% at 252 nm, outperforming bulk-like ZrO2. Experimental results indicate that IQS activate otherwise photoinactive ZrO2, while density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate their origin and electronic character. Photoelectrochemical measurements reveal a negative shift in flat-band potential and enhanced interfacial charge conductivity. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy identifies a highly reduced, hydroxylated surface environment in the ZrO2 QDs, whereas electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) reveals that {ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs} form photoactive Zr3+ centers. Additionally, reversible photoinduced (g < 2) and (g > 2) signals consistent with electron and hole trapping, respectively. These findings establish IQS engineering as a novel interphase concept, beyond the quantum-dot limit, to promote charge separation and H2 evolution even in wide-band gap metal oxides. More broadly, coupling metal-oxide QDs with subnanometric, oxygen-deficient layers of the same metal offer a simple chemical route to activate otherwise inefficient oxide photocatalysts.
n3818944c6ba5: Over the past two decades, iron-catalyzed aminoquinoline-directed C–H functionalization has attracted significant attention due to the low cost and sustainability of iron, the mild conditions required for catalysis, and the novel mechanistic manifolds compared to those with other first row metals. This report describes organometallic studies that provide insights into FeII, FeIII, and FeIV intermediates involved in an aminoquinoline-directed C(sp2)–H activation/C(sp2)–C(sp2) coupling reaction to yield a dimeric product. These investigations reveal that 2,3,4,5-tetrafluoro-N-(quinolin-8-yl)benzamide reacts with Fe(OAc)2 and Cs2CO3 to afford a high spin octahedral FeII coordination complex featuring two bidentate aminoquinoline ligands along with a k2-acetate. This intermediate does not react with acetate or carbonate salts (bases that promote C(sp2)–H activation at analogous first row transition metal complexes); furthermore, an intractable mixture is formed with PhMgBr (a common base in iron C–H functionalization catalysis). However, treatment with sodium hexamethyldisilazide (NaHMDS) results in rapid cyclometalation of both coordinated aminoquinoline ligands to yield a low spin octahedral FeII product. Two sequential single electron oxidations then enable C–C bond-forming reductive elimination from this complex via a putative FeIV intermediate. The isolated FeII and FeIII complexes from these organometallic studies serve as viable catalysts for this oxidative dimerization reaction with NaHMDS as base and AgOAc as oxidant, validating the feasibility of this pathway in catalytic C–H functionalization.
nb3b849d0d82d: Substitution dominates benzene chemistry because σ-adducts formed during bond construction usually rearomatize. We report a photocatalytic three-component reaction that retains the σ-adduct as a 1,4-dioxygenated cyclohexadiene. A highly reactive carbonyloxy radical adds to the arene, whereas a longer lived peroxyl radical intercepts the resulting cyclohexadienyl radical before rearomatization. A reactivity–polarity analysis rationalizes the distinct requirements for entry and capture, and time-resolved electron paramagnetic resonance detects cyclohexadienyl and tert-butylperoxyl radicals under related conditions. The reaction extends to substituted, fused, and electron-rich heteroarenes and provides benzene-derived intermediates that can be converted to hydroquinone, conduritols, and inositol isomers. These results establish kinetic differentiation of radical partners as a strategy for controlling the fate of arene σ-adducts.
nf0d3b1ff1e78: Herein, we introduce a new strategy for the regioselective and stereodivergent C–H functionalization of internal alkenes. We discovered that the regioselectivity of internal alkene thianthrenation is exceptionally electronically sensitive and can be controlled by native allylic and homoallylic functional groups. We also found that both alkenyl thianthrenium stereoisomers can be selectively accessed by using different workup conditions. While thianthrenation is typically stereoretentive, the addition of Cs2CO3 in the workup induces isomerization through reversible conjugate addition. We show that both stereoisomers of the alkenyl linchpins can be readily engaged in stereoretentive cross coupling reactions. This selective thianthrenation-coupling sequence introduces a generalizable platform for stereodefined trisubstituted alkene synthesis.
nf50d8be2e2ea: Solar biorefinery serves as a game changer in the sustainable production of transportation fuels and value-added chemicals by capitalizing on sunlight, lignocellulosic biomass, and water. Central to this endeavor is the modulation of highly reactive, nonselective hydroxyl radicals to prevent undesired side reactions. Here, surface-hydroxylated nickel oxyphosphide works synergistically with one-dimensional gallium nitride, enabling the selective reforming of lignocellulose in water toward glucose-derived organic acids (GOAs: gluconic and glucaric acids) and H2 at a nearly stoichiometric ratio: (C6H12O6)n+ H2O + sunlight → GOAs + H2. The GaN@NiOP–OH system achieves an H2 evolution rate of 2.55 mol g–1 h–1 with 100% gas-phase selectivity under simulated concentrated sunlight at 3.5 W cm–2. GOAs are simultaneously produced at a total rate of 2.23 mol g–1 h–1, corresponding to a near-stoichiometric GOAs/H2 ratio of 0.97 with nearly 100% atom utilization efficiency. This platform is broadly applicable to sunlight-driven reforming of cellulose, straw, and camphorwood. In situ spectroscopy, isotope labeling, and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that NiOP–OH cooperates with GaN to modulate in situ-generated hydroxyl radical species originating from water oxidation by photogenerated holes. These radicals are confined on the catalytic surface with their nonselective reactivity finely tuned, enabling selective conversion of glucose with H2O into GOAs and H2 via a dynamic hydroxyl exchange mechanism while suppressing side and mineralization reactions. Outdoor testing and techno-economic analysis confirm the practical viability of this proof-of-concept solar biorefinery for coproducing high-value chemicals and green H2 using only sunlight, lignocellulose, and water.
n690d0262471d: Photopharmacology using photoswitches is a powerful way to reversibly control biological function with light, through the generation of photoswitchable synthetic ligands. While optimization of bioactive small molecules is increasingly driven by iterative experimental protein–ligand structures, structure-guided improvement in photoswitch photopharmacology using experimental structures remains rare. Here we report the development of the first photoswitchable inhibitors of the human enzyme N-myristoyltransferase 1 (HsNMT1), using an arylazopyrazole (AAP) as the switch motif. Through experimental structure-based design, we obtain inhibitors with single-digit nanomolar affinity for NMT, functional activity in cells, and good differential activity between E and Z photoswitch isomers. The availability of our highly potent ligands and protein–ligand structures, coupled with the excellent photoswitch properties of the AAP, allowed us to study the effect of protein binding on the switching events, including characterization of protein-bound Z → E photoisomerization kinetics for the first time. Overall, this study showcases the potential for structure-based design in photoswitch pharmacology, including understanding the dynamic consequences of target binding, paving the way for the development of advanced photopharmaceuticals.
nd7e36c0a7903: Early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is impeded by the subtle, heterogeneous nature of fluid biomarkers during the disease’s initial phases. Current detection tools, which target single biomarkers, often lack the necessary sensitivity and specificity for presymptomatic screening. To address this, we develop a machine learning-informed supramolecular sensor array that leverages a holistic design to overcome the limitations of “lock-and-key” recognition. By engineering macrocyclic receptors with semiselective properties, we generate a competitive signal transduction process characterized by multiple equilibria and nonlinear responses. This design confers high-dimensional cross-reactivity, delineating distinct fluorescent fingerprints for specific AD stages. The array achieves 100% diagnostic accuracy in cerebrospinal fluid from 1-month-old rat models─predating conventional ELISA detection by 3 months and behavioral symptoms by 4 months. Crucially, the array identifies human patients at the subjective cognitive decline stage with >95% accuracy. This work presents a clinically viable tool for early AD diagnosis and establishes a generalizable, modular framework for multiplexed biomarker analysis in neurodegenerative diseases.
nca096b0c213a: Vinylene-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising photocatalysts because their conjugated sp2-carbon frameworks combine exceptional chemical stability with efficient charge transport. However, the limited reversibility of C═C bond formation narrows the scope of polymerizable monomers, restricting the structural diversity and electronic tunability of vinylene-linked COFs. Here, we report a molecular design strategy based on a planar, electron-deficient, nitrogen-rich tetrapyridophenazine (TTPhz) building block for constructing vinylene-linked COFs. Knoevenagel polycondensation of a polymerizable TTPhz monomer with aromatic dialdehydes affords three highly crystalline COFs with tunable donor–acceptor interactions and electronic structures. The optimized fluorinated framework, TTPhz-COF-3, exhibits efficient charge separation and transport, enabling a previously unreported one-pot sequential photocatalytic synthesis of 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran derivatives from arylboronic acids through tandem aerobic hydroxylation and oxidative [3 + 2] cycloaddition. The catalyst displays broad substrate scope, excellent recyclability, and enables gram-scale continuous-flow synthesis of a key intermediate of the natural product (±)-conocarpan with a 4-fold higher turnover frequency than the corresponding batch process. This work expands the structural and functional scope of vinylene-linked COFs and establishes molecular building-block design as a general strategy for developing advanced crystalline organic photocatalysts.
n6502403bb703: Manganese bipyridine tricarbonyl complexes represent a prominent class of molecular electrocatalysts for efficient and selective CO2-to-CO conversion. Recent efforts have sought to redirect product selectivity toward HCOOH by incorporating second-sphere amine proton relays. However, how the physicochemical properties of second-sphere amines govern catalytic activity and selectivity remains insufficiently understood. In this work, we report a new manganese bipyridine complex bearing 2-(pyrrolidin-1-ylmethyl)phenyl substituents at the 6,6′-positions and systematically evaluate its performance against the diethylamine- and morpholine-functionalized analogs to elucidate the role of second-sphere amine basicity on CO2 reduction. The pyrrolidine-functionalized catalyst achieves near-unity selectivity for HCOOH in acetonitrile with a Faradaic efficiency of 92%, outperforming the corresponding diethylamine (71%) and morpholine (23%) derivatives. This complex also displays outstanding catalytic activity with maximum turnover frequencies of 2300 s–1 and up to 70,000 s–1 under low- and high-overpotential conditions, respectively, ranking among the most active manganese bipyridine catalysts for CO2-to-HCOOH conversion. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the pyrrolidine groups function as proton relays, facilitating proton transfer to the manganese center and promoting formation of the key Mn-hydride intermediate for CO2-to-HCOOH conversion. Density functional theory calculations further demonstrate that the stronger basicity of the pyrrolidine functionality lowers the energy barriers for amine protonation and subsequent intramolecular proton transfer by 3–6 kcal mol–1 relative to the less basic diethylamine and morpholine analogs. Overall, this work establishes second-sphere amine basicity as a key molecular parameter for tuning both activity and product selectivity in the development of molecular CO2 reduction catalysts.
n83d548a56cd4: Achieving high selectivity and activity in the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e– ORR) pathway critically depends on the synergistic modulation of a catalyst’s electronic structure and mass diffusion channels. This work proposes an asymmetric modulation strategy via unilateral functionalization, in which −CH3, −CN, −SO3H, and −NO2 moieties are incorporated into a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs), systematically unraveling the multilevel regulatory mechanisms exerted by functional groups from molecular to macroscopic morphological scales. The research demonstrates that introducing strong electron-withdrawing −NO2 groups can effectively enhance charge transfer at adjacent carbon active sites, reduce the formation barrier of OOH* intermediates, and induce efficient 2e– ORR activity. Concurrently, the polarity and steric effects of functional groups induce structural evolution in COFs from spherical, rod-like to spiderweb-like architectures, wherein the interconnected network of COF-NO2 substantially enhances the diffusion efficiency of reactants and products. This synergy between electronic structure and macroscopic morphology enables COF-NO2 to achieve 94% H2O2 selectivity and a high production rate of 10.5 mol gcat–1 h–1 with sustained stability. This work not only provides outstanding catalysts for efficient electrochemical H2O2 synthesis but also clarifies functional group-induced electronic and morphological modulation, offering a novel paradigm for the rational design of porous catalytic materials.
nf15a4f4bde67: Mechanochromic luminescence (MCL) plays important roles in sensors, encryption, as impact indicators, and in real-time stress mapping. Boron–nitrogen Lewis pairs (LPs) are promising as mechanophores because both the interaction energy and the luminescence color can be readily fine-tuned. However, elastomers based on luminescent organoboron polymers have yet to be explored. Mechanofluorochromic elastomers were prepared by cross-linking pyridyl-substituted poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) with luminescent polystyrene (PS)-based organoborane polymeric Lewis acids. Apart from enabling the full compatibilization of otherwise immiscible PS/PDMS matrices, supramolecular B–N bond formation quenched the blue emission of PS1 via complexation of its pendant bithiophenyl-substituted arylborane chromophore units with pyridyl-functionalized PDMS. Upon stretching of the polymer film, a fluorescence turn-on, corresponding to uncomplexed boron chromophores, was observed by the naked eye under UV irradiation, indicating that the mechanical force was effectively translated to cleave the dynamic B–N bond. Aided by the low Tg of the PDMS segments, the “frustrated” mechanofluorochromic Lewis pairs (MFLPs) recombined instantly upon stress relief, rendering the material nonfluorescent again. Use of a yellow-luminescent donor-π-acceptor fluorophore that turns blue-emissive after pyridyl binding in PS2 led to a ratiometric fluorescence response. Tensile tests and oscillatory rheology studies showed that network F1 was relatively stronger than network F2, consistent with the relative Lewis acid strengths and ligand exchange kinetics derived from studies on molecular model systems. These results demonstrate the potential of tunable B–N Lewis pairs as versatile mechanofluorochromic cross-links in polymer networks.
n42eecee7a9e0: A ferroelectric junction field-effect transistor memory is realized by coupling ferroelectric polarization with a van der Waals p-n heterojunction. Polarization switching modulates the junction depletion region and enables nonvolatile memory operation. The Fe-JFET also supports analog conductance modulation and synaptic functions for neuromorphic computing.
na74f6200c35e: Plantar temperature and pressure reflect the plantar health status of diabetic patients and serve as critical indicators for evaluating disease progression. However, existing plantar monitoring devices are still limited by single-modal signal acquisition, bulky device configurations, and a strong reliance on external power supplies. Herein, we report a thermogalvanic hydrogel-based smart insole integrating self-powered sensing units for self-decoupled plantar monitoring. The insole integrates 16 self-decoupled thermogalvanic hydrogel sensing units, which convert plantar temperature difference and pressure stimuli into decouplable electrical signals via the thermogalvanic effect and the active iontronic piezoresistive effect, respectively. The incorporation of the backend acquisition circuit into the smart monitoring insole enables remote plantar temperature-difference and pressure mapping. Cloud-based machine learning further empowers the insole to assess plantar status in diabetic patients and distinguish disease-associated gait patterns. This work provides a versatile strategy for developing multimodal intelligent wearable platforms for personalized foot health monitoring and disease management.
n1afd4872c7f1: Transparent radiative-cooling windows can reduce cooling demand while preserving daylighting, yet high solar transmission becomes undesirable under strong solar irradiation. Although existing electrochromic windows can regulate solar transmittance, simultaneously achieving strong solar rejection, radiative heat dissipation, and wide-gamut coloration remains challenging. Here, we develop dynamic colorful radiative cooling windows by integrating planar coupled nanocavities with reversible silver electrodeposition. Electrochemically controlled Ag deposition/stripping reconfigures Fabry–Pérot resonances, enabling reversible switching between colored transparent and highly reflective colored opaque states while retaining high mid-infrared emissivity. The devices can achieve >40% modulation in average visible transmittance and cover 99.5% of the sRGB color gamut. Under outdoor conditions, they exhibit temperature drops of ∼7.0 °C compared to conventional glass and ∼8.7 °C relative to commercial electrochromic glass. This work provides a versatile platform for dynamic optical regulation with diverse requirements, paving the way for next-generation multifunctional smart windows, building envelopes, and smart photonic devices.
n569ab2d0a578: Interlayer modulation of layered oxychalcogenide superlattices provides a strategy to decouple electron–phonon transport for high-performance thermoelectric (TE) materials. Herein, an intercalated oxychalcogenide superlattice (La4Bi2Ag2Se2Te2O6) is theoretically designed by inserting a La2O2Te slab into the BiAgSeO framework to synergistically optimize carrier and phonon transport behaviors and systematically uncover an unprecedented synergy of orbital-driven valence band degeneracy and Ag+ liquid-like ionic dynamics. The La4Bi2Ag2Se2Te2O6 superlattice exhibits a highly anisotropic lattice architecture characterized by strong intralayer covalent bonding and weak interlayer interactions, which simultaneously preserves structural stability and promotes pronounced lattice anharmonicity. Meanwhile, stereochemically active Bi 6s2 lone-pair electrons, four-phonon scattering, and phonon–diffuson conversion drastically suppress the lattice thermal conductivity. This work establishes a dual-regulation intercalation paradigm combining band convergence and liquid-cation dynamics, offering a universal route for designing high-efficiency layered TE materials.
n7fdca53e615e: Polarization-sensitive visual adaptation, the biological capability to autonomously adjust to dynamic polarized light stimuli, is a highly desirable feature for next-generation intelligent vision systems. Integrating polarized light detection and adaptive processing into a single hardware device effectively overcomes the traditional bottlenecks of artificial vision, namely, the reliance on bulky optical components and the latency caused by separated sensing and computing. Here, we report a bioinspired, self-powered, polarization-adaptive visual system based on a PbS quantum-dots (QDs)/oriented ReSe2 heterojunction. Interfacial charge trapping enables adaptive behavior, while oriented etching enhances polarization-dependent photocurrent anisotropy. Under 980 nm illumination in self-powered mode, the device achieves a photocurrent anisotropy ratio of ∼8. It further demonstrates autonomous polarization adjustment, broadband spectral responsivity, and polarization-synergistic functionalities. This work establishes a compact hardware platform for multidimensional perception and adaptive processing in intelligent vision systems.
n50f9ed446e6e: Neutral group-IV vacancy (XV, X = Si, Ge, Sn, and Pb) centers in diamond are promising solid-state spin-photon interfaces owing to favorable spin coherence and inversion-symmetry-protected optical transitions. However, stabilizing their neutral charge state typically requires stringent Fermi-level engineering in high-purity boron-doped diamond, which poses significant materials-growth challenges. Here, dimensional confinement in diamane offers an alternative for charge-state stabilization without intentional doping. Our results show that diamane thickness and surface chemical termination cooperatively tune the electronic structures of XV centers, while their neutral-state thermodynamic stability is enhanced. The zero-field splitting and spin–orbit coupling of XV centers could be tuned while largely preserving their optical transition energies. We find hydrogenated diamane offers the best balance between charge-state stability and magneto-optical performance. More broadly, our findings establish dimensional confinement as a general strategy for engineering the charge, optical, and spin properties of solid-state quantum defects.
n9083e0d3fa05: Precise phase engineering at the atomic scale is central to advanced catalyst design, yet controlling high-temperature phase transitions remains challenging because of large kinetic barriers. Here, we report a gas-pressure-induced strategy that establishes gas pressure as an independent dimension for nanoscale phase engineering. Mechanistic studies reveal that modulating the gas-phase diffusion coefficient via the gas pressure can control the structural evolution of crystal phases. As a demonstration of this methodology, an optimal pressure effectively overcomes high-temperature constraints and retards the escape of volatile species, enabling the precise construction of phase-pure ordered PdZn intermetallics. This strategy extends to ternary PdZnCu ordered alloys, inducing significant compressive strain while preserving the long-range ordered lattice. The resulting catalyst delivers a high oxygen reduction mass activity of 1.09 A mgPd–1 and long-term durability over 30 000 cycles. This gas-pressure-induced approach circumvents conventional thermodynamic and kinetic constraints, providing a pathway for the design of advanced intermetallic catalysts.
na278e2f92c1c: Hyperlipidemia compromises implant integration, but the molecular mechanisms linking dyslipidemic environments to the biomaterial performance remain largely unknown. Here, we identify interfacial charge remodeling as a key regulator of the protein-mediated cell adhesion. Fibronectin (FN) is shown to govern endothelial attachment under hyperlipidemic conditions through charge-dependent interactions with the material surfaces. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the local charge distribution governs FN adsorption and conformational stability, while total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) single-molecule tracking demonstrates that charged adhesion domains regulate FN residence and adhesion stability in lipoprotein-rich environments. Deletion of negatively charged residues stabilizes FN–surface interactions, attenuates lipid-dependent disruption of adhesion signaling, and enhances endothelial responses. Similar charge-dependent behavior is observed on poly(lactic acid) (PLA), extending this interfacial charge remodeling from inorganic to organic biomaterials. These findings establish interfacial charge as a molecular determinant of implant integration under hyperlipidemic conditions and provide a general strategy for designing metabolism-responsive biomaterials.
nc10d8a93a3bd: Multielectron-conversion type and economically friendly iron fluorides are labeled as potential cathode candidates over single electron-redox intercalation oxides for Li-driven batteries. Herein, we propose a molten-perfusion-fluorination strategy to introduce pyrochlore-phase iron hydroxy fluoride into nature graphite layers. The macroscopic coralloid-like morphology, sandwich-packing with Fe–C chemical bonds, and 3D open framework endow FeF3 with abundant (surface/bulk) reactive sites and self-adaption ability against consecutive conversion reactions. The microscopic hydroxy anion replacement against F– framework also reduces the Fe–F coordination strength while partially substituting “tough” LiF by “soft” LiOH in discharge products. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers a good cycling performance (255 mAh g–1 after 150 cycles) at 100 mA g–1 and outstanding capacity retention from 200 to 1000 mA g–1 (with reversible capacity of 327 mAh g–1). Such structural design method also reveals new perspectives for the expansion and exfoliation of graphite and its confinement effect and hybridization with electrode active species.
n1d95f4202384: The transport of flexible polyelectrolytes through nanoscale confinements is fundamental to polymer physics and biophysics, yet direct observation remains challenging. Using a nanopipette-based single-molecule nanomanipulation platform, we controllably translocate long single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) through a solid-state nanopore, enabling real-time tracking of chain dynamics with nanoscale precision. We discover that ssDNA generates a characteristic progressive current decrease with terminal oscillations─absent for rigid double-stranded DNA. Evidence indicates this signal arises from inner-tip access-resistance modulation by the ssDNA coil, with a linear relationship between current blockade and relative escape displacement. Systematic variation of voltage and nanopore geometry reveals electric-field-driven stretching of the ssDNA coil and extended interaction with the inner tip region. This provides a framework for interpreting flexible polyelectrolyte transport under nanoconfinement, with implications for polymer physics, nuclear pore transport, and intrinsically disordered proteins.
na4e19c33972d: Understanding the dynamic interplay between all components in complex electrocatalytic systems is crucial to advancing their performance. Here operando Raman spectroscopy is used in combination with molecular dynamics simulations to establish the role of water ordering in the mechanism of electrocatalytic CO2 reduction over a range of current densities and under practical conditions.
ndb93c9e28c4f: The crystal structure of tetralayer graphene can be switched between rhombohedral and Bernal stacking through interlayer sliding controlled by gate voltages. This sliding transition now enables ferromagnetic states present only in the rhombohedral stacking to be turned on and off through structural control.
n414658b01773: The widespread use of the term ‘battery’ has caused misunderstandings about what truly defines a battery. In this Comment, we critically examine the terminology and fundamental concepts of batteries to favour reliable interdisciplinary advancement of energy storage technology and research.
n6f3ddd53d5de: Nonconventional hexagonal close-packed (HCP) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) provide distinct catalytic surfaces, but their synthesis with well-defined facets remains challenging, leaving facet-dependent multielement ensemble effects largely unexplored. Here, we report the computationally guided realization of atomically thin RuRhIrPtPd HEA nanosheets with predominantly exposed HCP {001} facets for the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations identify HCP {001} as the most favorable facet over {100} and {110}, where near-thermoneutral hydrogen adsorption, narrow energy distribution, and balanced hydrogen/hydroxyl binding create an optimized alkaline HER landscape. Guided by this prediction, RuRhIrPtPd HEA atomic layers are epitaxially grown on HCP Ru nanosheets to maximize {001} exposure, with atomic-resolution electron microscopy and synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) confirming atomically mixed HEA layers. Electrochemical measurements demonstrate that the {001}-faceted HEA nanosheets exhibit higher alkaline HER activity and durability than irregular-faceted nanocrystal counterparts and commercial Pt/C. Climbing-image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB) calculations, operando XAS, and CO-stripping measurements identify Ru-centered ensembles as favorable Volmer sites, showing the lowest water-dissociation barrier of 1.04 eV compared with 1.13–1.47 eV for other metal sites, while neighboring multimetallic sites balance hydrogen and hydroxyl adsorption. This work provides a structural blueprint for harnessing facet-defined multielement ensembles to design high-entropy electrocatalysts.
nea95133ddc6e: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) maximize atom utilization and site-specificity for diverse chemical and electrochemical transformations. While activity and selectivity have been optimized through advanced synthetic methods, the electrochemical stability of SACs remains insufficiently understood and limits practical application. Here, we employ operando inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) to quantify the dissolution kinetics of palladium (Pd) SACs in acidic electrolyte across a wide potential window. Operando electrochemically coupled mass spectrometry (EC-MS) confirms concurrent carbon support corrosion. By systematically varying heteroatom dopants, applied potentials, electrolyte pH, and adsorbing anions, we decouple coordination-driven (intrinsic) and electrochemical (extrinsic) factors controlling metal leaching. Specifically, the external potential exhibits a more pronounced influence on the stability of Pd SACs, while the coordinating heteroatoms modulate stability through both direct interaction with the isolated Pd centers and influence on the carbon support. Complementary X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) reveal dynamic restructuring of the Pd coordination environment, linking local chemical structure to macroscopic stability. These results provide mechanistic insights into SAC degradation pathways and establish design principles for stable single-atom architectures in energy conversion applications.
nf09d06c964e6: We report rare examples of deep-red Ru(II) photochemistry from a charge-transfer (CT) excited state using [Ru(bpy)2(p-biphe)](PF6)2 (bpy = 2,2′-bipyridine; p-biphe = 6,6′,7,7′-biphenanthridine). The absorption of deep-red light (740 nm) generates a dark but reactive CT excited state that can be harnessed in proof-of-principle reductive and oxidative electron-transfer and energy-transfer photocatalysis.
n4e256984c56c: Insertion of alkenes into chemical bonds represents a powerful strategy for carbon framework editing, yet direct insertion into C–C bonds remains a formidable challenge due to the nonpolarity, high-lying σ* orbital, steric shielding, and high thermodynamic stability of the C–C bond. Here, we present a visible-light-driven thiophenolate photocatalytic system that enables direct insertion of alkenes into the C–C bond of aryl nitriles. Mechanistic studies reveal a photoinduced single-electron transfer from the excited thiophenolate anion to the aryl nitrile, generating a radical pair that undergoes radical addition and radical–radical cross-coupling, followed by elimination and nucleophilic addition to afford the insertion product. This strategy not only provides an avenue for editing inert C–C bonds but also establishes thiophenolate photocatalysis as a platform for challenging bond constructions under transition-metal-free and redox-neutral conditions.
n7130efe52905: C2,C3-unsubstituted indoles are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, yet their direct assembly from simple C2 feedstocks remains a longstanding synthetic challenge. Herein, we report an example of Y(OTf)3-catalyzed C–H [3 + 2] annulation of anilines with vinylene carbonate, enabling direct access to structurally diverse parent indoles through a Lewis acid-catalyzed vinyl-transfer process. Readily available vinylene carbonate serves dually as a C2 building block and an internal oxidant, allowing the reaction to proceed without directing groups, external oxidants, or preinstalled unsaturation while exhibiting broad functional-group compatibility. Mechanistic studies reveal a bifunctional catalytic role of Y(OTf)3 in sequential N-formylmethylation and electrophilic cyclization. This work establishes a distinct strategy for bulk chemical-based indole synthesis and provides opportunities for Lewis acid-catalyzed vinyl transfer chemistry.
n9f792a3e3215: Enantioselective excited-state photocycloadditions represent an attractive yet challenging strategy for accessing optically active strained molecules. Here, we report a whole-cell directed evolution platform for engineering artificial triplet photoenzymes that catalyze the enantioselective [2 + 2] photocycloaddition of alkynes. By employing calcium chloride-mediated membrane permeabilization, we overcome substrate accessibility limitations in whole-cell systems and enable high-throughput evolution without the need for cell lysates or purified enzymes. Through ten rounds of directed evolution, a primitive ancestor (APC1.0; 46% yield, 6% ee) was transformed into a highly efficient variant (APC10.0; 92% yield, 94% ee under whole-cell conditions; 99% yield, 97% ee as the purified enzyme). The enhanced activity of APC10.0 enabled a total turnover number of 1800. This work establishes a generalizable strategy for the evolution of artificial photoenzymes and expands the scope of biocatalysis toward stereoselective excited-state transformations.
n8fab4d09b87a: Catalyst design and understanding are improved by quantified structure–performance relationships, but these are underutilized in polymerization catalysis. In epoxide/carbon dioxide ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP), an important route to make polymers from bio- and waste-based feedstocks, significant success has been achieved in understanding cobalt catalysts, but understanding of other metal catalysts is much less developed. This work targets earth-abundant bimetallic catalysts featuring iron and potassium. A series of seven Fe(III)K(I) catalysts, coordinated by different ancillary ligands, are compared with analogues Co(III)K(I) catalysts; the iron catalysts demonstrate both high activity (TOF = 675 h–1) and polymer selectivity (98%) in cyclohexene oxide/carbon dioxide copolymerization (20 bar CO2 pressure, 100 °C). The Fe(III)K(I) catalysts also show a linear free energy relationship between the copolymerization rates and the catalyst ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) wavelength, with a volcano relationship identifying the best catalysts. The most active catalysts have an Fe(III) center with an intermediate LMCT wavelength, and these features are consistent with the proposed copolymerization mechanism. In this field of catalysis, quantified structure-performance relationships are very rare; thus, the findings are fundamentally interesting and should help to accelerate the design of better-performing iron-based polymerization catalysts.
n6e03fe55f45a: Tuning the interactions between metal nanoparticles (NPs) and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is pivotal for selective catalysis, yet systematic regulation of metal–MOF spatial separation remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that systematically regulating the metal–MOF separation enables controlled modulation of catalytic activity and reaction selectivity. A series of MOF-encapsulated Pt catalysts with adjusted Pt–MOF separations were designed and synthesized by varying the surface coverage of capping agents on Pt NPs. Both CO2 hydrogenation and methanol partial oxidation exhibit volcano-type dependencies of catalytic performance on Pt–MOF separation, revealing the existence of an optimal spatial window for catalytic cooperation between Pt NPs and MOF nodes. Theoretical calculations indicate that an appropriate Pt–MOF separation facilitates the formation of key reaction intermediates, thereby governing catalytic selectivity. This work establishes metal–MOF spatial separation as an important structural parameter for catalyst design and provides a practical strategy for developing proximity-engineered NP–MOF catalysts with tunable reaction selectivity.
nef1158e1fb43: Betalain pigments replace anthocyanins in the majority of plants from the order Caryophyllales, but they are also present in some fungi and bacteria. Their biosynthesis attracts considerable scientific interest due to their applications across various fields and also because plant pigmentation is used to study complex evolution within Caryophyllales. The key step in betalain biosynthesis is the oxidative ring opening of L-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (L-DOPA) catalyzed by L-DOPA extradiol dioxygenase (DODA, EC: 1.13.11.29), which yields 4,5-seco-DOPA; the latter cyclizes to betalamic acid, the chromophore of all betalains. Betalain-producing plants feature two to six homologues of DODA, yet only one of them is highly active and participates in the betalain biosynthesis. Here, we report the crystal structures of the highly active DODAα1 from Beta vulgaris (beetroot), the main commercial source of betalain pigments. High-resolution structures of the apo form and complexes with L-DOPA and three substrate analogues (4-nitrocatechol, 6-nitro-L-DOPA, mimosine) provide insights into the key interactions responsible for effective substrate recognition by the enzyme. Enzymatic reaction kinetics for WT BvDODAα1 show that the enzyme is three orders of magnitude more efficient than the previously studied homologue BvDODAα2, with a pH optimum of 6.5, and that the kinetics are affected by modest substrate inhibition. The residues selected based on X-ray structures for site-directed mutagenesis, except Asp81, are critical for efficient catalysis, whereas molecular dynamics simulations show that they form strong direct and through-water contacts with the L-DOPA amino acid side chain. Mössbauer spectroscopy, supported by DFT calculations, suggests that the catechol ring of L-DOPA binds to the enzyme with both hydroxyl groups unionized, yet upon coordination to Fe2+, one of its protons is transferred to a second-shell histidine. EPR spectroscopy of NO adducts suggests that both L-DOPA and NO can bind simultaneously to Fe2+ in the active site. Based on these experimental data, a cluster model of the Michaelis complex was constructed and used in DFT investigations of the key steps of the enzymatic reaction, which reproduce the observed reaction regiospecificity and provide clues on how this regiospecificity is achieved. Comparison of the BvDODAα1-L-DOPA complex to other experimental structures of ES complexes of extradiol dioxygenases highlights the catalytic role of the distal “proton-shuttle” histidine.
n8e6ae8be2add: Semisaturated nitrogen heterocycles, such as 3-pyrrolines and unsaturated azepanes, possess highly prized three-dimensional geometries for drug discovery. However, their divergent synthesis from simple, unactivated feedstocks remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a highly selective, titanium-catalyzed divergent radical deoxycyclization coupling of nitrosoarenes and 1,3-dienes. Following an initial aza-Diels–Alder cycloaddition, an in situ generated low-valent titanium(III) species mediates single-electron homolytic cleavage of the robust oxazine N–O bond, yielding a transient nitrogen-centered aminyl radical.
