By rationally tuning the solvent coordination sphere and chlorosilane dissociation kinetics, this radical’s trajectory is selectively directed down two orthogonal pathways: a 5-exo-tet cyclization to afford 3-pyrrolines (formal [4 + 1]) and a highly strained vinylaziridine-mediated aza-Claisen rearrangement to yield unsaturated azepanes (formal [4 + 3]). This radical-polar crossover protocol features broad functional group tolerance and enables a streamlined, cyanide-free synthesis of the antiarrhythmic drug candidate SU-13197. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including EPR spin-trapping, support the crucial aminyl radical intermediacy and the important role of titanium coordination in orchestrating cascade divergence.
nede2bbadd508: Piezocatalytic H2O2 production, employing water and oxygen as the raw materials, is emerging as a promising and viable alternative for in situ H2O2 evolution. However, the understanding of the structure–activity relationship of piezocatalysts still poses challenges, and the key factor steering the H2O2 evolution pathway also remains ambiguous. Herein, two bismuth ferrite-based materials with different crystal structures, perovskite-type BiFeO3 and mullite-type Bi2Fe4O9, were prepared for a systematic comparison of their piezocatalytic activity and an in-depth investigation into the routes of H2O2 in situ production. As a result, BiFeO3 achieved a higher H2O2 production rate (252.86 μmol·L–1) than Bi2Fe4O9 (140.32 μmol·L–1) over 60 min in ambient aqueous conditions without any sacrificial agent. Mechanism analysis reveals that a higher piezocatalytic H2O2 yield of BiFeO3 arises from its stronger piezoelectric response and surface coordination mode of bridging hydroxyl groups. The piezoelectric-induced band bending made water oxidation thermodynamically feasible, and the bridging hydroxyl groups offered hole-transfer channels, thereby collectively triggering the simultaneous occurrence of oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and water oxidation reaction (WOR). This work provides fundamental insights into the crystal-structure-dependent piezocatalytic activity, offering a profound understanding of the mechanism underlying H2O2 evolution routes.
nf25093d305d3: The CRISPR-associated endonuclease Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9 (SpCas9) facilitates site-specific DNA cleavage, with structural transition from the checkpoint state to the catalytic conformation representing a critical activation step. This transition involves an approximately 38 Å displacement of the HNH domain catalytic residue H840 toward the target DNA. However, the molecular determinants governing this large-scale rearrangement of the HNH domain during checkpoint activation, and the conformational routes by which HNH repositioning may occur, remain incompletely understood. To address this knowledge gap, we combined nudged elastic band-guided sampling with unbiased molecular dynamics simulations, reaching a cumulative timescale of 160 μs, and constructed a kinetic model describing HNH domain dynamics during checkpoint activation with Markov state modeling. The mechanistic features suggested by these simulations were further evaluated through biochemical DNA cleavage assays and an intracellular fluorescence reporter system. Our results identify conformational plasticity of the L2 linker and coupled motion of the REC2 domain as key regulatory elements of the HNH domain relocation during SpCas9 checkpoint activation. The model suggests that L2 linker remodels toward a disassembled state to enable release and repositioning of the HNH domain, while the REC2 domain outward displacement guides HNH domain relocation through transient interactions that stabilize activation-associated intermediates. Site-directed mutagenesis of key residues in the L2 linker and REC2 domain significantly reduced DNA cleavage efficiency in both biochemical and cellular assays, supporting their functional importance in SpCas9 activation. Taken together, this study provides an experimentally grounded mechanistic framework for understanding how linker dynamics and REC2 domain coupling regulate HNH domain checkpoint activation, and offers insights for rational engineering of SpCas9 variants with altered activity and specificity.
na1cf152b01fc: The electrochemical carbon monoxide oxidation reaction (COOR) is an attractive anodic alternative to the oxygen evolution reaction, offering a route to lower the energy demand of electrosynthesis while utilizing abundant industrial waste gas. However, COOR has rarely been implemented in practical paired electrolysis systems because of modest device-level performance, reliance on purified CO feedstocks, and operational instability. Here, we establish a COOR∥two-electron oxygen reduction reaction paired electrolysis platform for H2O2 and CO32– coproduction using simulated CO-rich steelmaking flue gas. The system sustains bias-free operation for >140 h. Under high-current-density operation, in situ surface analysis revealed that interfacial carbonate accumulation causes anodic passivation and current decay. Pulsed electrolysis was introduced to alleviate such carbonate buildup and stabilized operation at 100 mA cm–2. Techno-economic analysis estimated an H2O2 minimum selling price of $0.71 kg–1. Together, these results establish COOR as a practical strategy for energy-efficient electrosynthesis using industrial waste gas.
na2ef69e2788a: Integrating dry carbon electrodes (CEs) into inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) offers a solvent-free, scalable route to low-cost photovoltaics. However, mechanical stress during lamination and the large work-function mismatch between the CE and the electron transport layer (ETL) can compromise performance. Here, we report an interface engineering strategy utilizing a silver-2-mercaptobenzothiazole (Ag-MBT) metal-polymer buffer layer to enable high-efficiency inverted CE-based PSCs (C-PSCs). XPS reveals Ag-induced changes in the sulfur and nitrogen chemical environments of MBT, consistent with the formation of an Ag-MBT interfacial coordination layer involving Ag–S coordination. This coordination-derived interlayer serves a dual function: it acts as a structural buffer, enabling damage-free dry CE lamination, and it establishes an energetic band alignment that bridges the ETL/CE work-function gap. Consequently, our devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.12% and maintain their initial efficiency after 1000 h of dark N2 storage, establishing metal-polymer interfacial coordination as a viable pathway for robust inverted C-PSCs.
nc8d8f7d0533e: Two-dimensional/three-dimensional (2D/3D) mixed tin halide perovskites are promising lead-free photovoltaic absorbers, but uncontrolled crystallization produces excessive low-n phases that impede charge extraction due to a quantum confinement effect. Here, we employ 1,4-benzenediammonium iodide (1,4-BDI2) as a multifunctional additive to regulate crystallization, phase distribution, and defects. The additive modulates precursor colloid assembly and retards low-dimensional crystal growth, yielding dense films dominated by highly oriented three-dimensional perovskites with suppressed n = 1 and reduced n = 2 phases. Meanwhile, 1,4-BD2+ cations and unincorporated organic ligands accumulate at grain boundaries to form a passivating complex that passivates deep-trap states and forms favorable interfacial energy-level alignment to promote charge transfer. Consequently, inverted tin perovskite solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 15.94% and an open-circuit voltage of 0.91 V, together with improved operational and storage stability. This work establishes an integrated molecular strategy for phase regulation and defect passivation in efficient lead-free photovoltaics.
na45074767b75: Ruthenium oxides have been the model catalyst for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction. It has been a challenge to achieve both stability and activity and establish a comprehensive descriptor for Ru-based catalysts. Herein, guided by the ligand field theory, we introduce the Ru orbital splitting energy (ΔRu) as a quantitative parameter to describe the interaction between Ru 4d and O 2p orbitals to govern the overall catalytic performance. A series of two-dimensional (2D) multielement metal oxides are synthesized via a self-assembly method to modulate ΔRu. The optimized RuCoFeNiO catalyst for water oxidation delivers a current density of 10 mA cm–2 at a low overpotential of 180 mV and shows high activity for more than 2500 h at 1 A cm–2 in acidic condition. In situ measurements and theoretical analysis reveal that the surface hydrogen-bond network balances the amount of surficial two-hydrogen-bonded water and free water, boosting the proton-transfer process. Moreover, the optimized ΔRu (2.405 eV) modifies the adsorption of *OOH on Ru sites, switching the dominant reaction pathway from the lattice oxygen mediated mechanism to absorbate evolution mechanism. This work highlights the pivotal role of ΔRu in tailoring both stability and activity and may offer insights into high-entropy 2D Ru-based oxides as high-performance oxygen evolution electrocatalysts.
ncf864f0943e5: Na2CO3 is a promising sacrificial presodiation agent owing to its high capacity, excellent air stability, and low cost. However, its practical application is severely hampered by a high decomposition overpotential (>4.3 V vs Na/Na+), inducing detrimental electrolyte oxidation and cell degradation. To break this high-voltage limit, we propose an in situ interfacial dual-modification strategy, synergistically introducing interfacial oxygen vacancies and triggering electronic reconstruction, which thermodynamically lowers the reaction Gibbs free energy and kinetically diminishes the activation barriers, resulting in a dramatically reduced decomposition potential by 350 mV. Operando three-electrode diagnostics within a full sodium-ion capacitor reveal that this interface engineering not only facilitates efficient Na+ release (496.9 mAh g–1) at lower potential but also reduces the actual working potential of cathode, thereby fundamentally avoiding high-voltage parasitic reactions, according well with the DEMS and TOF-SIMS results. Consequently, the full cell achieves a considerable 117.4% enhancement in energy density. Most importantly, this strategy demonstrates compelling practicality in ampere-hour-level devices, delivering a substantial 22.4% boost in energy density with only 3 wt % additive in 1.5 Ah pouch cells. This work bridges microscopic interfacial chemistry and macroscopic device performance, providing a scalable and efficient blueprint for low-potential presodiation toward high-energy-density sodium-ion devices.
n24d94df5e986: Selective detection of trace (weakly reducing) dimethyl sulfide (DMS) in highly humid exhaled breath using metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) sensors, with the presence of strong reducing H2S interference gas, is essential for the early diagnosis of hepatic diseases. However, it remains a big challenge in principle. Herein, a bilayer MOS sensor with a Pd–WO3 sensing film and a CuO/Al2O3 filtering overlayer was proposed. The temperature-dependent H2S catalytic oxidation experiment suggests that CuO could effectively filter H2S even under room temperature. Dispersing the CuO particles into insulative Al2O3 carrier could not only selectively remove H2S without significant consumption of DMS but also isolate the underlying Pd–WO3 sensing layer’s response signal from interference caused by that of CuO. By adding the CuO/Al2O3 1:9 filtering overlayer, the response ratio of DMS to H2S was significantly enhanced from 3.3 to 50.4, furthermore, an ultrahigh response (701.3) to 10 ppm DMS, and a low limit of detection of 10 ppb under 90% RH were achieved, which promises the future breath disease diagnosis.
nde1c87ded69e: The recent discovery of superionic conductivity in doped polyzwitterions (PZIs) has opened a new direction for polymer electrolytes (PEs). Solid-state battery research is currently dominated by inorganic electrolytes due to their rigidity and high conductivity, but they suffer from poor electrode adhesion and processability issues. While PEs overcome these issues, they typically suffer from low ionic conductivity. Recently, salt-doped PZIs have emerged as promising candidates, where high concentrations of ionic species and local dipolar interactions can reduce energy barriers for ion transport and therefore increase room-temperature ionic conductivity. Here, we demonstrate that superionic conductivity is not a universal behavior of doped PZIs, but rather a strategic design of ion-transport pathways is required. Using a flexible polysiloxane-based PZI doped with LiTFSI salt, we observe that room-temperature conductivity remains limited (∼10–8 S/cm at 293 K) despite a relatively low glass transition temperature and high dielectric constant. X-ray scattering reveals the structural origin of this behavior; namely, zwitterionic groups aggregate into isolated nanodomains separated by the polymer matrix, which slows down ion mobility. Once these clusters start overlapping, doped PZI showed significant enhancement in conductivity. These results demonstrate the critical role of percolating ion channels for superionic conductivity in PZIs.
n13f36e485d76: A consensus established by extensive thermodynamic and structural studies of proteins and DNA is that water acts as an indispensable structural cofactor rather than a passive solvent for biomolecules. Nevertheless, it remains unclear whether trace water still exerts a stabilizing effect on proteins under ultradry conditions. Nonpolar organic solvents that spontaneously absorbed trace water provide an ideal platform to investigate this issue. Herein, atomic force microscopy (AFM)-based single-molecule force spectroscopy (SMFS) was employed to investigate the mechanical behaviors of two model polyproteins, (GB1)8 and (I27)8, in nonpolar organic solvents with varying water contents. It was found that even at the ppm level, water protects protein stability and acts as a molecular switch: polyproteins fully denature at water contents ≤80 ppm (nonane and tetradecane), while metastable folded fragments can be retained at water contents ≥95 ppm (tetrachloroethane (TCE) and octane) with a characteristic unfolding force of approximately 100 pN. Force-free molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of a smaller (I27)2 model in TCE further suggested that trace water accumulated preferentially around the protein, reorganizing the local solvation environment, thereby serving as a stabilizer. Based on the SMFS results, the water-content range of 80–95 ppm was identified as a critical threshold, across which polyproteins toggle between fully denatured and partially stabilized states. This work reveals the protective effect of trace water on proteins, quantifies its stabilizing capacity down to the ppm level, and offers insights for protein storage and astrobiology research.
n6e24101de9bf: The rapid growth of data-intensive applications demands efficient data processing with reduced data movement. Logic-in-memory (LIM) and in-memory search, exemplified by ternary content-addressable memory (TCAM), offer promising solutions; however, their typical implementation in separate device modules leads to increased circuit complexity and limited cell-level functional density. Here, we demonstrate a split-gate van der Waals ferroelectric field-effect transistor (vdW FeFET) as a unified operational cell for multimode reconfigurable logic and ternary in-memory search. The architecture integrates two parallel split gates, employing MoS2 as the channel and ferroelectric CuInP2S6 as the gate dielectric. Polarity-dependent modulation by the split gates and the drain bias enables multimode reconfigurable logic operation, supporting six Boolean functions, including directional data transfer. The same device can be programmed for associative memory equivalent to a one-transistor-per-cell TCAM, where two spatially separated ferroelectric regions are programmed within one continuous MoS2 channel, allowing ternary states to be stored and match and mismatch responses to be encoded directly into the channel current. Device-calibrated statistical simulations confirm ranking-based row discrimination under realistic device variability. By linking reconfigurable logic, spatial ferroelectric programming, and current-domain associative search within a common split-gate device framework, this work presents a compact transistor platform for logic-search-coupled in-memory computing.
n1a00b0eaa8be: Stabilizing electrode/electrolyte interphases is crucial for high-performance lithium–sulfur batteries; however, simultaneously fabricating robust interphases on both the lithium anode and sulfur cathode is challenging. Here, we report an anion-transferring functional electrolyte containing non-expendable tetramethylammonium (TMA) bromide that enables the in situ formation of LiF-rich interphases on both electrodes. The TMA+ cations act as ion carriers that electrostatically shuttle PF6− anions from the bulk electrolyte to the electrode/electrolyte interfaces in the form of ion pairs. This localized enrichment of PF6 − facilitates its electrochemical decomposition, leading to the formation of a uniform LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase on the anode and a cathode-electrolyte interphase on the sulfur cathode. The LiF-rich interphases show a high Young's modulus, which help suppress interfacial parasitic reactions and Li dendrite formation. The adsorbed TMA+ cations form an electrostatic shielding layer that mitigates local Li+ flux heterogeneity, further suppressing dendrite growth. When applied to Li-SPAN batteries, they maintain a 92% capacity retention after 350 cycles at 1 C and deliver a high reversible capacity of 1039 mAh g−1 after 300 cycles at 0.5 C. This work provides an innovative alternative to conventional interphase engineering for stabilizing lithium battery interphases.
nf498d2730026: Relaxor ferroelectrics (RFEs) are promising dielectric materials for pulsed multilayer ceramic capacitors because of their rapid polarization response. However, under practical electric fields, polarization rapidly approaches saturation as polar nanoregions exhaust their nonlinear switching capability, fundamentally limiting energy-storage performance. Here we demonstrate that antiferrodistortive matrix engineering reprograms the polarization evolution pathway through a polarization dormancy–awakening process. Long-range antiferrodistortive modulation, introduced by the intrinsic lattice instability of CaZrO3 in a (Bi0.5Na0.4K0.1)TiO3 matrix, creates local strain fields that temporarily suppress PNR switching and progressively awaken dormant polarization under moderate electric fields. This substantially extends the nonlinear polarization-response regime without inducing ferroelectric or antiferroelectric ordering. Atomic-resolution electron microscopy, electron diffraction, and phase-field simulations collectively reveal the structural origin of the awakening behavior and its coupling to local polarization dynamics. Consequently, the engineered relaxor ceramic achieves an ultrahigh recoverable energy-storage density of 12.3 J cm– 3 with an energy-storage efficiency of 87.4% at 520 kV cm– 1, representing a benchmark performance for bulk RFE ceramics operating under moderate electric fields. This work establishes antiferrodistortive matrix engineering as a promising design strategy for reprogramming polarization evolution in RFEs toward high-performance dielectric energy storage.
nd0bb31c71c72: Accelerating water dissociation while maintaining efficient proton transfer remains a substantial challenge in high‐flux alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here, we introduce an interfacial engineering strategy to develop a high‐flux alkaline HER electrocatalyst with controllable spatially asymmetric interfacial charge gradients, by incorporating size‐tunable Ni nanoparticles at Mo2N/Ni0.2Mo0.8N interfacial regions to create a Ni‐nanoparticle‐bridged dual‐interface heterogeneous structure with coordinated proton‐transfer pathways. The resultant electrocatalyst achieves an industrial current density of 1.0 A cm−2 at 1.74 V in an anion‐exchange membrane electrolyzer, outperforming commercial Pt/C by 10%, while sustaining 100 h intermittent operation under 10–1000 mA cm−2 current cycling, demonstrating robust operational stability under high‐flux conditions. Such high‐flux HER capability can be attributed to the formation of asymmetric charge gradients along the Ni/Mo2N and Ni/Ni0.2Mo0.8N interfaces, which reorient interfacial water molecules into favorable configurations to promote dissociation at apical Ni nanoparticle sites and continuously supply protons. Simultaneously, the generated protons are directed through two coordinated pathways consisting of electrostatically guided surface migration at the negatively polarized Ni/Mo2N interface and hydrogen‐bond‐network‐mediated hopping at the positively polarized Ni/Ni0.2Mo0.8N interface, safeguarding against proton‐transfer bottlenecks and active‐site blockage under high‐flux conditions. This work establishes interfacial charge gradient regulation as a design principle for high‐flux alkaline HER.
nbdde4c32c9ee: Benefiting from the anionic redox activity, lithium‐rich layered oxide cathodes exhibit high specific capacity, but the migration of transition metal (TM) can exacerbate vacancy clustering, resulting in domino‐like structural degradation. To stabilize the structure, the electrostatic pinning effect is precisely incorporated into the Li layer to mitigate the TM migration via strong electrostatic repulsion. Concurrently, this configuration effectively modulates the electronic distribution around the oxygen ligands, thereby stabilizing the oxygen redox. Furthermore, robust electrostatic interactions endow the material with the capability to adaptively adjust its interlayer spacing, thereby buffering the structural evolution of the layered framework during (de)lithiation processes. The modified cathode achieves an 89.1% capacity retention over 400 cycles in half‐cells and an impressive 96.2% over 1000 cycles in full cells. To further decouple the capacity‐stability trade‐off while concurrently enhancing both bulk and interfacial stability, we engineered a gradient shielding architecture. This design not only attains 219.8 mAh g−1 at 0.5C and delivers capacity retention of 90.8% after 400 cycles but also promotes the formation of a compact CEI at the near‐surface region, markedly improving interfacial stability under harsh conditions. This progressive structural engineering paradigm offers fresh insights into overcoming the intrinsic structural challenges of lithium‐rich cathode materials.
ne619581bb49a: Iron‐based redox flow batteries (IRFBs) are compelling candidates for cost‐effective grid‐scale energy storage, benefiting from high safety, low cost, and the natural abundance of iron‐based active species. However, heterogeneous interface instability, side reactions, and kinetic deactivation lead to capacity decay and energy efficiency reduction, which limits the long‐term cycle stability of IRFBs. Chelation compensation is employed to regulate metal‐ion redox species through multidentate ligand design. Their coordination environment, solvation structure, and interfacial reactivity are thereby optimized, leading to improved energy efficiency and cycling stability. This review summarizes the major degradation mechanisms of IRFBs and highlights recent progress in chelation‐modified systems constructed with representative chelating functional groups. Particular attention is given to the influence of chelation on heterogeneous interface instability, side reactions, and reaction kinetics. Finally, current challenges and future directions in ligand design, electrolyte compatibility, mechanistic understanding, and practical implementation are discussed, offering guidance for the development of high‐performance chelation‐modified IRFBs for large‐scale energy storage.
nb2b48167b94e: SnO2 is a benchmark electron transport material for perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, SnO2 films from the conventional chemical bath deposition (CBD) are limited by impurities and defects that accelerate non‐radiative recombination and compromise device stability. Here, we present a volatile additive engineering strategy using pyruvic acid (PA) as a dual‐functional nucleation promoter and surface modulator during SnO2 deposition. Owing to its volatility (sublimation at 145°C), PA can be effectively removed during annealing, resulting in cleaner SnO2 surfaces with reduced residual groups. This is accompanied by a decrease in oxygen‐related defect densities in the SnO2 layer. This improvement leads to enhanced charge recombination and improved thermal stability at the buried interface. Consequently, PA‐engineered PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.17%, together with improved device stability, retaining >80% of their initial efficiency after 900 h of continuous operation, 1000 h at 65°C, and 30 days under 30% relative humidity. Furthermore, this approach is compatible with large‐area fabrication, yielding efficiencies of 24.83% for 1 cm2 lab‐scale cells and 20.21% for 30 cm × 30 cm industrial‐scale solar modules. These results suggest that controlling additive volatility improves CBD‐SnO2 quality and offers a promising route for stable, scalable perovskite solar cells.
n079ef1a29f6c: Neutral hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) faces sluggish kinetics due to strong cation hydration disrupting interfacial hydrogen‐bond (H‐bond) networks, impeding mass transport. Herein, we propose a nucleophilic doping strategy to reconstruct the interfacial water structure and boost neutral HER performance. By engineering a nucleophilic oxygen‐doped molybdenum selenide/molybdenum phosphide hybrid on carbon cloth (Ox‐MoSe2‐x/MoP/CC), we successfully manipulate the local electronic environment to attenuate cation hydration effects. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations coupled with in situ Raman spectroscopy provide compelling evidence that the incorporated nucleophilic O species trigger a reconfiguration of interfacial water, fostering the formation of highly connected H‐bond networks. These optimized networks serve as efficient highways for intermediate transport, significantly lowering the mass transfer resistance. Furthermore, density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal a synergistic mechanism where the MoP phase acts as a potent water dissociation promoter, facilitating the Volmer step. Consequently, the Ox‐MoSe2‐x/MoP/CC electrode delivers a remarkable overpotential of only 34 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in 1 M phosphate buffer solution, surpassing commercial Pt/C, and exhibits superior long‐term stability. This work not only presents a high‐performance electrocatalyst but also highlights the pivotal role of nucleophilic modulation in engineering interfacial H‐bond networks for efficient neutral electrocatalysis.
n1350b95d309b: All-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) with layered oxide cathodes such as LiNi 1-x-y Mn x Co y O2 (NMC), LiNi 1-x-y Co x Al y O2 (NCA), LiNiO2 (LNO), and lithium-rich layered oxides (LLOs) offer superior energy density and safety, yet their performance is severely limited by complex, coupled degradation mechanisms at the cathode/inorganic solid-state electrolyte (SSE) interface and within the cathode bulk. This review establishes a Diagnosis-Mechanism-Mitigation (D-M-M) framework that decodes these multiscale degradation phenomena by cross-validating multimodal diagnostic evidence from electronic structure to the cell level. Two categories are dissected: interfacial degradation, encompassing chemical decomposition, space-charge layer formation, and resistive interphase growth; and bulk cathode degradation, including structural phase transitions, cation disorder, oxygen loss, and microstructural cracking. Drawing on advanced spectroscopy, microscopy, 3D imaging, and in situ/operando methods, each degradation cascade is traced from its diagnostic signature to its mechanism and to the validated mitigation it informed, from interfacial coatings to dopant engineering and microstructure optimization. Machine learning and artificial intelligence are assessed for interpreting complex diagnostic datasets and guiding predictive cathode design. The framework is further extended to practically relevant conditions (thick electrodes, low stack pressure, and large-format cells), and the field's unresolved controversies are delineated together with the experiments that would decide them.
nd32a9e5ca34d: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) feature low cost, superior safety, and eco‐friendliness, promising extensive prospects for next‐generation electrochemical energy storage. Nevertheless, inferior interfacial stability, uncontrollable Zn dendrite formation, and poor temperature tolerance severely hinder their practical exploitation in flexible electronic devices. Herein, glycerol (Gly) and ethylene glycol (EG) are incorporated into a polyacrylamide (PAM) hydrogel matrix via a facile one‐pot route to fabricate a wide‐temperature‐tolerant PAM‐based composite hydrogel electrolyte (PAM/Gly/EG). Benefiting from the synergistic effect of the two diols, the hydroxyl‐rich structure reconstructs the intrinsic hydrogen bond network of confined water, while coordination interactions modulate the solvation configuration of Zn2+, thereby fundamentally restraining Zn dendrite propagation and parasitic hydrogen evolution. The resultant Zn||Zn symmetric cell delivers a long stable lifespan over 3000 h at 1 mA·cm−2, and sustains steady cycling for 500 h at −20°C and 300 h at 50°C. This synergistic diol modification strategy affords a feasible avenue for structural optimization and practical deployment of wide‐temperature flexible AZIBs.
n09d8e4399e02: Developing energy‐efficient and environmentally sustainable refrigeration technologies is critically important for mitigating climate change. Here, we report an electrochemically driven dissolution–crystallization refrigeration cycle (EDCR), a liquid‐state electrochemical cooling concept in which cooling is generated by the endothermic dissolution of electrochemically regenerated redox‐active salts. Unlike conventional electrochemical refrigeration, where the cooling effect arises directly from endothermic redox reactions and is therefore partly offset by Joule heating, EDCR spatially separates electrochemical regeneration from dissolution‐based cooling. The EDCR achieves a maximum temperature drop of 5.65 K and a maximum coefficient of performance of up to 15.51 under ideal condition without heat loss, corresponding to a relative Carnot efficiency of 29.8% at room temperature. This proof‐of‐concept study establishes EDCR as a promising hydrofluorocarbon‐free refrigeration strategy and provides a new route for exploring liquid‐state electrochemical cooling cycle.
nc9c99b47d173: Refrigeration Electrochemically driven dissolution–crystallization refrigeration couples the endothermic dissolution of redox‐active salts with electrochemical regeneration. As depicted on the cover, regenerated crystals dissolve in the foreground cooling reservoir to absorb heat, while the electrolyte circulates through the electrochemical cell for recrystallization and reuse. Spatially separating cooling from electrochemical regeneration minimizes direct interference from Joule heating. More in article number e71304, Pei Liu, Jia Li, Jiangjiang Duan, and co‐workers.
nbab3e4af9218: Elevating depth‐of‐charge (DoC) enhances the energy density of layered oxide cathodes for sodium‐ion batteries; however, such high‐DoC cycling inevitably triggers severe structural and interfacial degradation. In practice, battery management systems commonly adapt voltage‐derating strategies dynamically according to battery state of health, achieving a favorable trade‐off between energy density and cycle life. Nevertheless, a critical yet overlooked question remains: how high‐DoC‐induced damaged regions evolve when reverted to moderate‐DoC cycling. Here, using NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 (NFM111) as a prototype, a voltage‐switching strategy is employed to elucidate the dynamic and long‐term behavior of these damaged regions. During high‐DoC cycling (charging to 4.3 V), the rapid capacity fading is driven by pronounced formation of bulk defects and interfacial disordered spinel phases. However, upon switching these cells to moderate‐DoC cycling (charging to 4.0 V), these pre‐existing damaged regions become stabilized: their rapid propagation is suppressed, and they no longer accelerate degradation in surrounding intact regions. This enables degraded NFM111 to deliver capacity retention comparable to that of cells cycled solely under moderate‐DoC conditions. This work presents a dynamic and evolving picture of high‐DoC degradation and subsequent moderate‐DoC stabilization in NFM111 cathodes, providing mechanistic insights into voltage‐derating process and the lifetime prolongation of compromised cells.
n49556cc0d07b: Anode‐free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs) promise ultrahigh energy density (>350 Wh kg−1) and low cost, yet their operation under low‐temperature and fast‐charging conditions is critically hindered by limited sodium inventory and sluggish interfacial kinetics. This conflict creates a “stability paradox”: the pursuit of high energy density amplifies interfacial instability, leading to inhomogeneous sodium deposition and rapid capacity decay. This review systematically analyzes AFSMB failure mechanisms under extreme conditions and demonstrates that overcoming these bottlenecks requires integrated co‐design across four synergistic domains: (1) engineering electrolyte solvation structures (weakly solvating, high‐concentration, and high‐entropy designs) to lower the desolvation barrier and stabilize the solid–electrolyte interphase; (2) tailoring current collector interfaces with sodiophilic coatings or three‐dimensional architectures to guide uniform sodium deposition; (3) incorporating rational pre‐sodiation strategies to compensate irreversible sodium loss; and (4) leveraging artificial intelligence and molecular simulations for data‐driven electrolyte screening. We critically assess the trade‐offs of each strategy and provide a forward‐looking perspective on reversible sodium compensation, multi‐scale AI platforms, and full‐cell integration. This review offers a roadmap for developing practical, wide‐temperature‐range, high‐energy‐density AFSMBs, with recent pouch cells already demonstrating >200 Wh kg−1 and stable cycling from −40°C to 60°C.
naad96cbe1bef: Developing piezoelectric materials with a high figure-of-merit (FOM = d 33×g 33/tanδ) is crucial for advanced energy-harvesting technologies. Here, a high FOM is achieved in [001]-oriented Pb(Mg1/3Nb2/3)O3-PbZrO3-PbTiO3 (PMN-PZT) textured ceramics by synergistically integrating grain orientation, defect engineering, and morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) design. The textured ceramic exhibits exceptional properties (piezoelectric charge coefficient d 33 = 1120 pC·N−1, piezoelectric voltage coefficient g 33 = 62 × 10−3 V·m·N−1, and an ultralow dielectric loss tanδ = 0.23%). Atomic-scale analysis reveals that the [001] intrinsic anisotropy and mixed rhombohedral-tetragonal domains facilitate polarization rotation to boost d 33 and g 33, while Mn doping-induced defect dipoles suppress dielectric loss. Consequently, an ultrahigh FOM of 30,180 × 10−12 m2·N−1 is realized. Furthermore, a cantilever energy harvester utilizing this textured ceramic delivers an outstanding power density of 0.72 µW·mm−3, which is 78 times higher than that of commercial soft PZT. This work provides an effective strategy for designing high-FOM piezoelectric materials for high performance energy harvesting applications.
nb2e504cf5e59: Particulate photocatalysts have generated interest for the low‐cost implementation of various photocatalytic processes, including the production of solar fuels as clean energy sources. With light absorption, charge generation, charge transport, and interfacial charge transfer all constrained in individual particles, complex photophysical and photochemical processes occur on a wide range of timescales within spatially defined volumes. The allure of deciphering the charge carrier dynamics to build a fundamental picture of photocatalysis in different materials has motivated the development of state‐of‐the‐art spatiotemporal measurement techniques. Monitoring charge carrier dynamics on relevant time and length scales is a challenging experimental task. Many experimental barriers have been overcome in recent years, providing some guidance for future directions for material development. This review delves into the underlying origins of spatial heterogeneity in charge carrier dynamics, introduces charge carrier transport phenomena, and details the recent examples of spatiotemporal investigation of charge carrier dynamics in particulate photocatalysts. These new experimental capabilities pave the way for a more comprehensive description of photocatalytic processes, guiding the optimization of photocatalytic materials.
n37d8304e39b4: Hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) in alkaline media suffers from multiple challenges of sluggish kinetics, CO poisoning, and active-site degradation. Multi-metallic catalysts with multiple active sites hold promise for addressing the issues; however, they are thwarted by structural heterogeneity at the atomic level and reliance on empirical trial-and-error screening. Herein, we introduce a novel functional motif directed decoupling-recoupling strategy for the design of multi-site catalysts capable of super-active and durable HOR electrocatalysis. Leveraging the well-defined atomic coordinates for each element and superlattice ordering structure of the PtM intermetallic compound (IMC), the development of a multi-functional Pt-based HOR catalyst is decoupled into the independent screening of discrete Pt–M functional motifs. These optimally selected Pt–M motifs were subsequently recoupled into an L10-PtFe framework, constructing the designed PtRuFeGaMo-I catalyst. PtRuFeGaMo-I integrates the multifunctionality of Pt–Ru/Ga/Mo motifs to simultaneously overcome the key limitations of alkaline HOR. Consequently, the engineered PtRuFeGaMo-I exhibits exceptional HOR performance. In an anion exchange membrane fuel cell (AEMFC), PtRuFeGaMo-I achieves a remarkable mass activity of 0.84 A mgtotal PGM −1, surpassing commercial Pt/C and most reported noble-metal-based catalysts. This work provides a new platform to design advanced catalysts tailored to diverse electrocatalytic demands.
n545db5cee016: While perovskites have emerged as frontrunners in optoelectronics due to their exceptional properties, their performance remains bottlenecked by film imperfections such as interfacial defects, non‐uniform crystallization, and band alignment mismatches. Conventional treatments often fail to simultaneously address issues at the top surface, the bulk, and the buried interface. In this work, we introduce a holistic top‐to‐bottom restructuring strategy using a facile vapor‐phase post‐treatment. This approach induces a gradient‐distributed 2D perovskite phase that extends from the surface into the bulk while uniquely healing structural voids and chemical inhomogeneities at the buried interface. This synergistic restructuring optimizes the energy band structure for accelerated carrier extraction and passivates defects throughout the entire film depth. As a result, our unencapsulated n‐i‐p solar cells demonstrate exceptional environmental resilience, maintaining over 90% of their initial efficiency after 2,800 h of high‐humidity exposure. This study establishes a new benchmark for stability and provides a robust pathway for high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics.
n893cd1edc5f0: Two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D-COFs) with tunable structures offer a promising platform for photocatalytic overall water splitting (OWS) under visible-light. However, it is challenging to quickly find photocatalytic OWS materials from the massive amounts of 2D-COFs and then achieve precise synthesis. In this work, we constructed 11 934 hcb-type 2D-COFs by assembling 28 building blocks and 9 linkages. The machine learning (ML) and high-throughput computation (HTC) were integrated to predict feasible photocatalytic OWS hcb-type 2D-COFs. Through training 10 initial algorithms and optimizing the hyperparameters of top 4 algorithms in terms of performance, the ETR model for predicting the band-edge levels with R2 of 0.97 and 0.99 was developed, and the KNR and RFR models were built for predicting ΔG *H and ΔG *OH with R2 of 0.99 and 0.83, respectively. 2581 2D‑COFs (21.63% of dataset) are screened to be potential structures for visible‑light‑driven water splitting. After applying the optimal ML models on all assembled 2D-COFs, a list of high-frequency building blocks and linkages is suggested as a set of suitable candidates for the first time. Then TBTZ_FBN0_Imine (TBTZ-FBN0-COF) was assembled and experimentally synthesized. Its OWS activity verified our ML-HTC paradigm, which provides the researchers recommendation to construct photocatalytic OWS 2D-COFs.
n8f9e2ebd1d75: Composite polymer electrolytes (CPEs) exhibit considerable potential for solid−state lithium−metal batteries (SLBs). However, incompatibilities between the various components in the electrolyte continue to hinder the full realization of its performance and practical applications. In this work, a multifunctional ceria interfacial layer is proposed to achieve uniform dispersion of ceramic fillers and facilitated interfacial transport of lithium ions in CPEs. At the same time, the physical barrier provided by this multifunctional interface layer prevents direct contact between the ceramic filler and the lithium metal, thereby avoiding potentially harmful side reactions that could further lead to a performance deterioration in battery cycling. Owing to the introduction of this multifunctional interface layer, the CPE exhibits high ionic conductivity (0.772 mS cm−1) and Li–ion transference number (0.626), with a wide electrochemical window (5.03 V). Furthermore, the Li|CPE|Li symmetric cell exhibits a lithium deposition/stripping capacity exceeding 1500 h at room temperature, indicating the CPE's excellent ability to suppress interfacial side reactions. Li|CPE|NCM811 cells retained a capacity of 77% after 350 cycles, whilst pouch cells retained 76% after 300 stable cycles at room temperature and 0.5 C. The method of optimizing ceramic fillers offers new insights into the design of novel composite solid–state electrolytes for SLBs.
n0624d0090f9d: Lithium–sulfur batteries (LSBs) offer energy densities beyond lithium-ion batteries, yet parasitic reactions between soluble polysulfides and lithium metal cause active-sulfur loss and porous Li, undermining cycle life. To address this problem, an anode protective layer is needed, but interactions between protective layers and polysulfides remain insufficiently understood. In this work, representative anionic and ceramic protective layers are employed as model systems to establish how strong polysulfide adsorption and persistent sulfur-species retention affect protective-layer functionality. Building on these findings, a positively polarized ferroelectric β-pvdf layer incorporating fluorinated boron nitride nanosheets (PPFBN) is introduced. Corona poling aligns polarization to establish an internal field, while insulating nanosheets suppress free-charge relaxation, thereby sustaining the field. The field promotes Li+ transport to the anode and impedes the approach of polysulfide anions, while intrinsically low polysulfide affinity limits long-term degradation of layer functionality. With PPFBN, Li/Li symmetric cells cycle stably for >1000 h in polysulfide-containing electrolytes at 2 mA cm− 2 and 2 mAh cm− 2. Full cells retain 80.4% capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C; under lean-electrolyte conditions, cycle life extends by more than 150 cycles relative to bare Li. This study establishes a ferroelectric-field, low-polysulfide-affinity design principle for durable anode protection in LSBs.
n9f159bf6925e: Aqueous magnesium‐ion batteries (AMIBs) have emerged as promising energy storage systems owing to their intrinsic safety, high energy density, and cost‐effectiveness. However, the intercalation of high‐charge‐density Mg2+ usually leads to irreversible structural degradation toward conventional electrodes with low practical capacity and inferior stability. To overcome the inherent lattice stress caused by Mg‐ion, we investigated a series of flexible organic molecules (FOMs), and for the first time proposed a novel ion‐adaptive strategy, achieving a high‐performance FOM with modulated molecular steric hindrance, high practical capacity, and robust stability in AMIBs. In contrast with ever‐increasing lattice stress with successive Mg‐ion intercalation in conventional electrode, the subsequent ion intercalation reduced the stress by facilitated ion‐storage in the optimized ion‐adaptive FOM, such as tribenzoquinoxaline‐5,10‐dione (3BQ), with ultimately improved practical capacity (332.1 mAh g−1 at 1.0 A g−1), ranking among the highest capacity in AMIBs to date. Furthermore, the expanded planar architecture confers enhanced cycling stability on the ion‐adaptive 3BQ, maintaining a high specific capacity of 196.7 mAh g−1 even after 7,000 cycles at 10.0 A g−1. The novel ion‐adaptive strategy provides a new pathway to design high‐capacity electrode materials in AMIBs and other multivalent‐ion batteries.
n896035e9eade: The development of practical lithium metal batteries requires facile strategies that simultaneously stabilize anode and cathode interfaces while eliminating their native surface oxides. However, the reported research could rarely achieve this dual functionality. Herein, we have developed a dual‐side‐modification strategy using tributylphosphonium tetrafluoroborate (TBPFB) as a Lewis acid to synchronously eliminate the heterogeneous native oxide layers and reconstruct multifunctional inorganic interfaces on both the cathode and anode. The constructed artificial interface on the lithium anode contains LiF, LiBO2, Li3P, and Li3PO4, boosting the anode stability by reducing the Li+ desolvation barrier and enabling uniform Li+ transport. Meanwhile, the LiF‐rich LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) cathode interface suppresses side reactions and particle cracking, protecting the cathode from transition metal dissolution. Based on the benefits brought by the multifunctional interfaces, the Li||Li symmetric cells achieve a cycling lifespan of over 1700 h, while the Li||NCM811 full cells retain 77% capacity after 500 cycles. Additionally, a 2 Ah pouch cell with an energy density of 423.1 Wh kg−1 maintains over 90% capacity after 100 cycles. This work provides a simple but highly efficient surface modification strategy that stabilizes the most critical interfaces in lithium metal batteries.
na18474074eaa: Mixed‐halide perovskites often undergo reversible phase segregation under illumination, yet the origin and the material properties governing this process remain debated. Several driving forces for halide segregation have been proposed, including polaronic strain, bandgap effects, internal electric fields, and photoinduced redox reactions. These are often treated as competing frameworks for the interpretation of seemingly similar experimental observations. Here, we argue that progress in the field is limited due to an intertwining of kinetic and thermodynamic aspects of segregation and encourage the use of a generalized thermodynamic description in which different microscopic models correspond to different ways of modifying the free‐energy balance under illumination. We therefore analyze the assumptions, predictions, and experimental signatures of the most widely discussed mechanisms. We further identify key limitations in current experimental approaches, mostly associated with an overreliance on photoluminescence as a characterization tool, and how variations in experimental conditions further obscure comparison across studies. By outlining descriptors and experimental strategies, we provide a basis for systematically testing competing mechanisms. This work thus aims to move the field from parallel model interpretations toward a more unified and quantitative understanding of halide segregation in perovskites.
n5f7e8f1956a9: Developing ruthenium‐based anode electrocatalysts to replace commercial iridium is crucial for reducing the cost of proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis. However, conventional RuO2 suffers from limited long‐term stability and severe overoxidation drawbacks. Herein, we employ dynamic H2 bubble template (DHBT)‐assisted electrodeposition combined with calcination to fabricate disorderly connected regular/irregular Ru‐O6 octahedra. In situ experiments and theoretical calculations reveal that this local coordination asymmetry favors an oxide path mechanism (OPM) involving direct O‐O coupling while suppressing *OOH formation and substantial lattice‐oxygen participation. The optimized d‐RuO2‐x catalyst requires an overpotential of only 154 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2 and maintains stable operation for over 3200 h at this current density. Crucially, in a PEM water electrolyzer, the catalyst operates robustly for over 2100 h at 200 mA cm−2 under continuous and start‐shutdown conditions. These results demonstrate that local coordination asymmetry engineering can tune OER pathway selection in dopant‐free RuO2‐based catalysts and provide a promising route toward durable acidic OER anodes.
n1827ee6837b4: Rational design of high‐performance electrolytes is central to the development of next‐generation lithium batteries, but it remains hindered by vast molecular design space, intricate multiscale structure–property relationships, and multiple performance requirements. Although machine learning (ML) accelerates electrolyte discovery through data‐driven performance prediction, most existing studies rely on sparse performance data and provide limited physical interpretability, thereby falling short of true rational design. This review traces the evolution of ML‐enabled electrolyte research from macroscopic performance prediction to mesoscale mechanistic understanding, with particular emphasis on the limited coverage of electrolyte chemical space in existing performance datasets and the insufficient evaluation of model extrapolation. We then review the physically interpretable descriptors and examine their intercorrelations and domains of applicability using a common set of 26 representative solvents. The current maturity and remaining limitations of ML‐based descriptor prediction are further assessed to support the high‐throughput virtual screening of electrolyte candidates. Finally, we review recent advances in performance‐guided autonomous experimentation and discuss the key challenges associated with establishing descriptor‐guided closed‐loop discovery platforms. Although descriptor‐driven rational electrolyte design has yet to be fully realized, this review outlines an actionable roadmap for integrating physically interpretable descriptors, generalizable ML models, and autonomous experimentation toward interpretable, data‐driven electrolyte discovery.
n3f3cbf5797c2: Different from traditional industrial urea synthesis using NH3 and CO2, heterogeneous photocatalysis enables direct urea synthesis from N2 and CO2 in aqueous, where water acts as both solvent and hydrogen source. Its low yield is mainly restricted by poor reactant activation efficiency, mismatched reaction kinetics, slow C─N coupling and slow gas mass transfer via water hydrogen bond networks. Herein, an external magnetic field was adopted to boost photocatalytic urea synthesis. Upon magneto‐photocatalysis, water hydrogen bonds were disturbed to form gas diffusion channel and release sufficient hydrogen protons. Driven by the Lorentz force and magnetohydrodynamic convection, electron‐proton interactions were strengthened. Meanwhile, spin‐polarized electrons and regulated active sites activated N2 and CO2 and accelerated C─N coupling. Under ambient conditions and a 40‐mT magnetic field, ZIF‐67@MIL‐101(Fe) achieved a urea yield as high as 147.28 µmol g−1 h−1. Mechanism to the enhancement along with reaction pathways were clarified via experimental and simulation results. Practical applicability was confirmed using simulated flue gas, and the obtained urea solution could cultivate wheat seedlings. Overall, this work proposed a magnetic field‐enhanced photocatalytic urea production strategy, offering a universal approach for efficient N2 activation toward urea and other nitrogen‐containing chemicals.
n3c7c98f30f3b: Lithium‐ion batteries can deliver higher energy densities when using high‐voltage cathodes such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 (LNMO), yet their practical application is hindered by the catalytic nature of high‐voltage cathode materials which usually cause electrolytes decomposition. Although the utilization of fluorinated carbonates as electrolyte solvent considerably inhibited the parasitic reaction at cathode side, the irrational fluorination often leads to the sluggish Li+ transport which finally causes poor rate performance. Here, we design a family of trifluoromethyl‐substituted carboxylate esters as electrolyte solvents. We found that the spatial arrangement between the ‐CF3 and the carbonyl group in these fluorinated esters is critical for regulating the electrolyte solvation structures. A short distance (α‐substitution) severely weakens the solvating power of the solvent, resulting in a substantial decrease in ionic conductivity, whereas an extended separation (γ‐substitution) compromises the oxidation resistance against high‐voltage cathodes. Only the trifluoromethylation at the β‐position yields optimal solvent (methyl 3,3,3‐trifluoropropionate, MTFP) that can simultaneously meets high‐voltage and fast‐charging requirements of LNMO||Gr cells when pairing with fluoroethylene carbonate and 1 M LiPF6. In such electrolyte, the Ah‐level LNMO||Gr pouch cells deliver 78% capacity retention at 6C charge/discharge rate (13.2 mA cm−2), and stably operate over 300 cycles at the high rate of 3C.
nd51697cb7e81: Sulfide‐based all‐solid‐state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) with high‐loading cathodes are currently hindered by sluggish Li+/electron kinetics and poor interfacial compatibility. Conventional carbon additives, despite their high conductivity, often trigger detrimental side reactions with sulfide electrolytes. To mitigate these issues, we introduce a multifunctional nanoscale In2O3 conductive agent, integrated via a facile one‐step ball milling process. This nano‐In2O3 effectively mediates interactions between large Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 (LPSC) and LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) particles, enhancing mixing homogeneity and collision efficiency. The resulting composite cathode features a low‐tortuosity Li+ transport network and establishes rapid “NCM‐nano In2O3‐NCM” electronic pathways within particle gaps. Crucially, In2O3 improves interfacial compatibility between the LPSC and conductive additives, suppressing interfacial degradation. Consequently, a high‐loading cathode (18.34 mg cm−2) demonstrates a specific capacity of 131 mAh g−1 at 3C and exhibits excellent cyclability, retaining 97.6% capacity after 500 cycles in NCM811||Li cells. This strategy highlights the potential of nanoscale metal oxide additives for achieving high‐energy‐density ASSLBs through optimized interfacial and transport kinetics.
n7ed5f7545cd5: The carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO2RR) is central to carbon valorization and renewable electricity storage, yet its selectivity, efficiency, and durability depend on coordinating proton availability with electron transfer at dynamic electrochemical interfaces. Despite advances in catalysts, electrolytes, hydrogen evolution suppression, and devices, proton effects are described by isolated descriptors, such as pH, water activity, buffer capacity, cation identity, hydrophobicity, ionomer chemistry, and local alkalinity. This fragmentation obscures how protons regulate initiation, *COOH formation, *CO/formate branching, *CO coverage, C─C coupling, hydrogen evolution, and high‐flux decay. A proton‐centered perspective is needed to link atomic proton‐transfer events with interfacial microenvironments and device operation. This review establishes proton regulation as a mechanistic framework for CO2RR by examining proton sources, transport pathways, interfacial accessibility, hydrogen‐bond‐network reorganization, local electric fields, and proton‐coupled electron‐transfer timing. By integrating molecular mechanisms, microenvironment modulation, in situ characterization, and gas‐diffusion or membrane‐electrode architectures, we organize dispersed observations into a source–transport–utilization framework. This framework shows how proton location, dose, and temporal availability define kinetic boundaries between hydrogen evolution, one‐carbon (C1) products, and multicarbon (C2+) pathways, while governing stability under practical fluxes. Proton regulation guides selective, scalable, and durable CO2 electroconversion.
nee1bf3016c2b: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) show critical thermo-mechanical and defect mediated degradation at interfaces, limiting their deployment in terrestrial high-temperature and space-like environments. This study presents a dual-function interfacial passivation strategy that combines nanoparticle cerium oxide (CeO x ) with phenylethylammonium iodide (PEAI) to form a hybrid surface treatment (PC) for poly[bis(4-phenyl)(2,4,6-trimethylphenyl)amine (PTAA) based n-i-p PSC architecture, where defect passivation is complemented by redox coupling and enhanced thermal stress stabilization. Optimized PC-treated devices achieved a champion efficiency of 25.3% and exhibited enhanced operational stabilities under continuous 1 SUN light soaking and 85°C/85% RH damp heat respectively. To probe the engineered interface mechanistically, we employed an accelerated thermal shock (TS) cycling to mimic low Earth orbit (LEO) relevant thermal cycling condition. Under realistically simulated TS conditions of cycling temperature between 80°C and −80°C and 16°C/min ramp rate transition, PC-treated devices retained 95% of initial efficiency after 100 cycles of TS, showing superior stability compared to their counterparts without CeO x . Collectively, this work highlights a new insight into dynamic thermal fatigue in PSCs and introduces a practical route toward thermally resilient, high efficiency perovskite photovoltaics.
nbe0ed568e580: Perovskite Solar Cells Integrating cerium oxide nanoparticle (CeOx) into phenylethylammonium iodide (PEAI) creates a dual‐function passivation strategy that improves both efficiency and thermal shock stability in perovskite solar cells. Enhanced perovskite lattice stability and suppressed thermally induced degradation enable robust device performance, advancing perovskite photovoltaics toward demanding terrestrial and space operation environments. More in article number e71312, Behrang H. Hamadani, Jae Sung Yun, Helen Hejin Park, and co‐workers.
n599fdc12a766: After 30 years of commercialization and mass production, lithium‐ion batteries have generated massive waste streams, especially with their expanding use in electric vehicles. Recycling spent batteries and valorizing useful components are therefore increasingly urgent for sustainable development. However, conventional pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical methods are limited by high energy consumption or large chemical input, creating demand for greener and more efficient recycling technologies. Here, using LiCoO2 as an example, we report a closed‐loop electrified chemical process based on redox‐targeting reactions to recover valuable species from spent battery materials using only electricity and water. Complementary reductive leaching of LiCoO2 and oxidative leaching of LiFePO4 were performed with anthraquinone‐2,7‐disulfonate as a regenerative redox mediator to sequentially break down LiCoO2 and achieve efficient separation of Co2+ and Li+ in the form of Co(OH)2 and LiOH. This cost‐effective and environmentally friendly method was also extended to the recycling of LiNixMnyCozO2 with a high recovery rate of Li+ and transition metal species. It is anticipated that the electrified chemical recycling method demonstrated here would provide a credible solution to the valorization of battery waste and contribute to the sustainable development of lithium‐ion batteries.
n6b33e807d9e3: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are limited by poor operational stability arising from undercoordinated Pb/I defects that induce severe non‐radiative recombination. Here, a regioisomer‐guided molecular engineering strategy is proposed to modulate interfacial coordination and structural reconstruction. Pyridinecarboxamide isomers with distinct substitution positions are introduced, among which para‐configured isonicotinamide (INA) exhibits a larger dipole moment and enhanced charge redistribution, enabling stronger coordination with undercoordinated Pb2+ and more efficient interfacial charge transfer. The cooperative interaction between the amide group and pyridine nitrogen further directs ordered molecular stacking and anisotropic growth, inducing the in situ formation of a 1D (INA)PbI3 layer on the three‐dimensional perovskite surface and constructing a robust 1D/3D heterojunction. This architecture simultaneously suppresses defect‐assisted recombination and enhances environmental tolerance. As a result, INA‐modified devices achieve a high power conversion efficiency of 26.57%, representing one of the highest efficiencies reported for 1D/3D PSCs. Moreover, the unencapsulated devices retain 91% of their initial efficiency after 600 h under harsh damp heat conditions (85°C/85% RH) and exhibit excellent operational stability under cyclic illumination. This work provides a structure–property correlation for isomer engineering and offers an effective route toward highly efficient and stable PSCs.
n1e7f1e000e9e: The rapid growth of wearable electronics, smart textiles, and the Internet of Things (IoT) has increased the demand for sustainable, self‐powered energy solutions. Textile‐based triboelectric nanogenerators (T‐TENGs) have emerged as a promising technology by combining efficient mechanical energy harvesting with the flexibility, breathability, stretchability, washability, and wearability of textiles. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in T‐TENGs, covering the complete design hierarchy from fundamental mechanisms to wearable applications. The operating principles of alternating‐current and emerging direct‐current TENGs, including contact electrification, electrostatic induction, electrostatic breakdown, and tribovoltaic effects, are discussed. Recent progress in triboelectric material engineering, fiber and yarn design, and textile architectures—including woven, knitted, braided, embroidered, multilayer, and 3D structures—is systematically reviewed with emphasis on performance enhancement and scalability. Applications in biomechanical sensing, wearable healthcare, human–machine interaction, smart textiles, and self‐powered wearable systems are summarized, highlighting the distinction between self‐powered sensing and fully autonomous wearable platforms. Finally, key challenges, including low current output, environmental stability, washability, durability, scalable manufacturing, performance standardization, and commercialization, are critically analyzed, and future research directions toward intelligent, fully autonomous, and commercially viable self‐powered wearable systems are outlined.
ne9aacc6a39ec: Polyacrylonitrile‐based carbon nanofibers (CNFs) are widely regarded as promising sodium‐storage anodes owing to their high carbon yield/axial conductivity and superior mechanical flexibility. Nevertheless, the ambiguous understandings into the temperature‐dependent micro‐structure evolution, particularly the closed‐pore formation over pyrolysis, and the electrolyte induced electrode‐electrolyte interface micro‐environments, along with the involved influence mechanism upon sodium‐storage behaviors should be reasonably clarified. With systematical in(ex)‐situ physicochemical/electrochemical characterizations, it is first established that the optimal pyrolysis temperature of 1400°C combined with a “zipper‐like” point‐line‐plane solid‐phase fusion evolution effectively modulates micro‐structures, endowing the optimized pseudo‐graphitized CNFs film (i.e., GCNFs‐1400) with a synergistic balance among ions transport pathways (interlayer spacing), active storage sites (closed pores), and 3D conductive supporting framework (solid‐phase fusion). Concurrently, compared to the ester‐based electrolyte, the ether‐based electrolyte favors the formation of a thinner, more uniform, and chemically stable solid electrolyte interphase layer. It is the dual‐engineering of both material micro‐structures and interfacial micro‐environment that fully guarantees the competitive sodium‐storage properties of GCNFs‐1400 in terms of ultra‐high initial Coulombic efficiency (96.2%), rate capability, and long‐term stability toward presodiation‐free sodium‐ion batteries and sodium‐ion capacitors. More essentially, our in‐depth insights here provide meaningful guidance for future design of advanced hard carbon anodes toward efficient sodium storage.
nf0b40ca9c682: Strain engineering has emerged as an effective strategy for tailoring the electronic structure and catalytic behavior of materials at the atomic scale. For electrochemical water splitting, the sluggish kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction and oxygen evolution reaction are largely limited by scaling relationships and nonoptimized adsorption energetics of key intermediates. High‐entropy materials, featuring multiprincipal‐element compositions and pronounced lattice distortion, offer a unique platform for strain‐mediated catalytic regulation. Their intrinsic microstrain fields, derived from atomic size mismatch together with sluggish diffusion and cocktail effects, enable tunable electronic structures and abundant metastable active sites. This review summarizes recent advances in strain engineering of high‐entropy materials for water splitting. Fundamental concepts of strain and its influence on d‐band centers, adsorption energetics, and reaction kinetics are first introduced. This is followed by a discussion of strain modulation strategies, including doping, solid solution alloying, and defect engineering. Special emphasis is placed on the distinct behavior of high‐entropy materials compared with conventional alloys, particularly their nonlinear electronic hybridization and multisite synergy. Finally, key challenges involving strain quantification, operando evolution, and strain‐entropy coupling are highlighted, providing guidance for the rational design of next‐generation water‐splitting catalysts.
n24fdfe18c453: Formamidinium lead triiodide perovskite quantum dots (FAPbI3 PQDs) receive increasing attention for next‐generation solar cells owing to their remarkable optoelectronic properties and solution processability. However, the dynamic binding of native surface ligands inevitably induces surface lattice vacancies and distortions, significantly deteriorating the optoelectronic properties and stability of PQDs. Herein, a facile surface lattice‐adaptive integrity reconstruction strategy is reported to regulate the surface lattice of PQDs. After molecule screening, the 3‐guanidinopropionic acid (GPA) with a geometry‐adaptive configuration can effectively passivate the intrinsic surface lattice vacancies through the Pb‐O coordination and guanidinium‐mediated hydrogen‐bonding interactions. Meanwhile, the surface lattice‐adaptive configuration of the GPA can also substantially ameliorate the distorted surface lattice, which largely improves the surface lattice integrity and enhances the electronic coupling of PQDs, facilitating charge carrier transport in the PQD solids. Consequently, the power conversion efficiency is increased from 16.15% for the control solar cell to 19.32% for the GPA‐based solar cell. This work provides important insight into the physical design principles for the surface lattice of PQDs through lattice‐adaptive molecules and offers implementable strategies for the development of high‐performance optoelectronic devices.
nbe7978ee3b54: Quasi‐solid‐state sodium metal batteries (QSSMBs) have emerged as a pivotal technology for safe, high‐energy‐density, and large‐scale energy storage. However, the practical application of QSSMBs is severely hindered by the formation of an unstable and high‐impedance solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that fails to accommodate the dramatic volume fluctuations of sodium (Na) metal anodes, consequently leading to rapid capacity decay during high‐rate cycling. Herein, we propose a rational design strategy to construct a rigid‐inner/flexible‐outer gradient SEI architecture by modulating the stepwise reduction behavior of functional additives within a poly(1,3‐dioxolane) electrolyte. By introducing 2,2,2‐trifluoroethyl trifluoromethanesulfonate to undergo synergistic decomposition with fluoroethylene carbonate, this formulation enables the in situ construction of the dual‐layer gradient interphase. This unique SEI efficiently facilitates desolvation and accelerates Na+ transport, while achieving even Na plating after cycling. Consequently, the designed electrolyte delivers outstanding electrochemical performance, enabling Na || sodium vanadium phosphate full cells to exhibit long cycle‐life of 5500 cycles at 20 C and 97.5% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 25 C. This work highlights the critical role of gradient SEI engineering and offers an insightful design principle for developing next‐generation QSSMBs.
nfd3a4c4a0f93: Scaling aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) to pouch-type configurations amplifies electric-field and Zn2+ flux heterogeneities, causing non-uniform Zn deposition. Here, β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) and Tween 80 (Tw80) are systematically investigated to decouple bulk transport and interfacial kinetic regulation in scale-up pouch-type cells. β-CD increases ionic conductivity (3.44 to 5.95 mS cm− 1) and the Zn2+ transference number (0.16 to 0.47), promoting uniform bulk ion flux and extending symmetric pouch-type cell lifespan beyond 1000 h at 1 mA cm− 2. Conversely, Tw80 operates via interfacial adsorption to regulate local reaction kinetics, achieving stable cycling for >600 h. Spatially resolved analysis, operando Raman spectroscopy, and in situ thermal imaging reveal that β-CD suppresses macroscopic heterogeneity across near-tab, central, and edge regions by stabilizing bulk solvation, whereas Tw80 mitigates localized interfacial instability. In practical Zn||V2O5 pouch-type full cells, β-CD delivers superior long-term capacity retention, while Tw80 excels under high-rate conditions. This work identifies spatial electrochemical heterogeneity as a primary scaling limit and offers general design principles connecting additive chemistry, transport kinetics, and format-dependent deposition for practical AZIBs.
n980e1790c700: The inward diffusion of Ag electrodes and outward migration of perovskite constituents trigger a vicious degradation cycle in inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), severely limiting device longevity. Herein, 2,5‐dimercapto‐1,3,4‐thiadiazole (DMTD) is introduced as a bidirectional ionic barrier layer to simultaneously stabilize the Ag electrode and the perovskite lattice. The ‐SH groups strongly coordinate with Ag+ to establish a molecular barrier against Ag migration, while the ‐N‐N‐ groups bind Pb2+ to passivate defects and reinforce the crystal structure. This synergistic bidirectional inhibition effectively prevents interfacial reactions between perovskite species and Ag+, thereby breaking the chain of mutually reinforced degradation. As a result, DMTD‐modified devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.13% and exhibit outstanding stability, retaining 87.68% of their initial PCE after 3000 h of storage at 25°C (15% ± 5% RH), and 80.87% after 1000 h under continuous heating at 85°C.
n0f931627c5cc: Achieving dynamic, in situ switchable molecular recognition in porous composites remains challenging due to the difficulty of precisely modulating interfacial noncovalent interactions at the atomic level. Here, we demonstrated that proton‐coupled interfacial force reconstruction served as a general and efficient regulatory strategy to control adsorption‐desorption behaviors in a metal‐organic framework (MOFs)‐based covalent organic framework (COF) composite, NH2‐UiO‐66@COF‐TpDBA (NU@FC). Reversible protonation‐deprotonation at carboxyl sites induced precise redistribution of the interfacial noncovalent force field, thereby endowing switchable molecular capture and markedly improving the utilization efficiency of interfacial active sites, constructing a stimuli‐responsive adsorption platform featuring molecular capture and release. This atomic‐scale regulation, coupled with solvent‐ triggered microenvironment modulation, allowed adaptive recognition of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) under diverse environments. Combined with the mechanically reinforced sheath‐tube‐protected solid‐phase microextraction device (STP‐SPME), this proton‐responsive interfacial regulation strategy was extended to an in situ, low‐cost, anti‐interference sample pretreatment system, achieving reliable identification and efficient extraction of trace organic pollutants from complex environmental matrices. Beyond device‐level performance, this study established proton‐coupled force reconstruction as a general design principle for constructing intelligently responsive MOF‐COF composites, bridging atomic‐scale interfacial modulation with expansive environmental analysis.
ndc07e2f31dd0: As non‐precious metal catalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), the performance of transition metal oxides is limited by electronic‐state tuning from static doping strategies. This work proposes a novel strategy for dynamically regulating the electronic state of catalysts using an alternating magnetic field (AMF). We synthesized a series of MnxCo3‐xO4 catalysts, where Co substitution enriches high‐spin Mn2+ centers and introduces lattice flexibility. Under a low‐energy AMF, the magnetic moments of high‐spin Mn2+ undergo forced precession. Through dynamic magneto‐structural coupling within the compliant lattice, this spin dynamics acts as a continuous structural perturbation that provides a pathway for dynamic orbital regulation, potentially driven by the lifting of d‐orbital degeneracy. This optimized orbital configuration enables a favorable binding energy with H* intermediates, accelerating the sluggish Volmer step and enhancing HER activity. Under the AMF, the Mn2.5Co0.5O4 exhibits a low overpotential of 13 mV at 10 mA cm−2, outperforming previously reported manganese‐based oxides. This work offers a strategy to dynamically lift d‐orbital degeneracy for efficient water electrolysis.
n12f180b4a32f: Rechargeable magnesium batteries (RMBs) are a promising post‐lithium battery technology due to abundant magnesium reserves, high volumetric capacity, and dendrite‐free Mg anodes. However, the strong electrostatic interaction between Mg2+ and inorganic cathode lattices causes high diffusion barriers and sluggish kinetics. To circumvent this, two‐dimensional conductive metal‐organic frameworks (2D c‐MOFs), featuring favorable electronic transport characteristics arising from π‐d hybridization and structural tunability, have attracted widespread attention. This work systematically investigates the electrochemical performance of M3(HITP)2 (M = Co, Ni, Cu; HITP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexaiminotriphenylene) as cathodes for RMBs and reveals the decisive role of the metal center in Mg storage. All three materials achieve synergistic dual‐ion storage through heteroatomic N coordination with Mg2+ coupled with anion intercalation. Among them, Ni3(HITP)2 demonstrates superior overall performance, arising from its characteristic Ni2+ d8 electronic configuration, which facilitates the formation of a stable Ni‐N coordination environment and effective π‐d conjugation. It retains approximately 201 mAh g−1 after 1100 cycles at 1.0 A g−1, corresponding to a high‐capacity retention of 98.0%. This study elucidates how different metal centers regulate Mg storage in 2D c‐MOFs, providing molecular‐level guidance for designing high‐performance organic cathodes for multivalent‐ion batteries.
n081921de84bb: Bacterial biofilms are protected by an extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix primarily composed of extracellular DNA, proteins, and polysaccharides, rendering them highly resistant to conventional antimicrobial treatments. Although natural hydrolases efficiently degrade individual EPS components, their narrow substrate scope, poor stability, and high cost restrict effective biofilm eradication. Here, we report a catalytic microenvironment engineering strategy that enables broad‐spectrum hydrolase nanozymes through arginine‐directed modulation of Zr‐based metal–organic frameworks (ZrMOFs). Systematic amino acid‐directed defect engineering afforded a series of amino acid‐coordinated ZrMOFs, among which arginine‐coordinated ZrMOF (Arg‐ZrMOF) exhibited the highest hydrolase‐like catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km = 1437.5 M−1 s−1). The enhanced catalytic performance originated from the engineered catalytic microenvironment, characterized by increased surface hydrophilicity, enhanced formation of nucleophilic Zr–OH species, and strengthened electrostatic interactions with negatively charged substrates. Arg‐ZrMOF efficiently hydrolyzed phosphodiester, peptide, and glycosidic bonds, enabling concerted degradation of extracellular DNA, proteins, and polysaccharides within the EPS matrix. This expanded hydrolytic substrate scope enabled superior inhibition and eradication of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus biofilms, outperforming the benchmark enzyme DNase I while retaining over 80% catalytic activity after 60 reuse cycles and excellent storage stability for more than 100 days. Furthermore, a spray‐on Arg‐ZrMOF formulation enabled effective biofilm removal from stainless‐steel, plastic, and glass surfaces, demonstrating its practical applicability for surface biofilm control. This work establishes catalytic microenvironment engineering as a versatile strategy for constructing hydrolase nanozymes capable of broad biomacromolecular degradation and practical biofilm eradication.
n436e2606e35b: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage but suffer from Zn dendrite growth, water-induced parasitic reactions, and interfacial instability. Herein, inspired by natural nucleotide architectures, we introduce disodium inosinate (IMP) as a green multifunctional electrolyte additive to regulate Zn electrochemistry. Its naturally preorganized nucleotide framework integrates chemically differentiated phosphate, hydroxyl-rich ribose, and O/N-containing heterocyclic regions, which exhibit distinct interaction preferences toward Zn2 +, water molecules, and the Zn surface under different local electrochemical environments.
