Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that IMP participates in Zn2+ solvation and regulates the local water environment, while preferential multisite adsorption at the Zn interface homogenizes Zn2+ flux and promotes Zn(002)-preferred deposition, enabling dense and dendrite-suppressed Zn growth. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells achieve stable cycling for over 2000 h at 5 mA cm−2 and 2.5 mAh cm−2, while Zn||Cu cells maintain an average Coulombic efficiency above 99.8% over 3500 cycles. Zn||NVO full cells retain 87.3% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g−1, and pouch cells demonstrate stable cycling for 300 cycles. This work highlights how the intrinsic chemical differentiation of a naturally preorganized nucleotide architecture can translate into distinct molecular interactions across different electrochemical environments, providing a bio-inspired strategy for sustainable aqueous electrolyte design.
n6f8e625d26ac: Enhancing electron extraction and suppressing interfacial recombination are essential for achieving high‐performance inverted perovskite solar cells. However, the commonly used [6,6]‐phenyl‐C61‐butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM) electron transport layer (ETL) suffers from self‐aggregation during operation and possesses insufficient functional groups for perovskite passivation, which deteriorate charge collection and long‐term stability. Here, two C60‐terminated bis‐fullerene derivatives, namely C60‐IT‐C60 and C60‐L8BO‐C60, are employed to modify the PCBM ETL. These additives preserve high compatibility with PCBM and feature π‐conjugated bridge‐linkers that can regulate the intermolecular interactions with PCBM as well as the interfacial defect passivation toward perovskite. Compared with the IT‐bridged molecule, C60‐L8BO‐C60, featuring a more rigid and extended dithienothiophen[3,2‐b]‐pyrrolobenzothiadiazole (TPBT) bridge, enables more extensive π‐conjugated contacts with surrounding PCBM molecules and more effective interfacial passivation, leading to enhanced electron mobility, reduced trap density, and accelerated interfacial electron extraction. As a result, the unencapsulated C60‐L8BO‐C60‐based inverted device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 25.40%, and retains 80% of its initial efficiency after more than 1400 h of continuous thermal aging at 85°C in a N2 atmosphere in the dark.
nb023ee68ec93: 2D perovskites, characterized by distinctive quantum‐well structure and high exciton binding energy, offer unprecedented opportunities for photonic detection. However, synergistically driving efficient carrier extraction and rapid radiative recombination within monolithic single crystals (SC) remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, a room‐temperature chemical equilibrium‐modulated crystallization strategy is demonstrated to synthesize centimeter‐scale 2D (PA)2PbBr4 (PPB) SCs. The use of a hygroscopic acid‐base reactive agent precisely regulates the solvent evaporation kinetics, suppressing stochastic nucleation and yielding high‐quality SCs with suppressed light scattering. Consequently, planar PPB photodetectors (PDs) exhibit a notable and robust UV response, featuring a large on/off ratio of 2.77 × 104, a wide linear dynamic range of 159 dB, and an ultra‐low limit of detection of 3.5 nW cm−2. Simultaneously, the intense exciton confinement endows the PPB SCs with strong radioluminescence and robust radiation stability. Both SCs and flexible film scintillators demonstrate excellent practical x‐ray imaging capabilities. Crucially, the absence of grain boundaries inherently mitigates internal light scattering, enabling SC scintillators to achieve an impressive spatial resolution up to 26.5 lp mm−1, representing one of the highest values among the reported metal halide SC scintillators. This work establishes a kinetically control for high‐quality SCs synthesis and provides valuable insights for high‐performance and robust dual‐mode photonic detection.
n3b67de7e5599: Conversion-type anode materials hold great promise for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), yet their practical rate performance is fundamentally constrained by sluggish reaction kinetics beyond mass-transport limitations. Despite notable advances in accelerating ion/electron transport, intrinsically reducing the large reaction kinetic barrier and activation energy associated with robust metal–chalcogen (M─S) bonds remains a long-standing challenge. In this study, we propose a universal spin-polarization-engineered (SPE) antibonding-orbital modulation paradigm to fundamentally regulate M─S bond strength and enable ultrahigh-rate sodium storage. As a proof of concept, magnetic manganese heteroatom doping into heterojunctions enhances the saturation magnetization by ∼210%, inducing a spin-state transition from low-spin to high-spin configurations, which increases the electron occupation of antibonding orbitals formed between metal e g orbitals and chalcogen p orbitals, and thereby regulates M─S bond strength. Benefiting from this spin-engineered electronic reconstruction, Mn-FeS2/CoS2 anode delivers an ultrahigh-rate capability of 300 mA h g−1 at 120 A g−1, together with exceptional long-term durability (∼100% retention over 13 000 cycles at 100 A g−1), ranking among the best record. The generality of this strategy is further validated by extending SPE modulation to other magnetic dopants. Moreover, the industrial-level pouch cell is assembled to demonstrate the practical potential of this strategy.
nf0ba34601f09: The increasing fire accidents, excessive UV exposure, and health threats posed by bacterial infections urgently require advanced polymer materials integrating multiple safety protections. In this study, we propose an ultra‐efficient strategy to achieve the all‐in‐one integration of inherently flame‐retardant, UV‐resistant, and antibacterial polymer materials through a single biguanide unit. The key lies in the unique triple protection mechanism exerted by the biguanide unit: high‐temperature char‐formation for flame retardance, n→π* transition absorption for UV‐resistance, and disruption of the negatively charged bacterial surface for antibacteria. As a result, the biguanide‐containing polymer material achieves the best UL‐94 V‐0 flame‐retardant rating with excellent self‐extinguishing properties, ≥99.3% ultra‐high shielding rate for UV light, and ≥99.0% remarkable antibacterial rate. Importantly, the biguanide unit is chemically bonded to the polymer main chain, which not only avoids the health risks and performance degradation caused by the additive migration, but also exhibits outstanding heat resistance, thermal stability, and easy processability. This work simultaneously achieves triple functional integration of polymer materials through a single biguanide unit, realizing previously unattainable multiple safety protections against dangerous fires, harmful UV, and widely‐existed bacteria.
n1cb9b1ffcbf7: Touch behavior constitutes the most direct physical manifestation of human intentions, meaning that intention decoding requires human–machine interfaces to simultaneously sense touch position and pressure. Conventional systems, however, rely on physically stacked discrete sensors and von Neumann architectures, causing data redundancy and impaired wearability. Here, we present an in‐sensor‐computing dual‐modal neural fiber (ID neural fiber) that overcomes this fundamental limitation. The ID neural fiber achieves an unprecedented position resolution of < 5 mm and a pressure detection limit of 0.6 N, combined with exceptional robustness–sustaining 300 times load‐bearing capacity and exhibiting < 8% performance fluctuation under bending. Coupled with flexibility, waterproofing, and reconfigurability, the ID neural fiber can be seamlessly integrated into textiles for reliable operation in harsh environments, including underwater robotic control. Crucially, the ID neural fiber enables in‐sensor computing that dramatically increases the information density and allows synchronized feature fusion through programmable logic gates, enabling efficient real‐time intention recognition. To capture touch habits, an intelligent system with the ID neural fiber achieves a remarkable identification accuracy of 98.21%. This work establishes a new material–architecture paradigm that unifies ultrarobustness, dual‐modality, and in‐sensor computing, setting the stage for next‐generation wearable human–machine interfaces with both comfort and intelligence.
ne77e8942d76e: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have expanded from clinically validated prophylactic vaccines toward protein replacement and supplementation. Yet mRNA delivery remains centered on intramuscular vaccination and intravenous administration, largely optimized for systemic adaptive immunity or circulation‐mediated biodistribution. Many localized diseases, however, are confined to tissues or compartments accessible by topical, transdermal, inhaled, oral, catheter‐based, ocular, or intra‐articular administration without initial reliance on circulation. For these diseases, the therapeutic objective is likewise local: therapeutically relevant mRNA expression occurs within the affected tissue, and efficacy derives predominantly from the local biological activity of the encoded protein rather than from downstream systemic effects initiated by local expression. This therapeutic paradigm is defined here as Anatomically Accessible Local mRNA Therapeutics (ALmT). The review first distinguishes ALmT from intravenous mRNA delivery and intramuscular mRNA vaccination, then organizes site‐specific barriers and engineering strategies across major anatomical sites. It further examines disease‐focused ALmT applications, highlighting protein restoration, cytokine or growth‐factor supplementation, local antibody‐fragment production, regenerative modulation, and tissue repair. Finally, it discusses general design principles, quantitative PK/PD evaluation, repeat‐dose safety, and clinical translation. Overall, the ALmT framework may facilitate the design, quantitative evaluation, and clinical translation of mRNA therapies for localized diseases.
n047467a7c540: Photocatalytic semi-hydrogenation of acetylene (C2H2) to ethylene (C2H4) often suffers from inefficient interfacial electron transfer from the photocatalysts to adsorbed C2H2. Here, we demonstrate that axial coordination of benzotriazole (BTA) to Ni single atoms in C3N4 (BTA-Ni SAs-C3N4) facilitates interfacial electron-transfer processes. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, in situ transient surface photovoltage spectroscopy, in situ photochemical infrared spectroscopy, and theoretical simulations reveal that BTA-coordinated Ni SAs serve as the centers for rapid electron transfer by upshifting the Ni d-band center and strengthening the orbital overlap between Ni SA and adsorbed C2H2. Consequently, BTA-Ni SAs-C3N4 achieves a very high C2H4 production rate of 32.29 mmol gcat −1 h−1 with a C2H4 selectivity of 97.6% under simulated solar irradiation, which is ∼4-times higher than that for Ni SAs-C3N4. The apparent quantum yield at 365 nm is up to 4.65%, superior to reported photocatalytic acetylene semi-hydrogenation. This work highlights the importance of interfacial charge transfer in photocatalytic acetylene hydrogenation and provides a rational strategy for designing high-performance photocatalysts.
nd4328196c782: Uniform Li deposition on practical Cu current collectors remains challenging in lithium metal batteries. Despite extensive efforts in facet engineering, achieving homogeneous Li deposition on practical polycrystalline Cu collectors remains elusive, highlighting an incomplete understanding of the structural factors governing Li deposition. Herein, a defect-mediated interfacial engineering strategy is developed by simultaneously introducing a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) and enriched <110>/<111> textures on commercial electrodeposited Cu foils. Theoretical calculations and experiments reveal that densely distributed dislocations provide thermodynamically favorable Li adsorption sites and abundant preferential heterogeneous nucleation sites, while the enriched <110>/<111> textures promote Li surface diffusion and lateral growth. This combined effect promotes uniform and compact initial Li deposition, guiding path-dependent deposition evolution and suppressing interfacial heterogeneity. The control experiments further support a key contribution of dislocation defects, while variations in surface chemistry or morphology alone cannot account for the observed performance differences. The optimized Cu foil sustains over 1200 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.52% ± 0.20% over the final 200 cycles (n = 4) in Li||Cu cells and improves N/P = 0 Cu||NCM811 full-cell cycling. This work establishes dislocation-mediated nucleation and orientation-regulated growth as a design principle for practical Cu current collectors.
n88af105ef95e: Twisted bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides, governed by a single twisted interface, offer a versatile platform for manipulating interlayer coupling and emergent optical behavior. However, despite extensive studies on single twisted interface systems, how multi‐interface twisted stacking influences nonlinear optical behavior remains unclear. Here, we address this gap by systematically investigating the nonlinear optical performance of chemical vapor deposition (CVD) grown twisted trilayer MoS2 (TT‐MoS2) with multi‐interface twisted stacking. We fabricate all nine distinct trilayer MoS2 configurations by CVD. Raman and photoluminescence show that twisted interfaces modulate interlayer coupling, giving rise to stacking‐dependent phonon and excitonic responses. Atomic‐resolution scanning, transmission electron microscopy, and selected area electron diffraction confirm dual twisted interfaces and a supermoiré lattice. Guided by these structural insights, we examine the second harmonic generation (SHG) response across all nine trilayer configurations. Extending the coherent SH field superposition model to a trilayer system with two independent twisted interfaces, we develop a framework that describes how the dual interfaces govern the SHG intensity and polarization orientation across stacking configurations. Our findings establish TT‐MoS2 as a versatile nonlinear platform and open new avenues for understanding and exploiting multi‐interface twisted coupling to engineer nonlinear optical responses in van der Waals materials.
n993902559ccb: The growing demand for microwave absorbers in 5G/6G technologies motivates processing routes that balance matching thickness, attenuation, and temperature response. Here, magnetic field annealing (MFA) is investigated in rGO‐supported FeCoNi, FeCoNiCr, and FeCoNiCrCu compositionally complex alloys at 0, 0.5, and 0.95 T. Among the investigated FeCoNiCr samples, the 0.5 T sample exhibits a favorable combination of dielectric and magnetic responses. Reflection loss yields a minimum of −72.30 dB at 1.59 mm, and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 4.40 GHz. At 85°C, the maximum bandwidth is 4.08 GHz, corresponding to 92.7% retention of temperature‐specific maxima. Local microscopy, field‐associated atomistic modeling, and fixed‐composition electronic‐structure calculations support an interpretation of the electromagnetic response in terms of Co‐centered chemical correlations. Finally, flexible antennas and strain sensors based on this composite demonstrate stable wearable responses, validating this SRO strategy from atomic design to device integration.
n89ff613d8293: Integrated visible photonic engines for solid‐state quantum defects provide a foundation for scalable quantum networks. While miniaturization is advancing, active manipulation remains limited by the difficulty of achieving simultaneous milliwatt‐scale visible light generation and high‐contrast modulation. Despite extensive efforts, the concurrent chip‐scale realization of nonlinear frequency conversion and fast temporal gating for high‐fidelity quantum control has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate a monolithic thin‐film lithium niobate (TFLN) platform integrating periodically poled frequency conversion with GHz‐bandwidth electro‐optic (EO) switching. The device delivers off‐chip green‐light power exceeding 1 mW with an extinction ratio (ER) of 42.2 dB, enabling coherent spin control and time‐resolved lifetime measurements of individual nitrogen‐vacancy (NV) centers in diamond through nanosecond gating. System performance is validated through pulsed optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR), Rabi oscillations, and Ramsey interference, supported by time‐tagged photon counting with nanosecond resolution. By unifying sufficient nonlinear light generation with high‐speed active manipulation, this platform establishes a scalable framework for the realization of high‐rate quantum communication nodes.
nf4363554a3c0: Nonreciprocity reflects the asymmetric propagation or motion of an object in two opposite directions and can achieve directional transport in physics. However, nonreciprocity in natural quasi‐static mechanical systems, including nonreciprocal bending, has rarely been explored. Here we demonstrate nonreciprocal bending in a freestanding ferroelectric single‐crystalline PbTiO3 membrane using suspended‐membrane nanoindentation. The mechanical bending of the ferroelectric membrane is strongly asymmetric in the two opposite bending directions with a difference in effective elastic modulus of up to 33%. The elastic recovery of bending deformation also becomes polarity‐dependent. Such unconventional nonreciprocal bending originates from the asymmetric ferroelectric domain switching driven by the crucial flexoelectricity, as revealed by phase‐field simulations. This work enriches the nonreciprocal functionalities of ferroelectrics and presents a route for exploring more nonreciprocal effects by flexoelectric engineering.
n36bbfe21c9d5: Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 2D perovskites show great potential in stability but do not meet theoretical expectations for photovoltaics due to the random crystallographic orientation in films. We herein report ordered crystallographic orientation of the DJ 2D perovskite, achieved by modifying the intermediate‐phase film with a Ruddlesden‐Popper (RP) phase 2D perovskite based on the two‐step processing method. The introduction of the RP 2D perovskite lowers the energy barrier for the transition from the intermediate phase to the 2D perovskite phase with the ordered alignment, and this strategy is applicable to various organic diammoniums‐based DJ 2D perovskites. Solar cells with oriented DJ 2D perovskite films achieve an efficiency of 21.1% (19.05% for 1 cm2 devices) and exhibit outstanding stability by retaining 98.1% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking at 65°C under continuous 1‐sun illumination (ISOS‐L‐2 protocol) and 98.7% after 2500 h testing at a relative humidity of 85%.
n0c66e8980a95: The pursuit of noble metal‐free alternatives to iridium for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is critically impeded by a pervasive activity‐stability trade‐off, wherein non‐precious metals undergo rapid oxidative dissolution under operating potentials. Here, we report a lutetium‐stabilized cobalt oxide catalyst (Lu0.08Co2.92O4) designed through site‐specific electronic modulation, achieving a synergistic enhancement of both activity and stability in acidic OER for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Operando spectroscopies combined with theoretical simulations reveal that Lu incorporation introduces robust Lu‐O bonds and induces charge redistribution that strengthens Co‐O covalency and suppresses Co2+ dissolution, which is critical for improved OER durability, and simultaneously optimizes the Co‐Co distance to favor direct O‐O radical coupling with a reduced energy barrier. Leveraging these structural advantages, a practical PEMWE employing Lu0.08Co2.92O4 delivers an industrially relevant current density of 1000 mA cm−2 at 1.837 V. Separately, it maintains stable operation for over 900 h under a stepwise current density from 200 to 500 mA cm−2, highlighting its potential for sustainable hydrogen production.
n7c7b5c85abca: Globally, warmer lakes disrupt thermal balance, causing hypoxia, salinization, biodiversity loss, and increased evaporation. Conventional floating covers used to reduce evaporation absorb sunlight and warm the underlying water, limiting suppression efficiency to less than the coverage ratio (η eff /Φ ≤ 1). Here, we break this limit by developing Superhydrophobic Radiative Cooling Covers (SRCC) via multi-level structural design. SRCC actively cools the water surface by combining high solar reflectance, strong mid-infrared emission, and superhydrophobicity. Experiments show SRCC lowers water temperature by 2.2°C versus uncovered water, achieving 93.1± 0.1% evaporation suppression at 91% coverage, yielding η eff /Φ > 1.0 for the first time. Large‑scale simulations for nine Chinese lakes indicate that SRCC reduces water temperature by 4.87°C (vs. no cover) and by 12.44 °C (vs. black covers). This cooling could increase annual freshwater reserves by 10.78 km3 across China under full deployment, equivalent to 20.9 L per person per day. Unattainable with conventional covers, SRCC uniquely mitigates thermal accumulation while enhancing freshwater storage, providing a quantifiable engineering solution to climate‑driven water stress and enabling adaptive lake ecosystem management across regional and global scales.
nde086d75db1a: High-energy lithium metal batteries are promising for space, polar, deep-sea, and other extreme environments, but their operation is constrained by temperature-sensitive ion transport, Li+ solvation, and interfacial chemistry. A solvation-equilibrium-locked electrolyte (SELE) is reported by combining dimethyl sulfite (DMS), a low-freezing weakly solvating solvent, with Pyr13DFOB (1-methyl-1-propylpyrrolidinium difluoro(oxalato)borate) as an ionic-liquid co-solvent. Cooperative ion–dipole and weak C–H⋯O interactions between DMS and Pyr13 + regulate the free-solvent reservoir, while TFSI− (bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide) and DFOB− enrich the primary Li+ coordination shell. Variable-temperature 7Li NMR, Raman, and molecular dynamics simulations show that solvent-separated ion pairs, contact ion pairs, and aggregates remain nearly invariant from −60°C to 60°C, unlike the strongly temperature-responsive Pyr13DFOB-free electrolyte. This locked anion-rich solvation structure reduces solvent coordination around Li+, mitigates solvent-derived interfacial decomposition and gas evolution, and promotes LiF- and borate-rich interphases on Li metal and NMC811. Consequently, Li||NMC811 cells deliver discharge capacity at −85°C and operate up to 120°C, while pouch cells remain functional after cooling to −122.9°C. A 6.6 Ah Li||Ni90 pouch cell further achieves 565 Wh kg−1 under lean-electrolyte conditions, establishing solvation-equilibrium locking as a molecular design principle for lithium metal batteries operating over a broad temperature range.
n36e159024a2a: The multifocal nature of orthotopic breast tumors makes it difficult to treat due to individual tumor differences, requiring multiple therapeutic interventions. Here, a customized therapeutic strategy is presented for multiple tumors by using the same prescription based on a multi‐channel lanthanide nanocomposite and orthogonally controlled drug release. The upconversion luminescence of the nanocomposite at different wavelengths can monitor pH‐responsive mitoxantrone (MXT) release, reduced glutathione‐responsive near‐infrared (NIR) absorbance change, and eigen temperature, respectively, allowing modulation of photothermal treatment and temperature‐responsive paclitaxel release through customized whole‐body irradiation to achieve synchronized ablation of different individual tumors. Small animal experiments confirm multifocal breast tumors can be treated through this customized therapeutic strategy with both high efficiency and low overtherapy risk.
nd768807e63fc: We have synthesized layered superconducting LiNbO2 crystals through a bulk phase transformation from LiNbO3 single crystals via CaH2 reduction. As the Nb valence is reduced from 5+ to 3+, the material undergoes a structural transformation to the resulting product, LiNbO2, which is accompanied by metallic behavior and a superconducting transition, T c onset, as high as 14.4 K. Secondary ion mass spectroscopy (SIMS) and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) show that the resulting phase is hole-doped through de-lithiation during the reduction. Magnetization and AC susceptibility measurements from a tunnel diode resonator confirm the bulk nature of superconductivity with a superconducting volume fraction of ≈77% and an upper critical field approaching 26 T. Our study demonstrates extreme hydride reduction as an effective method to induce phase transformations with non-topochemical pathways and can be used to synthesize bulk materials with exotic properties.
n128ef9507713: Area‐type memristors are attractive for analog in‐memory computing, but their use is often limited by parasitic charge storage, causing readout drift, non‐pinched hysteresis, and degraded readout fidelity. We show that near‐ideal area‐type switching emerges within a tunneling‐governed transport regime in ultrathin layers that suppresses charging‐related readout artifacts. By varying the thickness in TiN/Ta2O5/Pt in a range of 3–10 nm, we reveal the transition from filamentary switching to near‐short‐circuit transport with two gradual‐switching modes with different readout stability. The 5–6 nm thickness window suppresses non‐pinched hysteresis and short‐time drift while preserving analog switching, yielding nearly polarity‐symmetric hysteresis and readout, clear area scaling, and continuous near‐linear conductance modulation. Our analysis indicates that trap‐assisted tunneling dominates the stabilized‐state response, whereas ionic redistribution governs pristine‐state reconstruction and the stability boundaries. A compact model is derived for the 5 nm device which reproduces the quasi‐static I–V behavior and the dynamic resistance evolution based on pulse‐width‐dependent characteristics. The verified model is provided as Verilog‐A code enabling simulation in circuit design tools. Our results demonstrate that ultrathin scaling is a regime‐defining design rule for near‐ideal area‐type operation in oxide memristors, implying a fundamental approach to fabricating robust multi‐state memristors for in‐memory computing applications.
neca4c2001f52: Rare‐earth permanent magnets (REPMs) are crucial for electric vehicles, wind turbines, and other high‐efficiency electric motor systems. However, their production is energy‐intensive, and global recycling rates are below 0.2%. Machining swarf is the main industrial waste from REPMs production. Despite its high rare‐earth elements (REEs) content (∼20 wt.%), it has received limited attention for sustainable recycling. We introduce hydrogen plasma reduction (HPR) as a new environmentally friendly method to recover REEs from REPM swarf. By tuning the hydrogen content and treatment time, we achieve phase separation into metallic Fe and a Nd2O3‐rich rare‐earth fraction, providing a concentrated intermediate for subsequent REPM production. The process also enables direct rare‐earth hydride formation, confirming the plasma‐assisted partial rare‐earth metallization in the molten state. This procedure turns REPM swarf into separated, high‐value, high‐purity feedstock in a single, acid‐free step. Against the ∼70 kg CO2‐eq kg−1 footprint of conventional REPM production, this recycling route offers a pathway toward substantially lower‐emission magnet production while reducing reliance on primary REE supply.
ne75f9b014521: Cathodes exploiting oxygen redox chemistry underpin the realization of lithium battery systems with specific energies beyond 600 Wh kg−1. However, voltage hysteresis exceeding 1 V, especially during the first cycle, remains a long‐standing and unresolved challenge, severely limiting energy efficiency and practical deployment. Here, we propose a quasi‐flat‐band framework in which oxygen 2p states near the Fermi level are intrinsically sensitive to perturbations. Even weak perturbations, such as minor lattice distortions during delithiation or thermal vibrations at room temperature, can disproportionately amplify band dispersion and induce hysteresis. This insight reframes the long‐standing design strategy by extending it beyond suppressing structural reconstructions to include control of perturbation‐driven electronic instability. Future materials design should pursue two principles: stabilizing symmetry to sustain quasi‐flat‐band characteristics and engineering orbital hybridization to enhance their robustness against perturbations. This work rethinks the origin and mitigation of voltage hysteresis, bringing oxygen‐redox cathodes closer to reliable operation at high voltages.
n406d611f880f: Persistent organic contaminants are increasingly accumulating in saline waters, where high ionic strength and complex electrolytes hinder oxidative remediation. Electrogenerated reactive oxygen species (ROS) offer a promising route for pollutant degradation, yet the role of electrolyte cations in controlling ROS pathways remains poorly understood. Although singlet oxygen (1O2) is more persistent and matrix‐tolerant than hydroxyl radicals (•OH), whether cation‐induced changes in interfacial water structure govern ROS selectivity remains unclear. Here, using atomically dispersed Cu on Fe2O3‐carbon nanotubes (Cu1/Fe2O3‐CNTs) as a dual‐ROS electrocatalyst, we show that alkali‐metal cations exert distinct effects on ROS generation. •OH production follows the expected cation‐size‐dependent trend, whereas 1O2 generation exhibits an anomalous maximum in Na+‐containing electrolytes, leading to superior contaminant degradation. Quantitative ROS measurements, in situ electrochemical analysis, spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations show that this behavior is primarily governed by selective stabilization of the *OOH intermediate rather than enhanced O2 adsorption. Na+ promotes a highly interconnected interfacial hydrogen‐bond network that stabilizes *OOH and favors 1O2 formation. In natural seawater, this regulation enables >98.2% contaminant removal within 8 h at an estimated energy demand of 0.779 kWh m−3. These findings identify electrolyte cations as important regulators of ROS selectivity and provide a basis for efficient saline‐water decontamination.
n238ed126d7df: Solar‐driven H2O2 photosynthesis offers a sustainable route to on‐site oxidant production, yet the selective reduction of triplet O2 to spin‐paired H2O2 remains kinetically challenging. Covalent organic framework (COF) photocatalysts have largely focused on charge separation and active‐site reactivity, while overlooking the spin character of electrons transferred to O2. Here we discover that chiralization renders COFs significantly enhanced production of H2O2, and report a chiralization strategy for spin‐regulated H2O2 photosynthesis in β‐ketoenamine‐linked COFs. The chiral frameworks enable spin‐selective electron transport, favor the O–O‐bond‐preserving reduction pathway and lower the apparent kinetic barrier for H2O2 formation. Chiralization enhances H2O2 production by 38.7%–252.1% relative to achiral counterparts. A bipyridine‐containing chiral COF reaches 22.8 mmol g−1 h−1 using solely water and oxygen, with an apparent quantum yield of 10.3% at 420 nm, placing it at the forefront of sacrificial‐agent‐free COF systems. Membrane‐integrated chiral COFs enable continuous‐flow H2O2 production. These findings establish chirality as a design parameter coupling spin‐selective electron transport with O2 reduction pathway control, opening new directions for COF photocatalysis.
ne31b297914b4: Crystallographic orientation governs Zn deposition, dissolution, and cycling stability, but its influence on interfacial charge-transfer kinetics remains difficult to quantify. Here, scanning electrochemical cell microscopy coupled with fast scan cyclic voltammetry (FSCV) is used to resolve Zn plating and stripping on single-crystal (002), (100), and (101) surfaces. Meniscus-confined measurements reveal facet-dependent branch-specific apparent zero-current potentials and apparent exchange current densities, j 0, with the kinetic ordering j 0(100) > j 0(101) > j 0(002) for both plating and stripping. This ordering is reproduced across independently prepared electrodes and retained over different scan rates and aqueous electrolytes. Beyond charge transfer, Zn removal and regrowth are strongly crystallographically encoded: dissolution footprints preserve the symmetry of the parent facets, while potentiostatically deposited Zn adopts substrate-dependent growth geometries. These coupled kinetic and morphological differences translate directly to battery performance. Despite its slower apparent kinetics, the close-packed, low-energy (002) facet exhibits the longest cycling life in Zn/Zn symmetric cells and substantially improved capacity retention in both polyaniline/Zn and Na0.33V2O5/Zn full cells, whereas the faster (100) and (101) interfaces fail earlier. These findings establish a facet-dependent kinetics–stability trade-off and show that durable Zn anodes require coordinated control of charge transfer, dissolution topology, and crystallographic reconstruction.
na70c1b95a55c: Developing highly efficient long‐wavelength exciplexes remains a challenge due to the constraints of the energy gap law and severe non‐radiative loss. In this study, we report a rigid nitrogen‐rich donor, 3N, featuring the first fused framework constructed from two anti‐aromatic phenazine units. This unique architecture ensures 3N has good planarity and an exceptionally shallow highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level of −4.88 eV. Meanwhile, the effective suppression of structural relaxation by its rigid scaffold contributes to a narrow emission at 456 nm. By pairing 3N with planar boron‐containing acceptors through strong intermolecular interactions, highly efficient exciplex emissions ranging from green to orange‐red were successfully achieved. Two representative exciplex systems reached outstanding photoluminescence quantum yields of 92% at 557 nm and 78% at 604 nm, respectively. Correspondingly, organic light‐emitting diodes based on these exciplexes delivered maximum external quantum efficiencies of 25.6% at 556 nm and 24.7% at 586 nm, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, these values rank among the highest performance metrics reported for long‐wavelength exciplexes. These results demonstrate that fusing multiple phenazine units could significantly raise the HOMO level and enhances structural rigidity, thereby enabling highly efficient long‐wavelength exciplex electroluminescence.
n35683bae8a9a: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is a crucial environmentally benign oxidant. Photoanodes in bias‐free photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems suffer from poor H2O2 selectivity at low potentials, limiting the efficiency of bipolar H2O2 production. Herein, we report a rare‐earth ytterbium oxide (YbOx) modified BiVO4/WO3 photoanode for efficient PEC water oxidation to H2O2. The optimized photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 4.83 mA cm−2 at 1.23 VRHE, an H2O2 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of over 80% across the potential range of 0.6–1.8 VRHE, and a peak FE of 90.4% at 1.6 VRHE. Yb3+ Lewis acid sites suppress the competitive four‐electron oxygen evolution reaction by forming Yb‐hydroxyl complexes, while YbOx enhances charge transfer and reduces interfacial resistance. Importantly, when coupled with a FeZnWMnYb high‐entropy amorphous oxide cathode for the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction, the bias‐free tandem cell achieves ∼160% bipolar H2O2 FE. Scaling the photoelectrode to 20 cm2 under 0.7 suns illumination yields an H2O2 production rate of 3.03 mmol L−1 h−1. This work demonstrates a viable strategy for large‐scale solar‐driven H2O2 synthesis for environmental applications.
nd05a4bac5ca4: Simultaneous detection of protein and nucleic acid (NA) provides complementary information essential for accurate analysis of complex samples. Conventional approaches for the analysis of protein and NA typically rely on separate workflows and instruments, limiting the reliability of point‐of‐care testing. Here, we present a digital microfluidics‐based dual‐mode molecular assay for simultaneous detection of both protein and NA from the same microscale sample. The protein is captured by a gold nanoparticle–antibody conjugate, while NA is enriched by magnetic beads. Magnetic manipulation separates the protein‐containing fraction from NA, enabling separate analysis of the two molecular classes within an automated workflow. By integrating the analysis of protein and NA, the platform enables more accurate analysis than either modality alone. In 56 clinical samples, the combined analysis of hepatitis B surface antigen and DNA reduces the false‐negative rate to 1.79%, compared with 12.5% for HBsAg alone. In food safety assays, simultaneous detection of Staphylococcus aureus‐associated toxins and PMA‐treated bacterial NA provides information not only on protein‐based toxins, but also the presence and viability of bacteria within milk. This automated DMF‐based dual‐mode molecular assay provides a highly integrated strategy for multimodal POCT and public health risk assessment.
n02826f075517: Near‐infrared (NIR) light‐driven single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal (SCSC) transformation holds profound significance for supramolecular chemistry and smart materials, yet remains a formidable challenge in purely organic molecular crystals. Herein, we demonstrate SCSC transformation driven by the intrinsic NIR photothermal effect of a rationally designed croconium derivative CR‐DPA‐OMe, which features strong NIR absorption and a high photothermal conversion efficiency of 60%. Solvated CR‐DPA‐OMe single crystals encapsulating CHCl3 molecules exhibit exceptional ambient stability with crystallinity preserved for over two years. Benefiting from the robust dimeric packing of croconium motifs and the conformationally flexible methoxy‐substituted diphenylamine moieties, the resulting crystals successfully reconcile long‐range lattice order with structural flexibility, thus enabling efficient SCSC transformation upon NIR photothermal stimulation. Combined density functional theory (DFT) calculations and in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction analysis confirm that the transformation is driven by the synergistic interplay of photoinduced molecular conformational reorganization and photothermally‐converted heat, affording markedly faster transformation than conventional oven heating. Furthermore, tailored NIR irradiation enables spatiotemporally programmable guest release, demonstrating a remote manipulation inaccessible via macroscopic conductive heating. These findings highlight the substantial promise of NIR photothermal modulation as an emerging stimuli‐responsive strategy for precise structural engineering in molecular crystals, opening new avenues toward tailored functional material applications.
n0a729aec98d2: The separation of linear and branched alkanes is critically important for improving the research octane number (RON) and advancing the sustainable development of the petrochemical industry. However, owing to their nearly identical kinetic diameters and closely related physicochemical properties (e.g., solubility parameters and boiling points), membrane‐based liquid‐phase separation of such linear and branched alkanes remains highly challenging. An example is the n‐heptane/iso‐octane pair, which exhibits minimal differences in molecular size and physicochemical properties but a dramatic difference in RON. Herein, we report a conjugated‐polymer‐framework (CPF) membrane that enables molecular‐level separation of linear and branched alkanes. The crystallized selective layer of CPF membrane features intrinsic sub‐nanometer pores of ∼5.5 and 8.4 Å. With ethanol as an assisting agent, the membrane achieves a separation factor of 5.24 for n‐heptane/iso‐octane mixture, together with a total mixture permeance of 0.020 kg m−2 h−1 bar−1. This pronounced selectivity stems from ethanol‐induced modulation of transmembrane transport, which selectively mitigates the transport barrier of linear alkanes while exerting negligible influence on their branched counterparts, thereby enhancing kinetic selectivity. Furthermore, the CPF membrane exhibits robust separation performance over extended operation and across a wide range of feed compositions and pressures, highlighting its robustness for linear/branched alkane separation.
n4ed998b08a17: Solvent arguably constitutes the single largest waste stream in synthesis. Mechanophotocatalysis, a synergistic union of mechanochemistry and photocatalysis, offers a solution to significantly reduce solvent use in photochemistry. Here, we show how photochemical reactions in the solid state can be driven by visible light using in situ formed electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes in air, obviating the need for an external photocatalyst. Under the optimized conditions, only 2–4 equiv. of solvent is used as a liquid‐assisted grinding (LAG) agent, thus significantly reducing solvent use. We demonstrate EDA mechanophotochemistry across five reactions: a Giese reaction; a C─S cross‐coupling reaction; a phosphorylation reaction; a sulfonylation reaction; and a Povarov reaction. While the first four proceeded readily and competitively with the solution‐state EDA photochemical reaction, the latter one, requiring O2 as a terminal oxidant, does not. In investigating the sulfonylation reaction we further identify the first example of a photomechanoredox reaction in which the stainless‐steel milling ball directly participates in the reaction, revealing the milling medium as a previously unrecognized reactivity parameter. Together, these results establish visible light‐promoted mechanophotochemistry as a solvent‐minimized and viable alternative to solution‐state photochemical reactions.
nd218b67b54f2: Catalytic oxidative cancer therapy exploits elevated hydrogen peroxide levels within tumor microenvironments to induce selective oxidative damage in malignant cells. However, many ROS‐generating therapeutic systems rely on heavy metals or structurally complex inorganic architectures, limiting their biological compatibility and catalytic selectivity. Inspired by nonheme iron‐mediated redox catalysis, we report a series of water‐soluble biomimetic first‐row transition metal complexes supported by a picolylamine‐derived nonheme ligand scaffold bearing a pendant hydroxyl group. Systematic variation of the metal center (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Zn) generated divergent electrochemical behavior and distinct peroxide‐activation reactivity, yet only the iron complex, [Fe(N2Py3OH)]2+ (1‐Fe), promoted hydroxyl radical formation via Fenton‐like hydrogen peroxide activation in water. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and crystallographic analyses revealed a biomimetic coordination environment that stabilizes a quasi‐reversible Fe(II)/Fe(III) redox couple suited to catalytic peroxide activation. In gastric cancer cells, 1‐Fe induced intracellular oxidative stress, mitochondrial depolarization, lipid peroxidation, and concomitant apoptosis and ferroptosis, while exhibiting negligible toxicity toward normal fibroblasts. In combination with paclitaxel, 1‐Fe produced synergistic antiproliferative activity in vitro and suppressed peritoneal tumor dissemination in vivo without overt systemic toxicity. Collectively, these results establish biomimetic iron complexes as molecular platforms for Fenton‐like oxidative catalysis in redox‐based cancer therapy.
nafbfef21b7d0: Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) represents the most common solvent for dispersing hydrophobic materials in aqueous solutions for biological usage. Generally, a DMSO content of below 1% is believed to exert no effect on cells, and thus little attention is given to its influence on drug efficacy. During our recent research on a lipid droplet‐targeted photosensitizer, PNA‐9, we notice the drastic influence of low‐concentration DMSO (<1%) on its photodynamic therapy (PDT) performance. In‐depth investigations reveal the significant role of low‐concentration DMSO on PNA‐9 particle size, which further affects cellular uptake via passive diffusion and results in a drastic PDT effect. The results uncover the differential influences of low‐concentration DMSO: camptothecin (CPT) and TPE‐IQ possess similar DMSO effects, whilst the therapy effects of paclitaxel (PCT), bortezomib (BTZ), and DTTPB are not obviously influenced. nd95c8a99d118: Charge‐transport layers fundamentally dictate interfacial recombination, carrier extraction, and operational stability in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet scalable routes to simultaneously regulate their colloidal stability and defect chemistry remain elusive. n5f1cf5d62769: Programmed supramolecular confinement is introduced as a physical strategy to investigate aggregation‐enhanced reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation in twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT)‐active twisted photosensitizers without changing the conjugated photosensitizing unit. nce64cdcd4499: Polymer solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries are constrained by sluggish Na+ migration and unstable sodium–metal interfaces, both of which are closely associated with poorly regulated solvation chemistry. ne8f3776dd295: The catalytic asymmetric synthesis of chiral molecules containing both silicon‐ and phosphorus‐stereogenic centers represents a highly attractive yet underexplored domain in synthetic chemistry, largely due to the considerable challenge associated with the simultaneous control of two distinct stereogenic elements. na6232eeab159: Metal chalcohalides, an emerging class of mixed-anion compounds, have recently garnered increasing interest as they unite the exceptional stability of metal chalcogenides with the versatile electronic tunability of metal halides. nde05c8fc9cf6: The chlor-alkali industry, with the chlorine evolution reaction (CER) as its core anodic process, accounts for nearly 4% of global electricity consumption. nae349e85fe17: Redox-conductive metal-organic frameworks (RC-MOFs) combine molecularly tunable redox chemistry with crystalline, porous architectures. n3f9ff6cc68a9: Two-dimensional infrared (2DIR) spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for probing the structure and picosecond dynamics of complex, condensed-phase systems at the molecular level. This review highlights seminal and recent advances in understanding the behavior of these systems using 2DIR spectroscopy, with particular emphasis on spectral diffusion, vibrational relaxation, and chemical exchange dynamics. The review also describes how complementary information from the vibrational modes of solvents, salts, and external probes enables detailed characterization of ion–ion interactions, hydrogen-bonding networks, and solvation environments, providing a molecular framework of the structure and time evolution of these charged systems. Moreover, particular attention is given to the dynamics of distinct molecular moieties and to the role of specific anions, cations, and solvent environments in governing behavior on femtosecond to picosecond time scales. Finally, the review describes current challenges, including the limited availability of intrinsic vibrational reporters and experimental constraints, and key open questions in electrochemical and energy-relevant systems that remain despite an extensive number of studies in the area.
ne76deac1490b: This review offers a unified view of large-scale first-principles electronic-structure algorithms through the tension between locality and global quantum constraints. It also highlights stochastic methods, AI, and advanced-computing paradigms.

n0204b953e2c2: The incorporation of noble metals into iron oxide nanomaterials represents an effective strategy to tailor their redox and structural properties through metal-oxide interactions. nc5a177fd0583: Terrestrial electrochemical design implicitly relies on Earth-bound physics, such as gravity and natural convection. nb5ff9d360902: Confinement within nanoscale cavities can profoundly alter molecular structure and electronic properties, but this strategy has never been applied to inherently linear and symmetric uranyl cations (UO22+). nf810a78cface: Catalytic asymmetric electrophilic alkene functionalization provides a powerful strategy for the construction of complex chiral molecules. In this approach, for 1,6-dienes bearing bulky sulfonamide or quaternary carbon linkers, one double bond of the substrate interacts with an external electrophile, such as a trifluoromethylthio, arylthio, alkylthio, or chlorine species, generating an electrophilic carbon species that promotes the transformation of 1,6-dienes under chiral indane-based chalcogenide catalysis. Notably, the reaction can be terminated by intramolecular nucleophiles via cis-addition or can be captured by various intermolecular nucleophiles. A diverse array of optically pure polycyclic and monocyclic compounds can be obtained, including 5-5-6 tricyclic N-heterocycles and pentasubstituted chiral cyclohexanes. The same strategy can also be efficiently applied to 6-endo cyclizations, leading to the formation of 6-6-6 tricyclic and monocyclic N-heterocycles. The resulting products can be readily converted to various other valuable compounds, further demonstrating the utility of this methodology. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to rationalize the observed selectivities, revealing that the preferential transition-state conformations lower the activation barriers for the desired cyclization pathways. This work offers a versatile platform for the synthesis of enantioenriched chiral scaffolds prevalent in bioactive molecules and pharmaceuticals, significantly expanding the scope of polyene cyclization chemistry.
n470bc9cf92ec: Metal oxyhalides are versatile materials, exhibiting properties relevant to photocatalysis, solid-state battery systems, ferromagnetism, multiferroics, and nonlinear optics. Density functional theory combined with Bader charge analysis shows that preferred stacking sequences are those that minimize charge disproportionation across distinct chlorine environments, consistent with Pauling’s fifth rule, and we support this bonding-based framework through computational cation substitution that shifts the ionic-covalent balance of the metal–chloride bonding. Density functional theory calculations reveal that intergrowth formation destabilizes the O-2p orbitals, raising the valence band maximum for visible-light absorption, with the lone-pair interaction and layering-driven internal electrostatic field acting as competing effects on the resulting band gap. Significantly, this experimental-computational study establishes a transferable, bonding-based framework for stacking-sequence stability in layered oxyhalide intergrowths, while also clarifying how the same structural levers used to control stability can be tuned to engineer band structure.
na9e04b79a058: Photolabile linkers (PLLs) enable spatiotemporal control over substrate release but often suffer from slow photorelease kinetics, low quantum yields, or limited functionalization options. Six heterobifunctional NQMP-based linkers bearing terminal acetylene, cyclooctyne, amine, carboxyl, allyl, and biotin groups were synthesized and employed for the immobilization of fluorescent dyes, acetylsalicylic acid, biotin, avidin, and doxorubicin on silica microspheres and mesoporous silica nanoparticles. Mild UV-A irradiation resulted in efficient release of the attached payloads while preserving the integrity of the solid support. Mesoporous silica nanoparticles provide high loading capacity and are suitable for light-controlled drug delivery. The modular design, excellent photochemical efficiency, orthogonal conjugation chemistries, and compatibility with diverse substrates make NQMP-based PLLs versatile tools for reversible surface functionalization, controlled cargo release, affinity capture, and photoresponsive drug delivery applications.
ne142938bdece: We report that the Na+ ion within the calcium–sodium–calcium (Ca–Na–Ca) metal triad in two thermostable bacterial α-amylases (ca. 58 kDa) can be directly detected by 23Na (I = 3/2) quadrupole-central-transition (QCT) NMR spectroscopy in aqueous solution. We also use 23Na QCT NMR to monitor EDTA titration experiments, which yielded the apparent binding constants of the Na+ ion to BAA and BLA to be (0.3 ± 0.1) × 109 and (0.6 ± 0.1) × 109 M–1, respectively. This work represents the first time that Na+ ions tightly bound to an enzyme are directly observed by 23Na QCT NMR in aqueous solution. This new 23Na QCT NMR approach can potentially be extended to detection of other metal ions with quadrupolar nuclei such as K+, Mg2+, and Zn2+ in metalloenzymes in their native aqueous environment.
n4b41cf1c5b90: Baromagnetic effect (BME), arising from pressure-induced spin reorientation, holds great potential for next-generation information technologies owing to its strong multifield coupling characteristics. Temperature-dependent neutron powder diffraction (NPD) measurements reveal a clear evolution from the nearly collinear antiferromagnetic (cAFM) configuration with k = (1/2, 1/2, 1/2) to the ferromagnetic (FM) configuration, indicating that the spins are highly susceptible to reorientation under external perturbations. This demonstration establishes spin engineering, achieved through precise control of spin configurations via targeted element selection, as an effective strategy for realizing high-performance baromagnetic systems. n9fa0c41cd7c5: Although group theory is widely used to analyze symmetry and electronic transition selection rules in condensed matter physics and coordination chemistry, its use as a predictive design tool for organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) remains largely unexplored. This targeted structural modification reorganizes the frontier orbital symmetry, converting the lowest-energy transition from symmetry-forbidden to dipole-allowed, while preserving the rigid, highly symmetric molecular framework and suppressing excited-state structural relaxation and vibronic coupling. The resulting cis-I2A2 derivatives exhibit high photoluminescence quantum yields (ΦPL) of 70–99% and narrow emission bandwidths with full-widths at half-maximum (fwhm’s) of 20–32 nm. This work establishes orbital-symmetry engineering as a rational strategy for decoupling orbital symmetry from overall molecular symmetry, providing a general approach to transforming intrinsically weak luminophores into efficient narrowband emitters.
n9edd83b6ff48: Single-molecule reactions reveal intrinsic heterogeneity that is obscured in ensemble measurements. This coordinated control enables single-molecule reactions to be actively regulated under conventional solution volumes and reaction concentrations. By coupling individual reaction events to single-photon emission through electrogenerated chemiluminescence (ECL), we can directly count and image the reactions. Using this approach, individual Au nanoparticles were imaged over a broad potential range, and particles as small as 5 nm were distinguished from the substrate background. nbbc8c425d33b: Weak interlayer coupling, originating from electron interactions of adjacent layers, can provide promising prospects for two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), which can be respectively evaluated by energy criteria qualitatively and by band-gap transformation and band-shifting ratios quantitatively. nd0b03b2e60f4: Point defects govern the properties of complex oxides, yet they are hard to control precisely. nfd4943dedbf3: Precise control of solution aggregation enables flexible organic photodiodes processed from sustainable solvents to combine high detectivity with strong mechanical durability. By slowing rapid nucleation and improving film formation, this approach reduces trap formation and structural defects, offering a practical route toward sustainably manufactured wearable optoelectronics.
n2cd7ecd258a8: All-optical generation of pure spin current─the flow of spin in the absence of a corresponding charge flow─relies on symmetry based compensation between the two spin channels. 2D d-wave altermagnets, which in many respects are ideal spintronic materials due to their very low spin–orbit coupling, possess a magnetic point group and highly anisotropic valley manifolds that would appear to preclude such current compensation, excluding them as materials for the ultrafast generation of pure spin current. These results provide a practical and all-optical route to the generation of pure spin current in 2D d-wave altermagnets, opening a path to lightwave control of spin in an environment with very low intrinsic spin–orbit coupling.
na215a4fdde39: Atomic-level insight into structure, charge distribution, chemistry, and electronic states is essential for understanding emergent properties at oxide interfaces. This work not only resolves long-standing ambiguities regarding oxide interfacial conductivity but also provides a robust, transferable framework for related material systems.
n4dda93323b2f: Interfacial charge transfer in van der Waals heterostructures provides a powerful, contact-free mechanism to activate two-dimensional plasmons.
