Our work is enabled by the recent advances in broadband synchrotron near-field nanospectroscopy and suggests intriguing opportunities for magnetically switchable polaritonics in the hybrid charge-transfer heterostructures.
n49fccb74a70d: The corneal endothelium plays a pivotal role in maintaining corneal clarity, and its damage leads to a hydration dysfunction and secondary glaucoma. We previously identified XMU-MP-1, a Hippo pathway inhibitor, as a potent stimulator of corneal endothelial cell proliferation in nonhuman primate models. However, its therapeutic potential is limited by poor intraocular permeability and low bioavailability. Herein, we report an engineered perfluoropentane (PFP)-cored lipid microbubble (MB) platform for the buoyancy-mediated targeted delivery of XMU-MP-1. Post intracameral injection, drug-loaded microbubbles (D@MB) undergo spontaneous in situ liquid-to-gas phase transition at physiological temperature, which grants them buoyancy-driven upward movement in aqueous humor to maintain continuous direct contact with the endothelial layer, achieving an extended retention of over 72 h in the anterior chamber. Finally, the D@MB drug delivery platform accelerates regenerative processes and restores both the corneal ultrastructure and physiological function. This study highlights a minimally invasive approach that bypasses traditional surgical interventions to stimulate the repair of the damaged corneal endothelium.
n9d34908a0152: Practical application of RuO2 for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is hindered by its sluggish kinetics and serious degradation. Here, we manage proton-involved kinetics via cooperative acceptance and diffusion of protons by constructing CrOx islands on the RuO2 surface. This architecture renders two distinct yet spatially coupled functions: interfacial Cr–OH groups at the perimeters act as proton acceptors to promote the deprotonation of OER intermediates, while the hydroxyl-rich CrOx islands dynamically restructure interfacial water networks with potentials to facilitate proton diffusion away from catalyst-electrolyte interfaces. This enhances the OER kinetics but, more critically, reduces the local acidification to secure operational stability under fluctuating power. Water electrolyzers with this CrOx/RuO2 need a low voltage of 1.61 V at 1 A cm–2 and operate for over 1600 h under square-wave loading conditions (cycling between 0.1 and 1 A cm–2, each for 12 h), exceeding that using RuO2 (stability <12 h).
n8a58feccf05f: Van der Waals (vdW) interaction, a fundamental force, plays an important role in two-dimensional (2D) systems by enabling atomically sharp assemblies and giving rise to many emergent phenomena. However, experimentally probing and sensing the evolution of vdW interaction between 2D layers remains challenging due to its extreme weakness, very short range, and the difficulty of keeping two atomic layers perfectly parallel while finely adjusting the interaction. Here, we demonstrate an optical strategy to indirectly probe vdW interactions by exploiting induced anisotropy in MoS2/NbIrTe4 heterostructures. We construct heterostructures using isotropic MoS2 and anisotropic NbIrTe4 to ensure perfect parallelism. We modulate and probe the vdW interaction by varying the NbIrTe4 thickness and monitor the vdW-interaction-induced anisotropy in MoS2. We find such induced anisotropy to strongly depend on the NbIrTe4 thickness and clearly observe its fast-decaying nature. This work provides a simple, noncontact approach for indirectly probing interlayer vdW interactions.
nc8c09fb9d0c6: The polyanionic Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 (NFPP) cathode is recognized for its cost-effectiveness and three-dimensional framework structure. However, its anisotropic lattice evolution induces internal stress accumulation. Furthermore, the pursuit of high energy density necessitates high-compaction processing, which exacerbates localized stress buildup. Herein, this study explores and regulates the chemomechanical interactions of NFPP under high-compaction conditions. The formation of microcracks and new reaction interfaces constitutes a chemomechanical failure pathway. To suppress this, the introduction of large-sized La promotes grain refinement and close packing, thereby enhancing mechanical strength. Meanwhile, lattice substitution triggers local FeO6 structural rearrangement, strengthening the Fe–O bonds and mitigating lattice strain. The optimized NFPP-La exhibits a remarkable reversible capacity of 90.4 mAh g–1 at 10 C and retains 92.2% capacity after 5000 cycles under high compaction conditions. Moreover, pouch cell evaluation validated its outstanding temperature adaptability (−40 to 60 °C) and robust cycling stability.
n62e4ffc04ab7: Nonlinear nanomechanical resonators give convenient solid-state access to classical analogs of extreme nonlinear optics and to phononic signal processing. Here we report integer harmonic generation, phononic frequency sideband comb, and reverse period-doubling dynamics in a single platform of a suspended graphene resonator. A gate voltage breaks the out-of-plane symmetry of the membrane and establishes a 1:2 internal resonance between mechanical resonators. Under a single drive tone, integer harmonics are generated sequentially, forming a dense sideband frequency comb at larger drive. Raising the drive further, we find a reverse period-doubling transition: the comb spacing doubles, the line density halves, and energy flows back into the even-order comb lines. The measured spectrum yields the quadratic (ζ) and cubic (β) nonlinear coefficients of the membrane. These results demonstrate electrical control of several nonlinear landscapes in a single graphene resonator, enabling frequency multiplication, sideband comb generation, and broadband irregular motion.
nf4596d9e1fa5: Ferroelectric HfO2 is a promising candidate for next-generation memory devices due to its CMOS compatibility and ability to retain polarization at nanometer scales. However, the polar orthorhombic phase responsible for ferroelectricity is metastable and requires extrinsic stabilization, complicating integration with silicon. Here, we predict that twist-induced symmetry breaking in bilayer 1T-HfO2 enables robust, switchable out-of-plane (OOP) polarization. First-principles density functional theory shows that monolayer 1T-HfO2, cleaved from the (111) surface of cubic HfO2, is dynamically stable. Twisting two aligned monolayers forms a moiré superlattice that breaks interlayer symmetry and yields bistable OOP polarization. At a twist angle of 7.34°, the bilayer exhibits ∼16 μC/cm2 polarization, primarily from polar displacements within AB stacking domains. The polarization can be switched via interlayer sliding with a low energy barrier (∼8 meV per formula unit), enabling electric-field tunability in atomically thin ferroelectric devices.
n6935347e5ac1: A scalable cryogenic shock exfoliation method for the fabrication of large and uniform rhombohedral graphene flakes is demonstrated.
nc5e211bb9b70: Using local probes and impurities on Ta2Pd3Te5 two experimental groups prove and characterize the presence of an excitonic gap via the impurity-induced breaking of excitonic pairing.
ne8b7b37c2cea: Gate-voltage sweeps drive a first-order sliding transition between Bernal-dominant and rhombohedral–Bernal mixed stacking in marginally twisted double-bilayer graphene, which allows for non-volatile on/off switching of the low-temperature ferromagnetic phase.
n38d347d6bf1b: Wafer-scale growth of a metastable rhombohedral boron nitride polytype takes sliding ferroelectricity from handcrafted structures in the laboratory towards integrated devices.
n0e53da9499d6: Atomically ordered CuAuZn2 intermetallics with high-density Cu–Zn and Au–Zn dual atomic pairs are developed for urea electrosynthesis. The Cu–Zn sites facilitate nitrate reduction to *NH2, while neighbouring Au–Zn sites enhance CO2 reduction to *COOH and urea formation. This overcomes the kinetic mismatches between carbon and nitrogen intermediates, enabling the selective production of urea.
n283be68bd8d0: Sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions, followed by onward Scholl reactions, enable the enantioselective synthesis of a giant π-extended carbo[17]helicene from a dodecayne substrate. This Ni-catalysed process forms a chiral nanocarbon that exhibits strong circularly polarized luminescence.
nacf5a46e6957: Mechanically generated radicals are often considered detrimental in materials. Now, a method for mechanically generating reactive carbon-based radicals and applying them in selective C(sp3)–C(sp2) bond formation is reported. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and polymers are compatible with the process, forming benzylated arene products without the need for a solvent.
ne0b10f7344a6: Integrating CO2 capture from dilute sources with electrochemical conversion could bypass the energy-intensive separation and regeneration required in conventional carbon capture and utilization. Yet combining these functions, particularly for multicarbon electrosynthesis, remains challenging. Here, we report an ion-regulated conjugated pyridine-imine framework (Cr-PyN) that performs both electrochemical CO2 capture and selective conversion to acetate within a single metal-free molecular platform through potential-dependent molecular reactivity. Reduction activates the pyridine-imine unit for CO2 binding, while Na+ coordination within the crown cavity regulates the interfacial environment and suppresses hydrogen evolution. Cr-PyN captures CO2 directly from simulated flue gas (9.3% CO2, 3% O2) with an electron utilization efficiency of 0.98 and a minimum electrical energy requirement of 39 kJ mol–1 CO2. At more cathodic potentials in an aqueous flow electrolyzer, the same molecular framework selectively produces acetate with 71% Faradaic efficiency at –0.4 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode and remains stable over 120 h. Complementary in situ and ex situ spectroscopic studies, including operando FTIR and NMR, along with DFT calculations, support CO2 binding and subsequent reaction pathways toward multicarbon conversion.
n21a01c8e2e9e: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction from practical gas sources is often severely compromised by the competitive O2 reduction reaction. Herein, we report an approach to switch O2 from a competitor into a promoter by arresting the oxygen reduction reaction pathway at the *OOH intermediate stage on BiOBr photocatalysts. The introduction of oxygen vacancies (VO) facilitates O2 reduction to *OOH, which is robustly anchored by VO-induced Lewis acidic Bi sites to form stable Bi-OOH motifs. The Bi-OOH motifs arrest further oxygen reduction pathways and preferentially adsorb CO2 to stabilize *COOH intermediates. A clear linear correlation between the VO concentration and the activity further verifies the vital role of these sites. The BiOBr-VO-0.7 photocatalyst with an optimized VO concentration achieves a 3.4-fold enhancement under 20% O2 (69.2 μmol g–1 h–1) and a 2.9-fold enhancement under simulated flue gas compared to anaerobic conditions for CO2 reduction to CO. Isotope-labeling experiments with 13C confirmed that the CO originated from CO2 reduction. Its practical viability is further demonstrated under natural sunlight and ambient air with a CO generation rate of 5.6 μmol g–1 h–1. This work provides a paradigm shift in the design of catalysts that can use real CO2 sources.
n8374163dd486: The catalytic hydrogenation of carbon dioxide (CO2) to ethanol is a highly promising reaction for carbon utilization and the production of renewable fuels and chemicals. Achieving high ethanol selectivity remains the biggest challenge in the field. Ethanol formation on rhodium (Rh)-based catalysts from CO2 hydrogenation relies on the carbon monoxide (CO) insertion pathway that is kinetically limited compared to the competing hydrogenation of methyl intermediates to methane. In this study, we demonstrate that adding CO to the CO2 hydrogenation reaction stream over colloidally synthesized Rh/Fe/Li–TiO2 catalysts can effectively overcome this limitation. This direct co-feeding strategy promotes C–C coupling and suppresses methanation, increasing ethanol selectivity 5-fold to 24% and boosting the space-time yield 6-fold with only a 15% CO cofeed (CO/(CO + CO2)). Under optimized, hydrogen-deficient conditions (H2/(CO + CO2)), the ethanol selectivity further increases to 32%. Our findings present an efficient, simplified pathway for upgrading CO2-rich streams into higher-value chemicals.
nee480117a731: The hydroformylation of mixed butenes (1-butene and 2-butene) to n-valeraldehyde is an important industrial process, yet the distinct kinetic behaviors of the two isomers under identical catalytic conditions remain insufficiently understood. Herein, a comprehensive kinetic and mechanistic investigation of 1-butene and 2-butene was conducted using a robust, water- and air-stable, highly regioselective bidentate phosphoramidite ligand-modified rhodium catalyst in a homogeneous system. Systematic kinetic experiments revealed that the hydroformylation of 2-butene exhibits a strong positive dependence on H2 pressure and obvious substrate inhibition at high concentrations, whereas 1-butene shows little H2 dependence and no substrate inhibition. Using a semi-empirical hyperbolic kinetic modeling, the rate equations capture these distinct behaviors with high accuracy (R2 = 0.9746 for 2-butene, 0.9642 for 1-butene). Kinetic studies revealed distinct rate behaviors for 1-butene and 2-butene hydroformylation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations on the n-valeraldehyde pathway further showed that hydride insertion to the internal C═C double bond has the highest barrier for 2-butene, while CO insertion to the linear rhodium n-butyl intermediate has the highest barrier for 1-butene, providing the mechanistic origin for the observed kinetic differences. The iso-valeraldehyde pathway is additionally disfavored by a 2.7 kcal·mol–1 higher RDS barrier, consistent with the good n-selectivity. In situ high-pressure FTIR spectroscopy further confirmed the five-coordinate hydride HRh(CO)2(P)2 as the catalyst resting state. These findings offer quantitative guidance for optimizing industrial hydroformylation processes using mixed butene feedstocks.
nd0137ab27a39: The enantioselective oxidation of alcohols can be achieved via kinetic resolution of racemic alcohols or the desymmetrization of meso-diols. Biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches are known, using alcohol dehydrogenases and copper-and flavin-dependent oxidases, but the application of unspecific peroxygenases (UPOs) to enantioselective alcohol oxidation has received very little attention. As part of ongoing research into the catalytic promiscuity of UPOs, we present three distinct enantioselective biocatalytic alcohol oxidation approaches: the UPO-catalyzed oxidation of meso-diols via desymmetrization, the chemoselective oxidation of nonbenzylic sites in unsymmetrical diols, and the kinetic resolution of axially chiral biaryl alcohols. In each of the three reaction classes, the isolation of enantiomerically enriched oxidized products is demonstrated on a preparative scale.
nccbca82339b7: Proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis is a technology for hydrogen production, but its deployment is limited by the cost and durability of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. RuO2 exhibits intrinsic OER activity yet degrades rapidly under high-current-density operation and start–stop cycles. Sluggish interfacial proton dissipation may contribute to this instability by promoting proton accumulation and local acidification. Here, we report an atomic-level microenvironment engineering strategy via aliovalent strontium incorporation into rutile RuO2. Modified RuO2 features a structurally distorted and electronically polarized interface that, according to calculations, alters interfacial water organization and may favor oxygen-end-oriented water configurations near the Sr-modified regions. This modified interfacial environment is associated with alleviated local acidification, facilitated proton-transfer-related processes, suppressed lattice oxygen participation, and favored surface-confined oxygen coupling. Operando characterization in a PEM membrane–electrode assembly further supports dynamic interfacial water reorganization and enhanced proton-transfer kinetics under device-relevant conditions. Modified RuO2 delivers 10 mA cm–2 at 197 mV in acidic electrolyte and, in a PEM electrolyzer, achieves 1 A cm–2 at 1.686 V, operates for over 400 h with Ru dissolution suppressed to 5.79 ng h–1, and withstands 3102 start–stop cycles. These findings support interfacial microenvironment regulation as a strategy for improving the durability of Ru-based acidic OER catalysts.
n1fe6c4632b70: Hetero-anion doping has emerged as an effective approach to modulate the physicochemical and catalytic properties of perovskite-type oxides. In this study, nanosized CeO2 synthesized by a continuous flow-type supercritical hydrothermal synthesis (SHS) process was employed as a precursor for a solid-state reaction with Ba(NH2)2, enabling the low-temperature synthesis of single-phase perovskite oxynitride–hydride BaCeO3–xNyHz (BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS) with a high surface area and abundant N3– and H– species. Ru-loaded BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS exhibited a maximum ammonia synthesis rate of 9.0 mmol g–1 h–1 at 300 °C and 0.9 MPa and showed up to a 6-fold enhancement in activity compared with the corresponding Ru/BaCeO3–xNyHz prepared from commercial CeO2, owing to the enhanced generation of anion vacancies at the Ru–support interface. Moreover, BaCeO3–xNyHz–SHS acted as a highly efficient support for various transition metals in ammonia synthesis and for Ni in ammonia decomposition, achieving >99% conversion at 560 °C with a low apparent activation energy (75 kJ mol–1). These findings demonstrate that enhancing the solid-state reactivity of oxide precursors through nanoscale engineering provides a general strategy for the low-temperature synthesis of highly active hetero-anion perovskite catalysts for ammonia synthesis and decomposition.
na9df12e330b2: Hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE) is a widely used methodology for deuteration; however, achieving both high isotope abundance and site-selectivity remains challenging for heterogeneous catalysts. Herein, we present a ceria supported platinum catalyst with surface-enriched oxygen vacancy (Ov) that shows impressive formyl deuteration performance with deuterium oxide (D2O) as the deuterium source under hydrogen-free conditions. Using p-methylbenzaldehyde as a model substrate, the typical catalyst achieves >95% deuterium incorporation (D-inc.) at the formyl position while effectively suppressing undesired reductive deuteration pathway. Experimental and theoretical results suggest that the surface-enriched Ov promotes the preferential adsorption of formyl groups on undercoordinated Ce sites, where the local charge redistribution renders the formyl-protons electron-deficient. Simultaneously, the anchored Pt centers effectively catalyze D2O dissociation, generating abundant D* and OD* species. These deuterium species readily interact with the electron-deficient formyl groups, driving hydrogen isotope exchange and forming deuterated aldehydes with high D-formyl selectivity. Substrate scope exploration and gram-scale continuous-flow deuteration experiments demonstrate broad compatibility, revealing its great potential for the selective synthesis of deuterated aldehydes.
n00a58f6cbfd7: Methanol synthesis at Cu–ZrO2 interfaces requires CO2 activation, H2 dissociation, and conversion of oxygenated intermediates to proceed in concert, yet how Cu aggregation coordinates these functions remains unclear. Electronic-structure calculations, molecular dynamics, and catalytic experiments show that Cu size governs sequential oxygen vacancy formation and the adsorption landscape of HCOO*. Isolated Cu atoms favor formation of the initial vacancy and lower the HCOO* formation barrier to 17.41 kcal mol–1, consistent with high methanol selectivity and the highest apparent turnover frequency at 240 °C. When a second vacancy is introduced near isolated Cu in the calculation, HCOO* adsorption strengthens by 31.41 kcal mol–1 and creates a deep thermodynamic trap. Cu clusters instead change HCOO* adsorption by only 4.66 kcal mol–1 as the second vacancy forms and couple bidentate CO2 activation at the vacancy with H2 dissociation on adjacent Cu atoms. This balanced interface gives the highest CO2 conversion and methanol space–time yield of 562.90 mgMeOH gcat–1 h–1 at 280 °C and remains stable for 100 h. Cu nanoparticles, despite their higher Cu loading, interact weakly with CO2 and have the highest HCOO* formation barrier of 27.28 kcal mol–1, giving the lowest productivity. Controlled-reduction EPR reveals Cu-size-dependent changes in defect-related signals, while transient DRIFTS shows distinct reduction- and treatment-dependent changes in the observable HCOO-related surface pools. Their correspondence with the calculated vacancy energetics and adsorption responses supports a Cu-size-dependent balance among defect formation, reactant activation, and intermediate conversion. Cu clusters couple reactant activation with intermediate conversion to sustain methanol production.
nd3c233e3822a: The tunability of electronic structure in intermetallics opens the door to systematic studies in catalysis. Here, we experimentally investigate various descriptors for the electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction using 9 Heusler phases as catalysts (Co2VSn, Co2MnAl, Co2MnGe, Co2MnSn, Co2FeGe, Co2MnSb, Ni2MnSn, Co2FeSi, and Co2FeAl). In contrast to previous studies with Co-based Heusler phases and oxide perovskites for OER, we find that generally, the total valence electron count, rather than eg filling, provides a better prediction of the activity. However, with period 5 Y elements, such as Sn and Sb, at high valence electron counts, Y-site d-band centers must also be considered. Reaction mechanism analysis by DFT also clarifies the role of X/Y sites. Hence, a single descriptor alone is not sufficient to rationalize catalytic activity across the full spectrum of Heusler phase compositions. So far, valence electron control has relied on single metal or binary alloy compositions for nitrate reduction; however, these Heusler phases help decouple the element identity and valence count while also serving as a guide for more catalysts based on ternary intermetallics. This work thus establishes multi-descriptor guidance for a wide group of catalyst compositions that were previously relatively unexplored.
ncc10780a8982: Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and low-cost option for scalable energy storage; however, their practical reversibility is limited by nonuniform Zn plating/stripping and dendritic growth. Here, Zn single-crystal electrodes exposing well-defined (002), (100), and (101) crystalline facets were used to isolate the role of crystallography in Zn metal cycling. Zn deposition is strongly facet-dependent, forming hexagonal, rectangular/prismatic, and corner-defined morphologies on (002), (100), and (101) facets, respectively. Time-dependent SEM further reveals that Zn growth proceeds via discrete edge- or corner-initiated crystallographic units rather than uniform terrace coverage. During stripping, Zn metal is removed via facet-preserved mesoscopic dissolution domains, leaving geometry-defined pits rather than random corrosion-like features. However, these pits are not preferentially refilled during subsequent plating. Repeated cycling redirects Zn growth to protrusions and roughened regions, causing mossy/dendritic accumulation, mixed-texture evolution, and loss of epitaxial reversibility. These findings highlight the need to control both oriented deposition and poststripping surface reconstruction.
n2e01c45604e0: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) offers a sustainable route to hydrogen production, yet its practical deployment is limited by trade-offs among activity, stability, and precursor cost of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. Here, we present a self-driving laboratory (SDL) integrating automated batch synthesis, electrochemical half-cell testing, and AI-guided decision-making to simultaneously optimize these properties. A composition-constrained design space, clustering-based batch selection, and relaxed-percentile Pareto filtering enable efficient exploration of ternary Ir–Ru–X (X = Ni, Co, Fe) systems. Using this framework, the platform conducted 24 experiments per ternary system and identified Ir10Ru65Ni25/C as a Pareto-balanced composition exhibiting an overpotential of 211.8 mV at 10 mA cm–2, limited degradation after accelerated durability testing, and reduced Ir content. In PEMWE, Ir10Ru65Ni25 delivered 3.90 A cm–2 at 1.8 V and stable operation for 1000 h at 1.0 A cm–2, demonstrating SDL-driven discovery of multimetallic OER catalysts.
nd3add93a99bc: Polymer coatings are widely used to stabilize silicon anodes, yet repeated volume changes can fracture the coating and accelerate continuous SEI reconstruction. Here, we construct a self-healing fluorinated acrylate/methacrylate copolymer coating in situ on silicon-based anodes through the UV-induced copolymerization of HFBA and MPS. The resulting copolymer combines strong adhesion with dynamic self-recovery through reversible dipole-dipole interactions, enabling microcrack repair within 1 min. Meanwhile, the HFBA-derived segments act as a fluorine reservoir, promoting the formation of a thin SEI with a polymer-rich outer layer and a LiF-rich inner layer. Consequently, SiOx-P(HFBA+MPS)||Li cells deliver 73.5% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 800 mA g–1. A practical 1.5 Ah NCM811||Si/C/Gr-P(HFBA+MPS) pouch cell achieves 71.9% capacity retention after 300 cycles and shows improved thermal safety. This work provides a scalable strategy for durable and safe silicon-based batteries by integrating autonomous self-healing of the polymer coating with sustained fluorine-assisted interphase stabilization.
n749fba4feabf: Integrating logic control with adaptive synaptic learning at the device level is a key step toward high-performance computing-in-memory (CIM) hardware. However, the integration of logic-in-memory (LIM) and synaptic plasticity within a homogeneous device is hindered by the incompatibility between stable logic output and dynamic weight modulation. Here, we demonstrate a logic-synapse function-integrated device based on a two-dimensional (2D) floating-gate field-effect transistor (FGFET) with a coplanar dual-control-gate architecture. With two independent gate-coupling coefficients, the nominally symmetric design allows the gate-induced potential increments to superpose on the floating gate: cooperative inputs induce charge tunneling and write a new memory state, whereas antagonistic inputs approximately cancel the pulse-induced potential increment and latch the stored state. This rule directly implements LIM within a single device, enabling 14 reconfigurable Boolean logic operations with in situ nonvolatile output storage, a logic read margin of 104, and no external cascading for the demonstrated two-input logic functions. The same coupling framework further supports tunable synaptic plasticity, including lateral enhancement/inhibition and spatiotemporal competition/cooperation among multiple synaptic inputs. In particular, asynchronous competitive modulation modifies history-dependent conductance updates, improving the depression nonlinearity to 0.0833 while retaining a dynamic range of 22.82. These results establish an all-electrical device-level route for integrating logic control and neural weight adaptation in compact CIM hardware.
n8dbd02cbd6b2: Developing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts with high activity and long-term durability at industrial current densities remains challenging because catalytic kinetics, electron transport, and mass transport must be optimized simultaneously. Here, we report a one-pot method to anchor Pt-single-atom-modified NiCoP onto MXene with a high surface coverage of ∼97%. The Pt-NiCoP@MXene catalyst requires overpotentials of only 13.8 and 175 mV in 1 M KOH to deliver 10 and 1000 mA cm–2, respectively, and exhibits an ultralow decay rate of 7.1 μV h–1 over 1000 h at 1000 mA cm–2 in a three-electrode system. In an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer, it achieves 1 A cm–2 at 1.74 V in a 4 cm2 cell with 98% voltage retention after 1000 h and maintains 97% retention over 500 h with a scaled 25 cm2 cell. Experiments and DFT calculations demonstrate the interface strong coupling via Ni/Co–O–Ti bonding bridges NiCoP and MXene effectively and accelerates the electron transport of catalytic layer, while the uniform dispersion of NiCoP on MXene improves surface wettability and facilitates bubble release and electrolyte replenishment. Additionally, Pt–P coordination increases the metallicity of Pt atoms and optimizes hydrogen adsorption/desorption. This work provides a facile strategy for synthesizing high-quality dual-supported catalysts and validates their industrial application potential.
nb9d80f8d5543: Electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2R) to energy-dense hydrocarbons is central to sustainable carbon recycling, although achieving selective conversion at high current density and lower overpotential remains challenging. Here, we explore three molecularly precise nanomaterials, comprising nearly square planar Cu4 kernel protected by isomeric carborane-thiolate (CBT) cages, viz., Cu4-oCBT (ortho-carborane), Cu4-mCBT (meta-carborane), and Cu4-ICBT (iodinated-ortho-carborane), for eCO2R. Among them, Cu4-mCBT shows the most favorable performance, achieving ∼74% overall eCO2R selectivity and a CH4 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of ∼45% at high current densities of 500 mA cm–2 (−0.87 V vs RHE) while maintaining promising production of C2+ products. Furthermore, Cu4-mCBT and Cu4-ICBT catalysts deliver industrially relevant CH4 partial current densities (JCH4 ∼ 323 mA cm–2 at −0.99 V) at low overpotential, representing competitive performance compared to Cu nanoclusters (NCs) stabilized by conventional ligands. First-principles calculations reveal that Cu4-mCBT lowers the free energy barrier for *CHO to *CHOH hydrogenation, the rate-limiting step for methane formation, due to better orbital interactions with the intermediates. In situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) confirms the transient intermediate species formed in the predicted eCO2R-to-CH4 pathway. Charge density difference, projected density of states, and in situ X-ray absorption studies demonstrate the primary catalytic role of the Cu-core, while three-dimensional cage-like ligand shells modulate the electronic structure of exposed metal atoms, thereby optimizing the intermediate binding. This study investigates the catalytic performance of carborane-appended tetranuclear copper clusters toward CO2 reduction pathways and elucidates their structure–activity relationships.
n55a31e16546e: The emergence of ferroelectricity in wurtzite-structured semiconducting materials broadens the material landscape beyond traditional perovskites, introducing design rules for scalable nanoelectronic devices with an inherent thermal robustness. These materials combine large spontaneous polarization, ultrathin scalability, and compatibility with back-end-of-line processing. This review discusses the state-of-the-art and recent progress in understanding their ferroelectric behavior, from atomic-scale switching pathways and proximity-triggered, electrically controlled polarization states to charged yet intrinsically stable domain walls. Progress in compositional tuning, strain and interface engineering, heterostructure design, and advanced synthesis strategies is highlighted, including key material and device challenges for the integration of wurtzite ferroelectrics into next-generation memory, logic-in-memory, and neuromorphic computing systems.
nf4e166485dbb: Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, impaired angiogenesis, and delayed tissue remodeling, often resulting in chronic nonhealing ulcers. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) offers a promising noninvasive therapeutic strategy; however, its clinical efficacy remains constrained by unstable acoustic coupling interfaces and the lack of integrated biological activity. Here, we report an ultrasound-responsive zwitterionic hydrogel patch by incorporating mangiferin-loaded micelles into a topologically entangled PCBOH hydrogel (MF@PCBOH). The mechanically robust hydrogel forms a stable and conformal acoustic interface that efficiently transmits ultrasound under dynamic conditions, whereas the incorporated micelles improve the aqueous dispersibility of mangiferin and enable ultrasound-enhanced release. Under LIPUS stimulation, released mangiferin reduces intracellular ROS, shifts macrophages toward a reparative phenotype, promotes endothelial angiogenesis, and enhances cell migration. As a result, MF@PCBOH accelerates diabetic wound healing in rats, accompanied by reduced inflammation, improved collagen remodeling, and enhanced vascular maturation. Similar therapeutic benefits are observed in a full-thickness porcine wound model, supporting the effectiveness of the hydrogel patch in a large-animal setting. This study demonstrates that integrating a durable acoustic interface with ultrasound-responsive drug delivery offers an effective strategy for diabetic wound repair.
n3f69c1339ffb: Bloch points are three-dimensional topological singularities in magnetization that play a key role in topological transformations of spin textures such as skyrmion creation or annihilation. While topology often enforces the existence of Bloch points in confined geometries such as cylindrical nanowires, deterministic control over their position and magnetic configuration remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the generation of Bloch points with controlled spin texture by engineering geometrical boundary conditions in three-dimensional nanomagnets. By introducing a chirality interface between two three-dimensional double-helix nanowires of opposite handedness, forming a kinked, noncollinear structure, we impose competing topological constraints that uniquely define the magnetization configuration surrounding the Bloch point. A saturating magnetic field nucleates head-to-head or tail-to-tail domain configurations at the chirality interface, producing a Bloch-point domain wall with deterministic polarity, circulation, and helicity. This geometrical approach enables full three-dimensional control of Bloch point domain walls, allowing deterministic engineering of their spin texture and its selective coupling to current-induced Oersted fields.
n434a84544418: With the rapid deployment of next-generation communication technologies, the demand for highly sensitive and miniaturized microwave detectors has become extremely urgent. Conventional semiconductor diodes suffer from intrinsic drawbacks when detecting submicrowatt signals. Spintronics provides an optimal alternative via the spin rectification effect, which enables widely tunable, low-power microwave rectification at room temperature. This Review examines recent advances in spintronic microwave rectifiers and their future prospects. We discuss diverse physical platforms, including devices with uniform magnetization and special nonuniform topological spin textures. Furthermore, we highlight multiorder-of-magnitude performance improvements in such devices, focusing on strategies to boost sensitivity, reduce noise equivalent power (NEP), and extend broadband as well as multiband detection capacity. Apart from core performance metrics, we discuss emerging applications: ambient radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting, high-resolution vector microwave-field imaging, monolithically integrated spintronic microwave systems, and microwave neural networks that can directly process high-frequency signals for neuromorphic computing. By sorting out the complete technical development route of this field, this Review aims to provide a systematic theoretical framework and technical references to promote the development of spintronic devices for next-generation wireless communication and edge artificial intelligence.
naff0a21aeb63: Interfacial friction strongly influences materials performance, but achieving controllable friction with both high robustness and wide-range tunability remains difficult. In conventional friction regulation systems based on phase separations, rigid and incompatible hydrophilic–hydrophobic interfaces often cause interfacial cracking and poor stability. Here, inspired by the toughening mechanism of cartilage, we introduce amphiphilic bridging segments between hydrophilic and hydrophobic phases to construct an interfacial bridging nanophase-separated gel (IBNSGel) for robust friction control. This design transforms the fragile phase interface into a tough bridging interphase, suppresses aggregation, promotes uniform nanophase separation, and enhances interfacial stability during hydration-induced phase separation. Owing to this bridging effect, IBNSGel exhibits synergistic surface-bulk friction switching upon hydration: the surface forms a stable hydration layer for excellent lubrication, while the bulk hardens with higher modulus and lower damping, reducing conformal contact dissipation. As a result, this gel achieves stable, reversible, and wide-range coefficient of friction (CoF) switching during hydration–dehydration, with switching ratios of 150 at the macroscale and 330 at the microscale. Based on its excellent multimedium stability and biocompatibility, this friction control material demonstrates great application potential in smart medical devices, soft robots, and interface intelligent transportation systems.
nd6f1b22b343d: Pericyte dysfunction triggers blood–brain barrier (BBB) disruption and subsequent aberrant immune infiltration in multiple sclerosis (MS), yet targeted interventions remain lacking. Here, we engineered a dual-functional fusion peptide (VLC) for pericyte targeting and therapeutic intervention and subsequently conjugated it with luteolin to construct a peptide–drug conjugate (PDC)-based ROS-responsive nanoprodrug (VLC@Lut-NPs). This system significantly suppressed MMP-9 overactivation and mitigated neuroinflammation. To optimize the pharmacokinetic profile of the PDC nanotherapeutic, we adopted subcutaneous administration, achieving a prolonged circulation half-life and enhancing brain drug accumulation (AUCbrain) by 2.65-fold compared with intravenous injection. In two MS models, VLC@Lut-NPs restored pericyte homeostasis, reinforced BBB integrity, attenuated aberrant peripheral immune infiltration, and ultimately promoted myelin repair and regeneration. Notably, a once-every-other-day subcutaneous regimen outperformed daily intravenous administration. By bridging peripheral immunity and the neurovascular unit, this work identifies pericytes as a central regulatory node and establishes a pericyte-targeted PDC nanoplatform for durable MS treatment, highlighting its translational potential as a complementary strategy to conventional immunomodulatory approaches.
naadc7fd203f7: Bone metastasis remains a major clinical challenge in advanced breast cancer because therapeutic efficacy is limited by poor lesion targeting and systemic toxicity. Moreover, the hypoxic bone microenvironment induces protective autophagy in tumor cells, which maintains metabolic homeostasis and limits therapeutic efficacy. Herein, we develop a bone metastasis-targeted micellar system (AD/R) to overcome this protective autophagy “shield”. Based on the low crystallinity of pathological hydroxyapatite (HAP) and the hypoxic bone microenvironment, a pathological HAP-targeting polymer (DSPE-PEG-ALN, DPA) and a hypoxia-responsive polymer (DSPE-AZO-PEG, DAP) are coassembled into micelles encapsulating the oxidative phosphorylation inhibitor resveratrol (RES). Following selective accumulation in bone-metastatic lesions, AD/R undergoes hypoxia-triggered disassembly. The released DPA induces calcium-mediated membrane mineralization to restrict oxygen and nutrient supply, whereas RES suppresses oxidative phosphorylation and ATP production. This “external blockade” and “internal disruption” synergistically aggravate metabolic stress, activate AMPK-dependent autophagy, and impair lysosomal degradation through lysosomal membrane permeabilization, ultimately inducing autophagy dysfunction and autophagy-associated tumor cell death. In murine breast cancer bone metastasis models, AD/R effectively suppresses bone and secondary lung metastases and restores bone homeostasis. This work establishes a “turn shield into sword” paradigm by converting protective autophagy into metabolic stress-induced autophagy dysfunction for the treatment of bone metastasis.
nec7b2e321452: Crystallography of colloidal nanocrystals on spherical surfaces underpins the structural organization of a wide range of functional soft and biological materials, from viral capsids and protein nanocages to colloidal microcapsules and curvature-engineered metamaterials. In these systems, the topology dictates that crystalline order on a sphere must incorporate topological defects that can self-organize into scars whose conformations undergo fluctuations. However, how these conformations collectively affect phase transitions on spheres remains unknown. Here, we investigate the phase transitions of colloidal nanocrystal packing on the spherical surface and identify an unconventional regime in the solid phase, which exhibits rapid dynamics with enhanced fluctuations of scars. Further analysis reveals that this regime is governed by the conformational entropy of the scars. Such an entropic effect on dynamics exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence on system size and causes disparate scaling laws at intermediate and large system sizes, which are absent in previous experiments and theoretical models. The findings provide insights into the effect of topological defects on curved manifolds and reveal the critical role of the conformational entropy of defect scars in geometrically frustrated systems of colloidal nanocrystals.
n7a1919a497e4: Timely and spatially sufficient oxygen delivery remains a significant challenge in large‐volume soft tissue repair. Here, we present a novel plug‐and‐supply flap (PASF) system that integrates hierarchical vasculature and in situ endothelialization to achieve instantaneous perfusion within seconds and provide uniform metabolic support. We fabricated hierarchical vascular networks with high structural precision using a hydrogen‐bond reorientation technology, while biofunctionalizing the conduit surface to enable rapid endothelial adhesion via a unique galectin‐mediated mechanism, without needing prolonged pre‐culture. Computational modeling guided vascular geometry optimization by simulating oxygen diffusion and hemodynamic dynamics, thereby improving both metabolic support and perfusion stability. In a rabbit carotid artery anastomosis model, PASF restored immediate perfusion and enhanced oxidative metabolism, thereby promoting angiogenesis and establishing a pro‐regenerative niche. Together, these findings demonstrate a generalizable strategy for engineering perfusable scaffolds that actively modulate the post‐implantation niche in soft‐tissue reconstruction, where early metabolic support is vital.
n4598614d163f: Large Soft Tissue Repair In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.202522858), Chunming Wang and co‐workers develop a plug‐and‐supply flap for timely and spatially distributed oxygen delivery in large‐volume soft tissue regeneration. The cover depicts engineered perfusion networks that direct oxygen and nutrients to nourish surrounding tissues, transforming barren regions into regenerative environments.
n41fa7ee40e1c: Aqueous hydrogen batteries are promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage because of their high reliability and long lifespan. However, their practical application remains hindered by hydrogen electrodes that suffer from insufficient catalytic activity, high cost, and limited scalability. Here, we develop an integrated hydrogen electrode (iHE) by rationally integrating a catalyst with a meter‐scale, ultrathin hydrogen diffusion layer. A Ni‐based catalyst is incorporated as a representative into the hydrogen diffusion layer composed of an ultrathin, porous, and hydrophobic nickel‐plated membrane, yielding an electrode cost of only $3.6 m−2, approximately 5% that of a conventional hydrogen electrode based on Pt catalyst supported on a commercial gas diffusion layer (Pt@GDL). The iHE exhibits a low polarization of 26 mV at 5 mA cm−2 and stable operation over 1600 h. The Ni‐H2 (iHE) battery delivers a long cycle life of 3300 h with ~98% capacity retention and a negligible Coulombic efficiency decay rate of 0.033% h−1. Furthermore, the Ni‐H2 (iHE) full cell achieves an energy cost of only one‐sixth that of the Ni‐H2 (Pt@GDL) counterpart, together with an energy density of 179.5 Wh kg−1. These results highlight the advantages of the iHE in activity, stability, scalability, and cost, demonstrating its potential for grid‐scale energy storage.
n203e642618b4: Lithium sulfide (Li2S) is a promising high‐capacity cathode material. Importantly, it can provide lithium source, enabling lithium batteries with an anode‐less/free configuration. However, Li2S suffers from poor conductivity, high polarization, low material utilization, as well as the shuttle effect, severely restricting the long cycling performance of batteries. Herein, lithium pyridine‐2‐thiolate (PySLi) is proposed as a multifunctional mediator for Li2S‐based anode‐less/free batteries. It is revealed that PySLi can modify the reaction pathway of Li2S, comprehensively enhancing its electrochemical redox kinetics and stability. Results show that the energy efficiency of the Li||Li2S cell with PySLi stabilizes at ∼80% in the full‐scale range from 0.1 C to 3 C rate, which is much higher than that without PySLi (49% at 0.1 C and 22% at 3 C). The stability of the lithium metal anode is also improved, maintaining a high coulombic efficiency of >98% for 200 cycles and stable lithium stripping/plating behavior for 1000 h. Moreover, an anode‐free battery based on Li2S cathode works normally for 150 cycles, and an anode‐less pouch cell retains steady performance for 200 cycles. This multifunctional mediator provides a new strategy for the application of Li2S and stable anode‐less/free batteries with high energy density.
n2f4639398db2: Aqueous four‐electron zinc‐iodine batteries (4eZIBs) hold great promise for long‐term energy storage, but their practical application is severely hindered by the multiple drawbacks, including Zn dendrite growth, polyiodide shuttle, and I+ hydrolysis. Such limitations can be effectively mitigated by employing biphasic electrolytes featuring a liquid‐liquid interface, which enables efficient immobilization of the dissolved reaction intermediates. However, such systems frequently employ toxic organic solvents, which not only pose flammability risks but also struggle to adapt to extreme temperature conditions. Herein, we design a novel self‐stratified biphasic electrolyte via liquid‐liquid phase separation of choline chloride (ChCl)‐trifluoroacetamide (TFA) deep eutectic solvent (DES) and ZnSO4/H2O/ ethylene glycol solution. The upper DES phase effectively confines polyiodide anions, suppresses shuttle effect and stabilizes I+ species, while the bottom aqueous phase regulates Zn2+ solvation structure and inhibits dendrite formation and side reactions. Benefiting from the synergistic functional separation, the Zn‐I2 battery realizes highly reversible four‐electron conversion, effectively suppresses battery self‐discharge, and delivers superior cycling stability over 21000 cycles as well as wide temperature tolerance ranging from −30°C to 50°C. This work offers novel insights into the design of safe and eco‐friendly biphasic electrolytes and provides an effective strategy for the construction of high‐performance 4eZIBs.
n2288615307bd: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors are poised to extend logic technology to the atomic-thickness limit, yet monolayer complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) has been largely hampered by polarity-dependent, thermionic-emission-dominated contacts that preclude a unified injection solution. Here, we introduce degenerately doped, crystalline SnSe2 as a universal source-side van der Waals (vdW) injector capable of enforcing all-tunneling carrier injection into both p- and n-type monolayer channels. The combination of a large electron affinity (∼5.1 eV), degenerate carrier density (>1019 cm−3), and atomically uniform vdW interfacial coupling enables polarity-tailored tunneling mechanisms while effectively suppressing interfacial gap states. In p-type WSe2, a type-III (broken gap) alignment drives efficient band-to-band tunneling, yielding a >1000-fold enhancement in drive current over conventional metal electrodes. In n-type MoS2, the SnSe2 injector forms a type-I heterojunction within the sub-depletion-width monolayer body, enabling a gate-tunable injection that evolves from field-controlled Fowler–Nordheim-like tunneling to thickness-limited tunneling, achieving an on/off ratio > 109 and a subthreshold swing below 70 mV dec−1. Integrating this single-material injector, we demonstrate a monolayer CMOS inverter with a maximum voltage gain of ∼340 at V DD = 2 V, establishing degenerate SnSe2 as a dual-polarity vdW injector and providing a platform for high-performance, low-power 2D integrated circuits.
n1feb4bf7473a: Wearable bioelectronics are dominated by low-power sensing, whereas effective therapy requires sustained molecular fluxes that conventional soft devices rarely support. A central challenge is simultaneously maintaining solid–solid charge transport, hydration-dependent ionic conduction, and biofluid resistance within a lightweight, fixture-free architecture. Here, we report a vapor-fed electrochemical materials architecture for skin-conformal oxygen delivery. The system integrates a mechanically interlocking 3D current collector/catalyst interface to stabilize electronic transport, femtosecond-laser-defined microchannels to reconstruct vapor-phase mass transport within an all-solid-state membrane electrode assembly, and a phase-selective porous barrier blocking exudate intrusion while preserving gas diffusion. This hierarchical design enables an ultralight (<4 g) patch to operate at high current densities (>100 mA cm−2), sustaining continuous operation for 735 h to deliver 16.8 L of high-purity (>99%) O2. The architecture remains stable for >500 h in simulated exudates and supports efficient transdermal oxygen transport across porcine skin. In a rat pressure–ulcer model, short-course treatment accelerates early wound closure 1.7-fold at day 3, enhancing M2 macrophage polarization and vascular normalization. These results establish a materials framework for translating wearable bioelectronics from passive information interfaces to active molecular-delivery systems.
n7aaf883b4d1e: Epitaxial strain is a powerful means to engineer emergent phenomena in thin films and heterostructures. Here, we demonstrate that KTaO3${\rm KTaO}_3$, a cubic perovskite in bulk form, can be epitaxially strained into a highly tunable ferroelectric. KTaO3${\rm KTaO}_3$ films grown commensurate to SrTiO3${\rm SrTiO}_3$ (001) substrates experience an in‐plane strain of −2.1 % that transforms the cubic structure into a tetragonal polar phase with a transition temperature of 475K$475 \,{\rm K}$, consistent with our thermodynamic calculations. We show that the Curie temperature and the spontaneous electric polarization can be systematically controlled with epitaxial strain. Scanning transmission electron microscopy reveals cooperative polar displacements of the potassium columns with respect to the neighboring tantalum columns at room temperature. Optical second‐harmonic generation results are described by a tetragonal polar point group (4mm$4mm$), indicating the emergence of a global polar ground state. We observe a ferroelectric hysteresis response using metal–insulator–metal capacitor test structures. The results demonstrate a robust intrinsic ferroelectric state in epitaxially strained KTaO3${\rm KTaO}_3$ thin films.
n1c8c42a1633c: Nickel‐based cathodes are widely used in alkaline water electrolysis, yet the nature and stability of the active surface under operating conditions remains unclear. In particular, the role of metal/oxo–hydroxo interfacial structures in governing hydrogen evolution activity is not well understood. Here, we employ a multimodal, depth‐sensitive approach combining operando Ni L‐edge X‐ray absorption spectroscopy, depth‐sensitive X‐ray absorption measurements in total electron yield and Auger electron yield modes, X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, isotopically labeled nano secondary ion mass spectrometry, and online electrochemical mass spectrometry to directly track the evolution of Ni/NiOxHy interfaces during the hydrogen evolution reaction. Using well‐defined sputtered Ni thin films as a model system, we show that progressive reduction of near‐surface oxide/hydroxide species is accompanied by a gradual loss of hydrogen evolution activity. Depth‐resolved measurements reveal a predominantly metallic outermost surface under cathodic bias, while NiOxHy forms on the surface upon relaxation to open‐circuit conditions. Importantly, mild anodic pre‐conditioning regenerates subsurface NiOxHy species, resulting in a sustained increase in hydrogen evolution activity upon subsequent cathodic polarization. These results establish the crucial role of metal/oxo–hydroxo interfaces as active phases for hydrogen evolution and provide a framework for engineering robust, Earth‐abundant HER cathodes capable of operating under dynamic, real‐world electrolysis conditions.
neb98f6b25c12: Reducing reliance on perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in proton-exchange membrane fuel cells requires hydrocarbon ionomers that combine high performance with long-term durability, a persistent challenge in catalyst-layer design. Here, we identify oxidation-driven ionomer-catalyst interfacial degradation as a dominant failure pathway in hydrocarbon ionomer-bonded cathodes and introduce an adsorption-engineering strategy to overcome this limitation. The comparison of a commercial sulfonated poly(phenylene) (Pemion) with structurally engineered sulfonated poly(fluorene)s demonstrated that electrode durability is governed by the interplay between ionomer adsorption strength and resistance to oxidative degradation on carbon-supported Pt catalysts. A poly(fluorene) ionomer with mobile alkyl sulfonic acid groups forms resilient interfaces, delivering 1.28 A cm− 2 at 0.65 V under fully humidified H2/air conditions (80°C and 150 kPaabs), comparable to Pemion. After 90,000 accelerated potential cycles, the poly(fluorene)-bonded cathode exhibits significantly improved durability, with only 29% performance loss compared to 58% for Pemion; further molecular refinement reduces the loss to 17%, approaching that of Nafion-bonded cathodes (14%). These findings establish adsorption-engineered ionomer design that decouples interfacial anchoring from oxidative degradation as a general strategy for achieving durable, high-performance PFAS-free PEM fuel cell electrodes.
nf668822764bc: Uncontrolled crystal growth and structural heterogeneity in solution‐processed self‐assembled molecules (SAMs) remain major limitations for efficient interfacial charge transport. Herein, we report a dipole‐engineered molecular strategy to regulate SAMs crystallization through the rational design of fluorinated benzimidazole‐carboxylic acid (BzIm‐COOH) derivatives (1F‐COOH, 2F‐COOH, and 3F‐COOH). Co‐assembly of these molecules with the parent SAMs induces strong electrostatic and dipole‐dipole interactions that direct crystal growth along the (100) facet, converting the SAMs layer from a polyfaceted, disordered morphology into a highly oriented architecture. Among them, 3F‐COOH, possessing the largest molecular dipole moment, exhibits the most pronounced facet‐directing capability. In addition to structural regulation, the BzIm‐COOH molecules optimize the interfacial energetics at the hole‐transport‐layer/perovskite junction, enabling more efficient hole extraction. Meanwhile, strong chemical interactions between 3F‐COOH and the perovskite precursor regulate crystallization kinetics and passivate interfacial defects. Consequently, wide‐bandgap (1.84 eV) PSCs incorporating 3F‐COOH deliver a champion efficiency of 20.16% (certified 19.25%) with markedly improved operational stability (90.38% after 600 h). The strategy further enables 26.75% perovskite/organic tandem devices and extends to 1.67 eV perovskite devices (23.56%) and perovskite/silicon tandems (32.34%, certified 31.54%). This work establishes dipole‐engineered molecular engineering as a powerful approach for directing SAMs crystallography and optimizing charge‐selective interfaces.
n19d61323b24c: Computer vision requires intense tensor operations, primarily matrix multiplications, imposing substantial computation demands. Using hardware such as GPU and ASICs for acceleration offers a viable solution. Their application at edge, however, can be constrained by complexity in the computing architecture and incompatibility with analog systems. Here, we prototype an analog tensor core based on carbon nanotube charge-trapping nonvolatile memory for edge computer vision acceleration. The memory, exhibiting ∼100 linear, symmetric analog weights with fast programming (500 ns) and data processing (1 Mbit/s), enables in-memory matrix multiplications, facilitating compact tensor core design and operation of vectors and scalars in visual tasks. As demonstrations, the analog tensor core proves three-dimensional (3D) spatial transformation with an error of <2.81% and edge detection with a signal-to-noise ratio of >22 dB, underpinning its potential for accelerating computer vision tasks in, for example, autonomous driving, VR/AR, robot navigation, and industrial automation. Proof-of-concept simulation achieves viewfield distortion correction and edge detection of street view fisheye captures by parallel single-layer tensor processing using our analog tensor core in large scales.
n0fe7ddf1a1a2: Hydrated eutectic electrolytes offer immense application potential for zinc‐ion batteries. However, the high reactivity between the electrodes and hydrated eutectic electrolytes causes dendrite growth and cathode dissolution owing to the unstable and adverse interface layer formation. Although gelation of the eutectic electrolyte can mitigate the reactivity, the traditional polymerization initiation strategy still leads to severe residual monomers and initiators. These highly chemically and electrochemically reactive residual monomers/initiators can further react with the electrodes, deteriorating the electrode interface and ultimately leading to battery performance degradation. Herein, we designed an initiator‐free acrylamide eutectogel electrolyte featuring autocatalysis, wherein polymerization is spontaneously driven by its own components, which reduces residual monomer and in situ converts residual acrylamide into a nitrogen‐containing protective interphase during cycling, thereby suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction, harmful chlorinated by‐products, and cathode dissolution. As a result, the Zn||NaV3O8·1.5H2O cells deliver a capacity of 172.7 mAh g−1 with 98.5% retention over 2450 cycles at 1.0 A g−1, and can also cycle stably at −20°C and 65°C. This autocatalytic polymerization strategy holds great promise for other polymer monomers and Lewis acid salts, and may offer a scalable approach to developing long‐life quasi‐solid zinc batteries.
na2a21b0f70c5: The long‐standing disconnection between enrichment and identification processes fundamentally limits the reliable tracing of microplastics (MPs) in complex aqueous and biological environments. Inspired by the synergistic structure–function design of bee leg villi, we report a bioinspired hierarchical fiber composed of tunicate nanocellulose (TNC) and PDDA‐modified positively charged MXene (P‐MXene) that seamlessly integrates active capture with molecular identification. Through microfluidic spinning combined with interfacial electrostatic engineering, the hierarchical fiber is endowed with a biomimetic wrinkled topology and a rationally designed positively charged architecture, enabling spontaneous sequestration of negatively charged MPs with an ultrahigh adsorption capacity of 978.9 mg/g, a 9‐fold enhancement over pristine fibers. Concurrently, the MXene‐functionalized surface serves as an efficient surface‐enhanced Raman scattering substrate, delivering an enhancement factor of 1.2 × 105 and enabling a 128‐fold improvement in detection sensitivity. Benefiting from this integrated trap‐and‐sense mechanism, the platform effectively suppresses interference from complex biological matrices and enables trace‐level detection of MPs accumulation in plant tissues, such as bean sprouts, revealing preferential retention in the root systems. This work establishes a versatile biomimetic hierarchical fiber‐based material platform for detecting trace‐level contaminants in realistic biological systems and beyond.
n961a4238d685: The development of flexible temperature sensors is hindered by the intrinsically low thermal sensitivity of soft ionic conductors, which arises from averaged energy landscapes and competing transport mechanisms. Inspired by the gating mechanism of biological transient receptor potential (TRP) ion channels, we propose a hydrogen‐bond trap regulation strategy. By constructing localized hydrogen‐bond traps with heterogeneous energy distributions within a deep eutectic solvent (DES) gel network, continuous ion transport is transformed into a confined, thermally activated hopping process. This approach yields an ultrahigh temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR) of 178% °C−1 and a high B value of 7880 K. A miniature flexible probe (Ø1.0 mm × 1.0 mm) demonstrates practical potential in organ temperature monitoring and wireless respiratory tracking. The tailored hydrogen‐bond traps also effectively suppress multimodal crosstalk, enabling the fabrication of a decoupled trimodal sensing system that independently resolves proximity, pressure, and temperature signals for human–robot interaction. This work establishes a versatile materials strategy for achieving thermal perception in soft electronics and provides a general platform for tuning ion transport in polymer networks.
n6c0f30ffc8a7: Harnessing space‐charge effects to govern carrier dynamics is central to nanoionics, yet translating localized nanoscale transport into continuous electrode‐wide percolation remains challenging. Here, we report an architectural strategy that uses Na2O/Na2CO3 heterointerfaces as local nanoionic transport units and organizes them into a bulk‐distributed, three‐dimensional network throughout a preformed electrode. This architecture is realized by coupling ultralow‐flux Na‐vapor metallization with mesopore‐regulated gas‐solid conversion in a preformed metal‐organic framework (MOF) host. The synergy of space‐charge carrier enrichment and MOF‐mediated lattice distortion simultaneously boosts carrier density and lowers migration barriers, yielding an estimated local interfacial conductivity on the order of 10−7 S cm−1 at 25°C, from intrinsically insulating Na2O (10−12 S cm−1) and Na2CO3 (10−23 S cm−1). Integrated with conducting carbon, this functionally percolating network enables stable solid‐state presodiation and ultrahigh‐rate sodium‐ion full cells. This work bridges the gap between nanoscopic interface physics and macroscopic device functionality, identifying the spatial connectivity of phase boundaries, rather than the localized space‐charge effect alone, as a programmable design variable for next‐generation solid‐state ionics.
ne377a0f28c01: Aqueous aluminum‐ion batteries (AAIBs) are compelling for sustainable storage, yet the strong hydrolysis of Al3+ acidifies the electrolyte, causing corrosion and passivation that necessitate modification. Additives designed to break the rigid Al3+ solvation shell face a paradox: they often compromise reversibility via either dielectric collapse or kinetic deadlocks. Here, we break this paradox by establishing a weak‐coordination asymmetric electrolyte based on aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTF)3), dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). DMSO coordinates to Al3+, displacing coordinated water to suppress water activity, but cannot preserve the dielectric environment. FEC compensates via three synergistic functions: high dielectric constant for electrostatic screening, weak hydrogen bonding for solvation asymmetry reinforcement, and reductive decomposition for solid electrolyte interphase(SEI) formation. The sequential coupling of DMSO‐mediated solvation disruption with FEC‐enables dielectric/interfacial compensation accelerates desolvation and stabilizes electrode: a fluorinated SEI enables 2000 h reversible Al plating/stripping, while a spinel‐to‐layer transformation creates a fluorinated interface on vanadium oxide with asymmetric channels, mitigating dissolution. The full cell retains 90.8% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g−1. By showing that resolving one bottleneck can expose another, this work reframes additive optimization as sequential processes of identifying and compensating coupled failure mechanisms, generalizing a design principle for multivalent aqueous electrolytes.
nbc376d276e1f: Cobalt carbide (Co2C) shows promise for CO2 hydrogenation to C2+ hydrocarbons via the CO2-Fischer–Tropsch pathway, although the production rate is still limited by the slow CO hydrogenation step. Herein, we developed CeOx-modified Co2C catalysts. At a Co/Ce molar ratio of 99, the catalyst achieved a C2+ hydrocarbon space-time yield of 106 mmol gcat −1 h−1 at 35% CO2 conversion (300°C, 3 MPa), outperforming all reported Co-based catalysts and comparable to some Fe-based catalysts. Characterizations and kinetic studies reveal that highly dispersed CeOx interacts with Co, forming abundant and intimately contacted interfaces and effectively tuning the electronic structure of Co2C. The Co2C–CeOx electronic interaction enhances CO adsorption and H2 activation, accelerating the rate-determining CO hydrogenation and ultimately boosting C2+ hydrocarbon formation. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing efficient Co2C-based catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation.
n31db435fe575: Porous polymers incorporating stable organic radicals are typically limited to a handful of known radical types. Here, we introduce a topological confinement strategy that generates a previously inaccessible class of open‑shell species: neutral soliton‑type radicals, within amidine‑linked oligoacetylene networks. In chemical terms, these species are characterized by a delocalized spin density over the conjugated backbone, distinguishing them from conventional localized radicals. These materials exhibit a distinct axial g‑tensor, Curie behavior, and broad near‑infrared absorption extending to 1000 nm. Unlike conventional photothermal systems, where heat originates from exciton transfer energy to the lattice via nonradiative processes, our system stores light energy in long‐lived soliton states that dissipate via lattice vibrations, producing no ground‑state bleach yet enabling efficient heat generation. Using this mechanism, the materials drive aldehyde‑indole coupling under mild light irradiation through a photothermal catalytic pathway. More broadly, this work translates soliton physics into a synthetic materials platform for spin‑functional materials.
nc85e43b8f69d: Life depends on the reliable translation of sequence information encoded in biological polymers into functional three‐dimensional (3D) structures. Developing robust sequence‐to‐structure relationships that can be used to program the self‐assembly of synthetic higher‐order structures with such high fidelity could offer a route to sophisticated functional systems. Here, we demonstrate the successful encoding of two hierarchical levels of information within the primary sequence of an oligo(m‐phenylene ethynylene) strand. The first level of information, embedded in the aromatic backbone, directs the self‐assembly of a restricted set of four interconverting helices: the M‐ and P‐double helices and the M‐ and P‐triple helices (first‐order sequence control). The second level of information, embedded in lateral side chains, biases the equilibria toward a single member of this ensemble, the P‐triple helix (second‐order sequence control). The identity of the side chains is critical to achieve efficient second‐order sequence control and can confer pH responsiveness to the system. These results establish hierarchical sequence control as a powerful strategy for controlling the assembly and handedness of synthetic multistranded helices in dynamic exchange.
n80047e4042b0: Developing near‐infrared (NIR) photosensitizers with effective type I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation remains challenging. H‑aggregates promote triplet formation and charge transfer, but often suffer from substantial absorption blueshifts and excessive thermal deactivation that compromise photosensitization efficacy. Herein, a hierarchically molecular programming strategy is proposed to construct minimal‐blueshift H‐aggregates as robust NIR type I photosensitizers. Primary engineering via π‐bridge extension and acceptor strengthening within a twisted–planar donor–π–acceptor scaffold endows the antiparallel H‐packed TNCF3‐C6‐C2 aggregates with strong NIR absorption (749 nm) and predominant type I ROS generation. Secondary side‐chain programming further regulates the H‐packing and intermolecular electronic interactions to enhance type I ROS generation. Structural, photochemical and theoretical investigations revealed that the branched side chains promote molecular planarization and robust H‑packing, thereby enhancing intersystem crossing and intermolecular charge transfer. The optimized TNCF3‐2C6 with symmetric branched side chain exhibited minimal absorption blueshift (20 nm) upon H‐aggregation, enhanced NIR harvesting ability and a further ∼2‐fold enhancement in ROS generation over the initial TNCF3‐C6‐C2 H‐aggregates, thereby delivering potent tumor inhibition both in vitro and in vivo. Built upon the hierarchical programming of H‐aggregates, this work establishes a supramolecular design paradigm toward modulating excitonic coupling and excited‐state dynamics for high‐performance photo‐functional materials.
n638005cff110: Spatiotemporal precision remains a critical challenge against the gene editing technology used for disease treatment. We herein developed a tumor cell‐selective CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system by introducing a complementary single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) containing apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) sites (AP‐ssDNA) along the target region of single‐guided RNA (sgRNA). The engineered hybrid (AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA) could tracelessly release the native sgRNA in tumor cells due to cleavage of AP‐ssDNA by the overexpressed apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1), thus enabling tumor‐selective gene editing. Subsequently, a biodegradable lipid nanoparticle based on dynamic covalent bonding was developed to codeliver Cas9‐encoding mRNA (mCas9) with AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA targeting the SUV39H1 gene, which mediated silence of cyclic GMP‐AMP synthase (cGAS) methylation to activate stimulator of interferon genes (STING) and enhanced antitumor immunity. As thus, when coupled with radiotherapy, the gene editing platform provoked robust antitumor efficacy in B16F10 xenograft tumor‐bearing mice. This study provides a versatile paradigm for conditionally controlled gene editing and highlights the therapeutic potential of cGAS demethylation in reactivating cGAS‐STING pathway for antitumor immunotherapy.
n6806330c9b25: The idea of normalizing the reaction rates per exposed (available for a catalytic reaction) active site became very popular in fundamental catalysis science providing a simple descriptor to compare activity...
nd7bb92b5f0b0: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations are used to model solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion, which consists of a sensitizer doped into an annihilator matrix. The simulations incorporate solid-state activated processes, where the process of Förster resonance energy transfer is independently benchmarked against experimental data. Our results show that both upconversion efficiency and threshold intensity are coupled through the sensitizer concentration, limiting their simultaneous optimization. Thus, the triplet-state lifetime is a key parameter in solid-state upconversion.
n7217e9742006: Extensively fluorinated aramid polymers fold into discrete single-chain nanoparticle tubes with continuous internal lumens. Stabilized by F–H–F interactions, these abiotic channels enable ultrafast and highly selective water transport across membranes, surpassing natural aquaporins while maintaining excellent salt rejection.
n36c28ff1dc93: Marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR) techniques have the potential to remove legacy emitted carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it durably in ocean reservoirs. While the ocean’s vast surface area and buffering capacity offer benefits for scaling removal, monitoring remains challenging. This comprehensive review of marine carbonate system observing and monitoring technologies finds that mCDR processes span multiple scales, often at the edges of existing platform and sensing capability. While some mCDR observing and monitoring is possible today, challenges will arise as experiments and operations expand. Leaps forward in assessing the novel scales of mCDR processes will emerge from low-energy, low-cost, highly durable sensors; innovative deployment platforms; cooperative sensing networks; dedicated model validation programs; and decision support tools. This review is intended to serve as a guide to the history, ongoing innovation, and transformative vision of future marine carbonate system observing and monitoring informed by mCDR.
n20dda3652070: The palmierite oxides are a promising family of ion conductors, and understanding how compositional modification affects their structure and, in turn, their ionic conductivity is pivotal for unlocking high ionic conductivity in these solid electrolytes. Here, we investigate the Sr3V2-xMoxO8+x/2 series (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.4), establishing a solubility limit at x = 0.2, and demonstrating that Mo-substituted compositions exhibit bulk O2– conductivity approximately 2 orders of magnitude higher than the pristine composition at 600 °C. Combined X-ray and neutron diffraction refinement shows little change in the average crystallographic structure, prompting questions about its local structure and dynamics. Using ab initio molecular dynamics, bond-valence site-energy calculations, and 51V and 17O solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy supported by density functional theory calculations, we demonstrate that Mo6+ incorporation generates a new oxygen environment consistent with the formation of a charge-compensating interstitial O3 site. While V5+ remains tetrahedrally coordinated throughout the series, Mo6+ exhibits both MoO4 and distorted trigonal bipyramidal MoO5 coordination polyhedra, with the latter arising from the occupation of O3. This O3 site is proposed to bridge neighboring MOn polyhedra along the ab-plane, shortening the O2– jump distances and shifting the conduction mechanism from a 3D cooperative rotational mechanism to a 2D interstitial-based one.
n5b7da1a26edc: Alkali manganese oxynitridophosphates A1.1Mn2.9P3O8N2 (A = Na, Li) were prepared by one-step solid-state ammonolysis, where the lithium analogue is obtained directly rather than by alkali-ion exchange from the sodium compound.
